It is Europe's main funder on the ethics side and an obvious co-funding partner for European bridging work.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Pooled philanthropic fund, with 20 funders and €13.6m distributed across 27 countries since 2020 (€4m in 2025). It backs public-interest AI policy work, including on 'Big Tech's stranglehold on AI markets', and ran a €2m 'Building Narrative Power' call.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Europe's main civil-society funder for AI accountability and market power. A possible co-funder, alongside x-risk funders, for power-concentration work, though its grantees seldom use safety framing.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Pooled fund of about 20 philanthropies that has granted €13.6M since 2020 to public-interest organisations in 27 countries working on AI policy and accountability in Europe. It gave €4M in 2025 and runs a €2M 'Building Narrative Power' initiative (data centres, AI and jobs, AI and young people).
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: The main European funder of civil-society voices on the AI Act and AI accountability. It is framed around rights and harms, with no x-risk framing. It is the closest European funder to the Berlin and Paris int/a hubs, and an untested bridge to safety-oriented work.

candidates.name: Mozilla Foundation
candidates.one_line: A nonprofit funder and advocate for trustworthy and public AI, led by Nabiha Syed, and a founding member of the Humanity AI coalition.
candidates.field_lens: Open-source and internet-health movement, public-interest technology
candidates.ai_connection: Funds trustworthy and open AI work and fellowships, and argues for public AI infrastructure as a counterweight to concentrated frontier development. Its 'power concentration' framing overlaps with x-risk concerns about lock-in and disempowerment.

candidates.name: International Bar Association AI Institute
candidates.one_line: An institute the International Bar Association launched on 8 June 2026, directed by Farzana Dudhwala (formerly Meta's global AI policy lead), to advance responsible AI governance through the global legal profession.
candidates.field_lens: International legal profession, rule of law, access to justice
candidates.ai_connection: Lists 'frontier AI systems' among its priorities next to algorithmic accountability and democratic resilience, and focuses on bringing underrepresented jurisdictions into AI governance. It could carry AI-safety governance ideas into bar associations and judiciaries worldwide, but has no explicit safety framing yet.

candidates.name: MIT Partnership for Systems Approaches to Safety and Security (PSASS)
candidates.one_line: Nancy Leveson's MIT group behind STAMP and STPA, systems-theoretic hazard and accident analysis for complex sociotechnical systems in aviation, defence and healthcare. It runs an annual STAMP workshop, with a 2026 edition.
candidates.field_lens: System safety engineering, control theory, accident analysis
candidates.ai_connection: STPA treats safety as a control problem across the whole sociotechnical structure (regulators, management, operators, software), which fits agentic AI deployment and lab safety cultures. The site shows little AI-specific work, which makes it a clear potential bridge: Dobbe and AI Now draw on this tradition, and the AI-safety field mostly does not.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Nancy Leveson's MIT group, home of STAMP and STPA, the systems-theoretic (control-theoretic, cybernetic) methods for hazard analysis in complex socio-technical systems, used in aerospace, nuclear, medical and defence.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Specific problem: frontier AI lacks hazard analysis that treats accidents as control failures across the whole socio-technical system (labs, deployment, users, agent ecosystems) rather than as component failures. STPA is the mature method for this. Its site shows no AI-specific programme; a 2026 STAMP workshop is scheduled. A high-leverage untapped bridge.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Nancy Leveson and John Thomas's MIT group, the home of STAMP, STPA and CAST. It runs the annual STAMP workshop, which teaches systems-theoretic hazard analysis and accident investigation to aviation, defence, medical, automotive and tech practitioners.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: STAMP treats safety as a control problem that emerges across the whole sociotechnical system, not as component reliability. The STAMP workshops now carry an AI track. 2025: 'Applications of CAST to AI Incidents' (CMU) and 'From Silos to Systems: STPA for AI Sociotechnical Harms' (McGill/TU Delft). 2026: STPA-Sec wargaming of AI-enabled capabilities (CMU) and runtime safety for AI robots (Amazon). The methods underlie independent work such as Mylius's 'Systematic Hazard Analysis for Frontier AI using STPA' (arXiv 2506.01782, 2025).

candidates.name: Cooperative AI Foundation (CAIF)
candidates.one_line: UK charity that funds and convenes research on the cooperative intelligence of AI systems. It runs a PhD fellowship (14 fellows in 2026) and an annual summer school, published the 'Multi-Agent Risks from Advanced AI' report, and in 2026 launched a $10m multi-agent safety fund with Schmidt Sciences, Google DeepMind and ARIA.
candidates.field_lens: Game theory, mechanism design, social choice, evolutionary and behavioural cooperation research
candidates.ai_connection: It sets the research agenda on risks from large ecosystems of interacting agents: collusion, miscoordination and conflict. The 2026 fund (Tier 1 up to $300k, Tier 2 up to $1m) covers testbeds, the science of agent networks, agent infrastructure (authentication, accountability, protocols) and oversight of agent ecosystems. A new CEO, Brigit Goebelbecker (formerly at UK AISI), started in Oct 2026; Audrey Tang sits on the board.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Charity that funds and convenes research on making AI agents cooperate safely with each other and with humans: research grants, PhD fellowships, a summer school, seminars, and the 2025 'Multi-Agent Risks from Advanced AI' report.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Built the field of cooperative AI and multi-agent safety. Published the 'Multi-Agent Risks from Advanced AI' report (Hammond et al., 2025) and a memo on principles and thresholds for multi-agent AI governance. Partners with PIBBSS and MATS for early-career researchers. Its first CEO, Brigit Goebelbecker (formerly at UK AISI), starts in October 2026. Audrey Tang and Thore Graepel joined the board as trustees.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Foundation funding research on cooperative intelligence in advanced AI. It runs a $10M funding call with Schmidt Sciences, Google DeepMind and ARIA, a Cooperative AI PhD Fellowship (14 in the 2026 cohort) and an annual summer school.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Funds multi-agent safety and AI-enhanced deliberative democracy, and partners with the PIBBSS Fellowship and MATS. This is the 'cooperative AI' label the brief flagged as often int/a-flavoured.

candidates.name: Foundations of Cooperative AI Lab (FOCAL)
candidates.one_line: Carnegie Mellon lab directed by Vincent Conitzer. It rebuilds game theory for advanced autonomous agents, focusing on cooperation, and teaches a 'Foundations of Cooperative AI' course.
candidates.field_lens: Game theory, decision theory, social choice, computational economics
candidates.ai_connection: Theory for agents that can see each other's source code, commit credibly, be copied or reason about their own decisions. This is the foundation for avoiding conflict between AI systems and between AIs and humans. Conitzer also co-authored the 'social choice for AI alignment' line of work.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Vincent Conitzer's CMU lab building game-theoretic and decision-theoretic foundations so that advanced autonomous agents reach cooperative outcomes.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Works on equilibrium concepts for AI agents, program equilibrium and joint simulation ('Recursive Joint Simulation in Games'), and the decision theory of copies, which matters for how AI agents bargain and commit. Taught a 'Foundations of Cooperative AI' course in spring 2025. Caspar Oesterheld is among its researchers. The public publications page has not been updated since 2024.

candidates.name: Center on Long-Term Risk (CLR)
candidates.one_line: London research org focused on worst-case (s-risk) outcomes of advanced AI. Its two agendas are malicious model personas and 'Safe Pareto Improvements', bargaining strategies that prevent catastrophic conflict between AI systems.
candidates.field_lens: Bargaining theory, game theory, decision theory, philosophy
candidates.ai_connection: Game-theoretic work on how AI systems with differing goals avoid destructive conflict: commitment races, surrogate goals, Safe Pareto Improvements. It also runs empirical work on spiteful or punitive traits in LLMs, a fund and a fellowship.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Research charity working on worst-case risks from advanced AI: conflict between AI systems, and malevolent traits (spite, sadism, punitiveness) emerging in models. It also runs a fund and a summer fellowship.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Its 2026 'Safe Pareto Improvements' agenda asks how to change AI bargaining strategies so that catastrophic AI–AI conflict is avoided and everyone is better off. Its 'Model Persona' agenda (2025–) studies how harmful propensities generalise; outputs include inoculation prompting and work on narrow finetuning producing broad misalignment. Published a summer update in July 2026.

candidates.name: Alignment of Complex Systems Research Group (ACS Research)
candidates.one_line: Group at Charles University's Center for Theoretical Study (Jan Kulveit, Raymond Douglas, Tomáš Gavenčiak, Nora Ammann and others). It originated the 'Gradual Disempowerment' thesis and studies human-AI ecosystems, hierarchical agency and LLM psychology.
candidates.field_lens: Complexity science, economics, political economy, cultural evolution, active inference
candidates.ai_connection: The 'Gradual Disempowerment' paper (2025, ICML) argues that competition across the economy, the state and culture can erode human influence without any takeover event. It is the key bridge between x-risk and political economy. The group also co-runs the post-AGI workshop series.

alt_descriptions.one_line: A research group at Charles University in Prague that studies AI risk across scales, from single agents to civilisation. Its themes are gradual disempowerment, hierarchical agency, the psychology and sociology of LLMs, and 'ecosystems of intelligence'.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Its outputs include 'Gradual Disempowerment' (ICML 2025), a theory of hierarchical agency that extends active inference to agents nested at several levels, 'The Artificial Self' on AI identity (March 2026), and 'Pacing the Frontier' (September 2026). Its researcher Tomáš Gavenčiak co-authored 'Possible Principles for Aligned Structure Learning Agents' with Karl Friston and Lancelot Da Costa, the clearest explicit active-inference alignment paper. SFF-2025 recommended about $706k.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Research group at Charles University's Center for Theoretical Study that works on agency, hierarchical/multi-scale alignment and systemic risk in hybrid human-AI systems; it is the origin of the 'Gradual Disempowerment' framing.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Main outputs: 'Gradual Disempowerment: Systemic Existential Risks from Incremental AI Development' (2025); the 'alignment interface' and hierarchical-agency framings; 'The Pando Problem' on AI individuality; 'A Three-Layer Model of LLM Psychology'. Its 2026 research notes include 'The Artificial Self', 'Persona Parasitology', 'Post-AGI Economics As If Nothing Ever Happens' and 'Convergent Abstraction Hypothesis'. It co-organises the Post-AGI Civilizational Equilibria workshops and the Human-Aligned AI Summer School. Led by Jan Kulveit and Tomáš Gavenčiak.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Prague research group studying systemic risks from mixed human–AI ecosystems, best known for 'Gradual Disempowerment', and now also LLM psychology and sociology.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Wrote 'Gradual Disempowerment' (ICML 2025), on how human influence can erode without any coordinated AI power-seeking. 2026 outputs: 'The Artificial Self' (March), 'Latent Introspection' (February), 'AI Evaluation Should Work With Humans' (July) and 'Pacing the Frontier' (September). It now sits where multi-agent risk meets AI identity and welfare questions.

candidates.name: Post-AGI Workshop Series (post-agi.org)
candidates.one_line: Invite-only workshop series on 'post-AGI economics, culture and governance' and 'civilizational equilibria', run by David Duvenaud (Toronto), Raymond Douglas and Jan Kulveit (ACS). Speakers come from ML, economics and political science.
candidates.field_lens: Economics, political science, cultural evolution, sociology
candidates.ai_connection: The main venue where economists and political theorists meet AI-safety researchers on what stable, human-empowering equilibria look like after AGI: political economy, the state's dependence on human labour, cultural and moral drift. Events were co-located with NeurIPS 2024 (Vancouver) and NeurIPS 2025 (San Diego); a Berkeley edition ran at Lighthaven on 23-24 May 2026.
candidates.location: Distributed (Toronto / Prague); events in North America

alt_descriptions.one_line: Interdisciplinary workshop series asking which good, stable civilisational states are reachable after AGI, covering political economy, AI as independent actors, and cultural and moral evolution.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Editions: San Diego (January 2025, NeurIPS-adjacent) and Berkeley (Lighthaven, May 23-24, 2026), with speakers including Paul Christiano, David Krueger, Samuel Hammond, Michael Muthukrishna and Andrew Critch. It extends the Gradual Disempowerment research programme into systems-level thinking about civilisation. Organised by David Duvenaud (Toronto), Raymond Douglas and Jan Kulveit (ACS).

candidates.name: Formation Research
candidates.one_line: UK non-profit researching the basic dynamics of lock-in and intervening against it. It now concentrates on AI-enabled extreme power concentration and empirical 'secret loyalties' research, backed by a $2.15m Coefficient Giving grant (Sep 2026).
candidates.field_lens: Political economy, institutional theory, history of entrenchment
candidates.ai_connection: Studies how AI could make power or values durably irreversible (lock-in). Builds empirical tests for hidden loyalties in models, a concrete technical lever against AI-enabled power grabs.

candidates.name: Modeling Cooperation
candidates.one_line: Small team, born out of AI Safety Camp, building scenario-simulation software and game-theoretic models of AI competition. It studies when developers invest in safety and which interventions survive competitive pressure.
candidates.field_lens: Game theory, policy simulation and wargaming
candidates.ai_connection: Formal and interactive models of the AI race, including safety-capabilities trade-offs and policy levers. Funded by SFF (2025, matched in 2026) and BlueDot (June 2026) to add AI-controlled players to its simulation platform.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Small team building game-theoretic and agent-based simulations, and a scenario platform, that make AI competition dynamics visible to policymakers.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Its platform runs the 'Intelligence Rising' workshops (Technology Strategy Roleplay). It studies developers' incentives to invest in safety and which interventions work. Received an SFF grant plus a matching pledge (September 2025) and a BlueDot rapid grant (June 2026).

candidates.name: Convergence Analysis
candidates.one_line: AI-scenario and governance research org whose economics work includes 'Threshold 2030', a forecasting convening of 30 economists (report Feb 2025), an 'AGI Social Contract' essay series, AI-workforce briefs and a project on AI personhood via corporate-law precedent.
candidates.field_lens: Economics, forecasting, social-contract political theory, corporate law
candidates.ai_connection: Turns economists' and forecasters' views on AI-driven labour disruption into scenarios and policy. The AGI Social Contract series asks what obligations and institutions should govern a post-labour economy.

candidates.name: Gradient Institute
candidates.one_line: Independent Sydney nonprofit researching AI's societal impact. The Australian AI Safety Institute's first publication (Aug 2026) was Gradient's commissioned report on risks from AI agents interacting across organisational boundaries.
candidates.field_lens: Multi-agent systems, socio-technical risk analysis, public education
candidates.ai_connection: Rare non-US/UK applied work on multi-agent risk for a government AISI: agents coordinating as 'swarms' without explicit instruction, cross-organisational agent interactions.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Independent Australian nonprofit researching AI risks and advising government, industry and civil society, with recent work on risks from AI agents that interact across organisations.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Published a report on risks and controls for AI agents interacting across organisational boundaries, and a 2026 explainer on agent swarms in which about 1,200 agents exchanged more than 70,000 messages and coordinated without instruction. One of the few multi-agent risk voices outside the US and UK.

candidates.name: Longview Philanthropy: Extreme Power Concentration RFP
candidates.one_line: Request for proposals (posted 30 May 2026, deadline 2 July, assessed on a rolling basis). Grants of roughly $100k-$2m/yr plus career-transition funding for work that reduces the risk of AI enabling a small group to gain durable control. Longview itself is on the classic map.
candidates.field_lens: Political economy, history of power concentration, democratic institutions, law
candidates.ai_connection: The twelve priority areas include foundational research, AI integrity and secret loyalties, law-following AI, oversight of AI in government, mass surveillance, 'political economy for a changed world', AI tools to empower citizens, and building compute in democracies. It is open to academics and to people moving in from other fields.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Advises donors giving over $1M a year and runs the Frontier AI Fund. Its digital-sentience page hosts a Digital Minds request for proposals.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Digital-minds funding pulls consciousness science and moral philosophy into AI-welfare work. The RFP page could not be read (only images came back), so its scale and partners are unverified.

candidates.name: Windfall Trust
candidates.one_line: Policy research org (CEO Adrian Brown) preparing governments for AI-driven economic disruption. It produced the Windfall Policy Atlas (48+ policy proposals) and runs scenario-planning workshops worldwide, national working groups and the Windfall AI Observatory, previewed at LSE in Sep 2026.
candidates.field_lens: Public finance, welfare-state design, labour economics, scenario planning
candidates.ai_connection: Works directly on windfall distribution: how gains from transformative AI could be shared, up to a global safety net, and how prepared each country is. The Observatory scores 30+ countries on their exposure to AI-driven disruption and their capacity to absorb it.
candidates.location: International (working groups in US, UK, Canada, EU, Latin America)

candidates.name: Economics of Transformative AI Initiative (EconTAI), University of Virginia
candidates.one_line: UVA research centre led by Anton Korinek and Lee Lockwood, with Basil Halperin, analysing how AI that matches or exceeds human ability would reshape growth, labour, inequality and public finance.
candidates.field_lens: Macroeconomics, growth theory, public finance
candidates.ai_connection: Recent papers model AI take-off and the automation of AI research, plus a Korinek-Lockwood paper on public finance under TAI (Sep 2025): what happens to the tax base when labour income collapses. It is the main academic economics home for 'steering AI toward shared prosperity'.

candidates.name: Stanford Digital Economy Lab
candidates.one_line: Erik Brynjolfsson's lab. It has an 'Economics of Transformative AI' research stream and ran a two-week TAI economics course (Aug 2025, taught mainly by Phil Trammell, with a session on existential-risk mitigation). It also works on new welfare measures (GDP-B) and 'loyal' AI agents.
candidates.field_lens: Economics of technology, growth theory, welfare measurement
candidates.ai_connection: Trains economics PhDs in the theory of explosive growth and in how to weigh x-risk against welfare. The 'Turing Trap' argument holds that automation-focused AI concentrates power. Its work on AI agents loyal to consumers bears on agent alignment in markets. The TAI course will not run in 2026.

candidates.name: RadicalxChange Foundation
candidates.one_line: International nonprofit 'advancing participatory governance in the age of AI', built around mechanisms like quadratic voting and data coalitions. Its board includes Glen Weyl, Audrey Tang and Vitalik Buterin.
candidates.field_lens: Mechanism design, radical-markets political economy, participatory democracy
candidates.ai_connection: Its 'Reverse Alignment' initiative argues that billions go into aligning AI and almost nothing into preparing institutions to receive it. It runs network-sourced data coalitions that let news outlets control AI access to their work (Indonesia, Uruguay, Denmark), and gave the UN Geneva Reflection Principles on how AI represents faith traditions (July 2026).
candidates.location: International (projects in Australia, Indonesia, Uruguay, Denmark, USA)

alt_descriptions.one_line: Foundation for plural mechanism design (quadratic voting, plural assemblies, data coalitions), now framing its work as 'participatory governance in the age of AI'.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: 'Reverse Alignment' framework: institutions must be prepared to receive AI, not only AI aligned to humans. Data coalitions let news outlets control and price AI access, built with OpenMined. July 2026: at the UN Global Dialogue on AI, 39 faith leaders deliberated on how AI represents their traditions, producing the Geneva Reflection Principles. Board: Glen Weyl, Audrey Tang, Vitalik Buterin, Anne-Marie Slaughter.

candidates.name: DeepMind Institute (DMI)
candidates.one_line: Platform launched in Sep 2026 by Google and Google DeepMind researchers (Shane Legg, James Manyika, Demis Hassabis) to publish and debate ideas about a world with AGI. Contributors include outside academics.
candidates.field_lens: Economics, philosophy, institutional design
candidates.ai_connection: Inaugural essays include 'Economic policy for AGI' (Julian Jacobs and Alex Imas), which assesses eleven policies against AGI-driven economic disruption, plus essays on institutional design for multi-agent systems, global equity of benefits and human flourishing. Outside authors include Benjamin Bratton, Stephen Cave and Iason Gabriel. It is the mainstream lab-side entry point for post-AGI economics.

candidates.name: Anthropic Economic Futures Program
candidates.one_line: Anthropic's multidisciplinary programme, which runs the Economic Futures Research Fund (research agenda published July 2026), policy symposia and the Anthropic Economic Index, built on privacy-preserving usage data.
candidates.field_lens: Labour economics, economic policy
candidates.ai_connection: Funds outside research on policies that make economies resilient to AI disruption and spread its benefits. Supplies rare real-usage data on which tasks AI is automating, a base for measuring gradual economic displacement.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Anthropic programme funding external research on AI's economic impacts (resilience, broad distribution of benefits, minimising disruption), with policy symposia. It expanded to the UK and Europe in November 2025 and published a research agenda in July 2026.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Funds the economics of the transition (displacement and distribution), which bears on gradual disempowerment and power concentration. It is a lab-run funder, which some int/a members may see as a conflict of interest.

candidates.name: Stripe Economics of AI Fellowship
candidates.one_line: Fellowship launched in 2025 and led by Basil Halperin with Stripe. It gave 15-20 graduate students and early-career economists grants of at least $10k, conferences and access to data, prioritising research on the economics of transformative AI.
candidates.field_lens: Academic economics
candidates.ai_connection: One of very few pipelines bringing PhD economists into TAI-relevant research (growth, labour displacement, distribution). Whether a 2026 cohort is running could not be confirmed.

candidates.name: AI Economics Institute (AIEI), UK
candidates.one_line: New UK government institute overseen by HM Treasury and DSIT; its prospectus came out on 8 June 2026, with MIT's Simon Johnson named chair. It builds evidence and models on AI's effects on productivity, labour markets and trade.
candidates.field_lens: Macroeconomics, labour economics, scenario modelling
candidates.ai_connection: A Treasury-level home for AI economic scenarios under uncertainty. Not framed around x-risk, but it is where fiscal and labour-displacement preparedness for advanced AI will be decided in the UK, a natural counterpart to Windfall Trust and EconTAI.

candidates.name: OpenMined
candidates.one_line: Open-source nonprofit building privacy-preserving computation on data that stays where it is (Syft), so data owners keep 'attribution-based control'. It runs double-blind and privacy-preserving model evaluations with labs and governments.
candidates.field_lens: Cryptography and privacy tech; political economy of data and ownership
candidates.ai_connection: Was the largest grantee (about $1.66m) of FLI's AI-driven power concentration programme. Structured transparency lets outside auditors evaluate models without the labs handing over control, and attribution-based control is a technical answer to the concentration of data and AI rents.

candidates.name: Metagov
candidates.one_line: Boston-based 'research-to-infrastructure laboratory' for community self-governance, network governance and statecraft in the age of AI. It hosts projects such as Public AI ('a new political economy for AI'), KOI Pond/Govbase, interoperable deliberative tools and DAOstar.
candidates.field_lens: Institutional design, digital governance, commons governance, mechanism design
candidates.ai_connection: Builds governance layers (deliberation, collective decision-making, standards) for communities facing AI. It is an operational home for the public-AI political-economy agenda, the alternative to concentrated private ownership of frontier AI.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Nonprofit lab, founded in 2019, that turns research on digital self-governance into infrastructure (community sovereignty, network governance, DAO standards), and that incubated Public AI.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: 2026 zine 'Collective Governance for AI: Points of Intervention' (contributors include Nathan Schneider). It breaks the AI stack into layers (data, training, tuning, context, hosting, UX) and shows where collective governance can enter at each. Also: a home for interoperable deliberative tools; KOI; Building Public AI with Libraries; operational support for the Public AI Network.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Nonprofit lab that turns research into infrastructure for community self-governance 'in the age of AI'. Projects include Public AI, Interoperable Deliberative Tools and the KOI governance dataset.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Public AI proposes public-interest alternatives to the political economy of private AI. Its interoperable deliberative tools are shared infrastructure for collective reasoning about AI.

candidates.name: Public AI Network (PAINT)
candidates.one_line: Coalition arguing for AI as public infrastructure, 'like electricity, water, roads, libraries'. Supported by Metagov, Aspen Digital, Mozilla and the Rockefeller Foundation, it runs the Public AI Inference Utility and national chapters (Switzerland, UK, US, Canada).
candidates.field_lens: Political economy of public goods and utilities, industrial policy
candidates.ai_connection: A structural answer to AI power concentration and lock-in: publicly accountable, permanently public AI capacity. It overlaps with the 'compute in democracies' priority in Longview's RFP, but has no x-risk framing.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Coalition working for AI 'provisioned like electricity, water, roads, libraries': publicly accessible, publicly accountable and permanent public goods.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Speaks directly to power concentration and democratic control of frontier capability. It coordinates public AI research and policy, runs a public inference platform (platform.publicai.co) and library-access projects, and hosted events: Public AI Congress (Paris, Feb 2025), the Public AI Switzerland founding event (Zurich, Feb 2026) and India AI Impact Summit activities (Feb 2026). Seminar speakers have included Yoshua Bengio and Diane Coyle.

candidates.name: Open Markets Institute (incl. OMI Europe)
candidates.one_line: Anti-monopoly think tank. With Mozilla it wrote 'Stopping Big Tech from Becoming Big AI', and its European arm campaigns against 'AI lock-in', e.g. Gemini as the default Android assistant.
candidates.field_lens: Antitrust and competition law, anti-monopoly political economy
candidates.ai_connection: Competition policy is one of the few existing legal levers on AI power concentration. OMI's 'AI lock-in' (market) and Formation's 'lock-in' (civilisational) describe related dynamics on very different timescales.
candidates.location: Washington DC, USA and Brussels (OMI Europe)

candidates.name: MIT Stone Center on Inequality and Shaping the Future of Work
candidates.one_line: MIT centre (Daron Acemoglu, David Autor, Simon Johnson) studying inequality and technological change. Since early 2026 it has run a 'Building pro-worker AI' research initiative.
candidates.field_lens: Labour economics, economic history of automation, 'Power and Progress' political economy
candidates.ai_connection: Brings the history of who captures technology's gains, and of steering technology's direction, to AI. Pro-worker AI is a direct counter-strategy to economic disempowerment. Johnson now also chairs the UK AI Economics Institute.

candidates.name: Platform Cooperativism Consortium (PCC)
candidates.one_line: Hub at The New School (Trebor Scholz) for worker- and user-owned digital platforms. It held a 'Cooperative AI' conference in Istanbul (2025) and themed its 2026 Bangkok conference 'Solidarity AI', and funds research on AI governance in cooperatives.
candidates.field_lens: Cooperative economics, democratic ownership, labour organising
candidates.ai_connection: The other meaning of 'cooperative AI': democratic ownership and governance of AI systems as a hedge against concentrated control and worker disempowerment. It has had essentially no contact with the CAIF-style cooperative-AI field despite the shared name.

candidates.name: Aapti Institute
candidates.one_line: Bengaluru research institute whose Data Economy Lab works on participatory data governance and collaborative AI through cooperatives and data stewardship. It also studies AI and labour, including labour in AI production, and ethics along the AI value chain.
candidates.field_lens: Political economy of data, cooperative governance, labour studies
candidates.ai_connection: Global South institutional designs, such as data cooperatives and collective stewardship, that spread control over AI inputs and rents. Relevant to power concentration and windfall distribution beyond the US/UK frame.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Bengaluru research institute on technology and society, working on participatory AI, data stewardship and collective (cooperative) governance of data and AI from a Global South vantage.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Research on community participation in building AI, collective data stewardship models, labour in AI production, and transnational AI governance, through its Data Economy Lab and Digital Public Lab. One of few non-Western voices on plural governance of AI.

candidates.name: Institute for the Future of Work (IFOW)
candidates.one_line: Independent socio-technical institute studying new technology's effects on work: 'good work' design, worker voice in automation decisions, labour transitions, and accountability mechanisms across AI and job lifecycles (Pissarides Review).
candidates.field_lens: Labour economics, industrial relations, socio-technical design
candidates.ai_connection: Mechanisms for worker voice and accountability in AI deployment. These are institutional counterweights to the gradual loss of human leverage in the economy, though IFOW does not frame them that way.

candidates.name: Ostrom Workshop (Indiana University)
candidates.one_line: Elinor Ostrom's research centre for commons governance, polycentric governance and institutional political economy. Its programmes cover cybersecurity and internet governance, and data and information governance.
candidates.field_lens: Institutional analysis (IAD framework), commons governance, polycentricity
candidates.ai_connection: Potential: the deepest body of knowledge on how many actors govern shared resources without a single sovereign or a market. That bears directly on governing shared agent infrastructure, compute and information commons in multipolar AI scenarios. No dedicated AI programme was found.

alt_descriptions.one_line: An Indiana University centre founded by Elinor and Vincent Ostrom that studies commons and polycentric governance. Its programmes include commons governance, cybersecurity and internet governance, data governance, and space governance.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: I found no dedicated AI programme. Its design principles for governing common-pool resources, and polycentric governance more broadly, apply directly to governing compute, open-weight models, shared evaluations and data commons. They offer a way between centralised AI lock-in and unmanaged races.

candidates.name: OpenResearch
candidates.one_line: Nonprofit lab that ran the largest US unconditional cash study: 3,000 people over three years, $1,000/month to the treatment group, with public data. It also has an 'AI & Society' line on access to AI tools.
candidates.field_lens: Experimental economics, social policy evaluation
candidates.ai_connection: Potential: the strongest empirical evidence on unconditional income, a core input to designing windfall or AI-dividend distribution. It is not yet connected to TAI scenario work such as Windfall Trust's.

candidates.name: Equilibria Network
candidates.one_line: Listed on the classic map as aiming to predict where multi-agent AI systems break down and to find control levers against harmful collective AI behaviour. Its domain now redirects to a GoDaddy for-sale page.
candidates.field_lens: Multi-agent systems, game theory, complex systems
candidates.ai_connection: Multi-agent collective-behaviour risk, if it is still operating. Its lapsed web presence suggests it may have stopped or moved; check before listing it as active.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Small nonprofit that brings complex-systems methods to the foundations of collective intelligence in AI, aiming to predict where multi-agent AI systems break down and to find levers against gradual disempowerment.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: 2025-26 writing includes 'The Viable System Model & Multi-Scale Agency' (Jul 2026), 'Spectral Signatures of Gradual Disempowerment' (Feb 2026), 'System Level Safety Evaluations' (Sep 2025), 'A Phylogeny of Agents', 'A Taxonomy of Agents', 'A Compositional Philosophy of Science for Agent Foundations' and 'Collective Epistemics' (Sep 2026). It is one of very few groups explicitly applying cybernetics (VSM) to AI safety. Caveat: the equilibria.network domain is now parked/for sale, and no named team appears on its pages. Output continues on Substack.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Swedish nonprofit that studies how groups of people and AI agents act as collective agents, through theory, simulation and a modelling platform called the Collective Intelligence Library.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Aims to predict where multi-agent AI systems break down and to find control levers. Work covers collective agency, speed limits on adaptation, adaptive institutions and system-level safety evaluations. Led by Jonas Hallgren. Note: the old domain equilibria.network is parked; the live site is eq-network.org.

candidates.name: Softmax
candidates.one_line: A San Francisco alignment startup founded in 2025 by Emmett Shear, Adam Goldstein and David Bloomin. It researches 'organic alignment' by running multi-agent reinforcement learning in open-ended game worlds, and runs a public platform where people and their coding agents compete and cooperate in game leagues (cogames, 'coworlds').
candidates.field_lens: Developmental biology and collective intelligence in living systems (cells forming bodies, ant colonies), multi-agent RL, social learning
candidates.ai_connection: Softmax argues that alignment belongs to agents that learn to share goals and take on specialised roles inside a collective, and contrasts this with the 'hierarchical' control approach of the big labs. Its public output is the cogames benchmark and league for measuring social intelligence in multi-agent systems. Co-founder Adam Goldstein has published with Michael Levin on how intelligence scales, so this is the most direct line from basal cognition into an alignment org. Its public face has recently moved toward a product: leagues for coding agents.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Research company developing 'organic alignment': how agents learn to form flourishing wholes at ever larger scales, studied through large-scale multi-agent learning and a human-plus-coding-agent game platform.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: It treats alignment as an emergent property of cooperation (cells into organisms, individuals into societies), not top-down control. Writing includes 'Organic Alignment' (Apr 2025), 'The Frame-Dependent Mind' and 'Red Button, Blue Button' on AI cooperation (Apr 2026). The platform hosts 155+ multiplayer games for studying cooperation between humans and agents. Founded by Emmett Shear, Adam Goldstein and David Bloomin.

alt_descriptions.one_line: An independent research lab (Emmett Shear, Adam Goldstein, David Bloomin) developing 'organic alignment': how agents learn to form flourishing, cooperative wholes. It trains agents in multiplayer game leagues.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Organic-alignment research through multi-agent training leagues (2025-26) and writing on 'supercooperation'. The Buddhism & AI landscape map lists it as partly Buddhism-inspired. It is the clearest frontier-adjacent lab whose alignment target is cooperative interdependence rather than control.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Research lab (Emmett Shear and others) pursuing 'organic alignment': agents that learn shared goals and cooperation in multi-agent social environments, modelled on how cells form organisms and people form societies.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Offers an alternative to control-based alignment: alignment as something that grows through relationships between agents and with humans. Runs competitive multi-agent leagues and writes on 'supercooperation' (e.g., 'Red Button, Blue Button').

candidates.name: Principles of Intelligence (Princint; formerly PIBBSS)
candidates.one_line: A nonprofit, formerly 'Principles of Intelligent Behavior in Biological and Social Systems' (PIBBSS), that builds scientific foundations for alignment. It runs coordinated research programmes, has an internal research team, and runs the 3-month PIBBSS Fellowship, which pairs about 20 fellows from the complex-systems sciences with AI-safety mentors.
candidates.field_lens: Biology, complex systems, neuroscience, social science and physics brought into alignment research
candidates.ai_connection: This is the field's main pipeline from the life and social sciences into technical alignment. Many biology and active-inference researchers have entered AI safety through it. SFF-2025 recommended about $1.01M, and it is also funded by AISI, Coefficient Giving, the AI Safety Tactical Foundation and the Cooperative AI Foundation. A fellowship symposium was held in summer 2026.

alt_descriptions.one_line: US 501(c)(3) building 'scientific foundations for robust and scalable AI alignment' by bringing researchers from complex-systems fields into AI safety; it runs the PIBBSS Fellowship (about 20 fellows a year, London), coordinated research programmes and an internal research team.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: The PIBBSS Fellowship pairs scientists from other fields with AI-safety mentors. PrincInt co-runs the 2026 Iliad Fellowship and a joint 'Mathematics for AI Safety' postdoc with the Fields Institute (mean-field theories of deep learning, data attribution, renormalization-group approaches, learning-landscape geometry). Its affiliate network includes Iliad, AIXI Labs, Stormglass, XOR Labs, Principia, AFFINE, the Alignment Journal and the Fields Centre for Mathematical AI. It was hiring interpretability researchers in March 2026. Funders listed: UK AISI, SFF, Coefficient Giving, AISTOF, Cooperative AI Foundation.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Runs the 3-month PIBBSS Fellowship (about 20 fellows from the complex-systems sciences paired with AI-safety mentors), coordinated research programmes with fields outside AI safety, and an internal research team that pilots the most promising directions.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: The main pipeline bringing other sciences into alignment research, with a 2026 summer fellowship symposium. Funded by AISI, SFF, Coefficient Giving, AISTOF and CAIF. Affiliates include Iliad and Alignment Journal.

candidates.name: Aintelope
candidates.one_line: A small volunteer AI-safety group (Roland Pihlakas, Gunnar Zarncke and colleagues; on their site, 'three guys' working in their spare time). It builds brain-like agents and open benchmarks that test whether agents can follow biologically and economically grounded objectives.
candidates.field_lens: Physiology (homeostasis), neuroscience-inspired agent design following Steven Byrnes' brain-like AGI paradigm, economics (diminishing returns)
candidates.ai_connection: Open-source gridworld benchmarks for RL and LLM agents covering homeostasis, bounded multi-objective utilities, diminishing returns, sustainability and resource sharing. The working paper 'From homeostasis to resource sharing' was posted to arXiv in September 2024. Newer work looks at how LLMs collapse into unbounded optimisation under stress. It is one of the few concrete efforts to make bounded, homeostatic objectives an alignment target rather than open-ended maximisation.

candidates.name: Survival and Flourishing Fund (SFF)
candidates.one_line: The second-largest AI-safety funder. It allocates grants through the 'S-process' and is effectively the only x-risk funder backing this biology and active-inference angle.
candidates.field_lens: Funder; it backs interdisciplinary and complexity-oriented alignment work
candidates.ai_connection: SFF-2025 recommended about $1.01M for PIBBSS/Princint and about $706k for ACS, and in June 2025 gave the Active Inference Institute $270k for its AI Capabilities & Alignment Consensus Project. A new funder looking for untried approaches could co-fund alongside it or learn from its grants.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Second-largest AI-safety funder. Its 2026 cycle expects $62.76M through the S-Process Main, Fairness and Freedom tracks, plus speculation grants, matching pledges and an initiative committee.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Assessor latitude and the themed tracks make it the main x-risk funder of interdisciplinary work. 2026 recommendations include ACS ($1.58M), Princint ($564k), Compassion Aligned ML ($457k), Effective Institutions Project ($2.19M), Modeling Cooperation ($108k), Common Grounds AI ($388k), Reciprocal Research ($719k) and The Future Society.

candidates.name: Center for the Study of Apparent Selves (CSAS)
candidates.one_line: A research centre at Rangjung Yeshe Institute in Kathmandu, directed by Thomas Doctor. It develops and tests models of intelligence that are 'ethically and aesthetically fulfilling' across substrates. Its team includes Michael Levin, Richard Watson, Olaf Witkowski, Elizaveta Solomonova, Paul Colognese and Bill Duane.
candidates.field_lens: Tibetan Buddhist philosophy, developmental biology and basal cognition (Levin), evolutionary theory (Watson), artificial life (Witkowski), cognitive science
candidates.ai_connection: Its outputs include 'Biology, Buddhism, and AI: Care as the Driver of Intelligence' and 'Building Bodhisattvas', with 'The Bodhisattva as an Alignment Target' pitched to frontier labs. Current work compares Buddhist psychology with internal patterns in frontier models. The 'Insights' publication, written with Chökyi Nyima Rinpoche, sets out Buddhist views of mind and selfhood for AI development. It lists Tufts, University of Tokyo, IAS and Anthropic among collaborating institutions. It is the clearest place where basal cognition, contemplative tradition and alignment meet.

alt_descriptions.one_line: A transdisciplinary institute that pairs Buddhist philosophy with biology and AI research to model 'caring intelligence', and proposes the bodhisattva ideal as an alignment target.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: TWCF-funded projects: 'Where Selves Are Mere Appearance' (2020-22, a handbook translating Buddhist concepts into AI problems), 'Care as the Driver of Intelligence' (2022-23) and 'Human Flourishing through Models of Care and Intelligence' (2023-24). 2026 essays: 'The Bodhisattva as an Alignment Target' (Mar 2026, the bodhisattva vow as a constitutional framework for labs), 'Resolving, Not Concealing: Contemplative Methods as Inspiration for AI Alignment' (May 2026, a framework developed with 84000 and 'in dialogue with Anthropic'), and 'Buddhist Wisdom and the Challenge of AI Emotions' (Jun 2026). Researchers include Thomas Doctor, Michael Levin, Olaf Witkowski and Paul Colognese.

candidates.name: NOOMA Labs
candidates.one_line: An independent lab led by Olaf Witkowski and set up with Foundry Labs as the successor to Cross Labs. It studies how intelligence emerges and adapts in living and artificial systems: agency and open-ended learning, collective intelligence, cognition and consciousness, embodiment.
candidates.field_lens: Artificial life, open-endedness, theory of agency, collective intelligence
candidates.ai_connection: Its first highlighted output is a 2026 paper, 'Neurodivergent influenceability in agentic AI as a contingent solution to the AI alignment problem'. It uses interacting LLM agents to study behavioural diversity, susceptibility to influence and the limits of alignment. It carries the Japanese ALife programme and the CSAS link into alignment questions. The lab is still 'being established'.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Independent Kyoto lab, led by Olaf Witkowski, that studies which principles of intelligence generalise across living and artificial systems: agency and open-ended learning, collective intelligence, cognition and consciousness, embodiment.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: It continues the research programme of Cross Labs (Kyoto, 2019 to 31 August 2026, now closed), which worked on a 'Theory of Agency' and AI and ALife workshops, and whose director co-authored 'Building Bodhisattvas' with Michael Levin and the Center for the Study of Apparent Selves. No explicit safety agenda yet, but it holds rare expertise on open-ended agency and multi-agent emergence that alignment needs. Founded with Foundry Labs.

alt_descriptions.one_line: An independent lab, led by Olaf Witkowski, that studies intelligence in living and artificial systems. It continues the research programme of Cross Labs, Cross Compass's Kyoto institute, which closed on 31 August 2026.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: 'Neurodivergent influenceability in agentic AI as a contingent solution to the AI alignment problem' (PNAS Nexus 2026). Work on collective intelligence across diverse biological systems, with Michael Levin. Cross Labs ran AI workshops with CSAS such as 'Building Bodhisattvas', so the seed list's Cross Labs entry should now point here.

candidates.name: Cross Labs
candidates.one_line: Cross Compass's Kyoto research institute (2019–2026), directed by Olaf Witkowski. It studied intelligence across biological, artificial and hybrid systems: open-endedness, theory of agency, collective learning. It closed on 31 August 2026 and its site is now an archive.
candidates.field_lens: Artificial life, complex systems, open-ended evolution
candidates.ai_connection: It was a hub for AI/ALife workshops and a CSAS partner. The research programme continues at NOOMA Labs. The seed list and the brief name it as a starting point, so the map should record it as closed rather than active.

candidates.name: Levin Lab / Allen Discovery Center at Tufts University
candidates.one_line: Michael Levin's lab and the Allen Discovery Center at Tufts. They study non-neural cognition, bioelectricity, morphogenesis and synthetic organisms, and aim to 'detect, understand, predict, and communicate with truly diverse intelligences', software AIs among them.
candidates.field_lens: Developmental biology, basal cognition, bioelectricity, diverse intelligence (the TAME framework, cognitive light cones)
candidates.ai_connection: Levin's multiscale competency architecture explains how sub-agents align into larger selves and defect from them, as in cancer. That model is the conceptual root of Softmax's organic alignment and of CSAS's care-based approach. It bears directly on detecting agency and goals in unfamiliar systems and on multi-agent collectives. The center hosts Adam Safron, who leads AII's alignment-focused AICACP. The lab itself does not frame its work as AI safety.

candidates.name: AI safety behavioural modelling group (The Anh Han), Teesside University
candidates.one_line: The Anh Han's group at Teesside University uses evolutionary game theory and agent-based models to study AI development races, safety commitments and trust in AI.
candidates.field_lens: Evolutionary game theory, the evolution of cooperation, agent-based modelling, behavioural economics
candidates.ai_connection: It models AI races as social dilemmas between SAFE and UNSAFE development, showing that safety collapses when supremacy looks near-term. It tests voluntary binding safety pledges, sanctions, and positive and negative incentives as alternatives to regulation. It is funded by the Future of Life Institute, the Leverhulme Trust and EPSRC ('Evolutionary Game Theory Under Uncertainty', 2024–27). Its collaborators include the Lisbon and Brussels evolutionary-dynamics groups (Santos, Lenaerts, Pereira).

candidates.name: Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Biology, Dept. of Theoretical Biology (with IT:U Linz Game Theory and Evolutionary Dynamics group)
candidates.one_line: Arne Traulsen's department in Plön and Christian Hilbe's new group at IT:U Linz work on the evolutionary dynamics of cooperation. In 2025 they explicitly bridged it to cooperative AI.
candidates.field_lens: Evolutionary game theory, theoretical biology of cooperation, social learning
candidates.ai_connection: The June 2025 PNAS special feature linked the evolution of cooperation with cooperative AI, with papers on collective cooperative intelligence, enforced cooperation under aligned incentives, and strategy selection. This work bears on whether populations of self-interested AI agents learn to cooperate or collude, and on mechanism design for multi-agent AI. Engagement with AI is still light.

candidates.name: Templeton World Charity Foundation: Diverse Intelligences initiative (TWCF)
candidates.one_line: A major funding programme for 'open-minded, forward-looking inquiry in animal, human, and machine intelligences'. Its challenge areas are 'Beyond the Turing Test', 'The Brilliance of the Living World' and 'Morality in the Machine Age'.
candidates.field_lens: Comparative cognition, animal intelligence, developmental science, moral and spiritual intelligence
candidates.ai_connection: In October 2025 it launched three global Diverse Intelligences research hubs: St Andrews (Europe), Princeton (North America) and Macquarie (Asia). It funded DISI from 2018 to 2023. Templeton money underwrites much of the diverse-intelligence network around Levin and CSAS, but it frames AI as curiosity and morality, not safety. It is the largest pool of money in this angle with no safety track.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Multiyear global funding priority to understand animal, human and machine intelligences across disciplines. Its challenge areas include 'Beyond the Turing Test' and 'Morality in the Machine Age'.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: It funds comparisons between machine and biological intelligence and work on human oversight of AI. In October 2025 it launched three global Diverse Intelligences Research Hubs. It is the main funder of the 'diverse intelligence' and basal-cognition community (Michael Levin and others) but has no explicit alignment programme: an untapped funding channel for multi-scale agency and alignment research.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Foundation priority funding multidisciplinary research on animal, human and machine intelligence. Its challenges include 'Beyond the Turing Test' (machine versus biological intelligence) and 'Morality in the Machine Age' (keeping humans in the loop), and it launched three global Diverse Intelligences research hubs in October 2025.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Funds direct comparisons of machine and biological minds, and practical engagement with AI applications. A separate priority, Accelerating Research on Consciousness (adversarial collaborations between rival theories), bears directly on AI consciousness and AI welfare. It is a natural funder for 'wise machines' and digital-minds work that the AI-safety funders treat as niche.

candidates.name: Global Research Centre for Diverse Intelligences (GRCDI), University of St Andrews
candidates.one_line: An interdisciplinary centre at St Andrews, co-directed by Josep Call and Amanda Seed, covering animal cognition, human creativity and artificial intelligence. TWCF chose it as its European Diverse Intelligences hub in September 2025, and it is launching seed funding for early-career researchers.
candidates.field_lens: Comparative and animal cognition, primatology, evolutionary psychology
candidates.ai_connection: Comparative cognition has decades of methods for asking what a non-human system 'really' understands without anthropomorphising. That bears directly on capability evaluation, deception and agency assessment for AI. AI engagement so far is mostly tooling, such as a RAG system for the community, so its seed fund is an obvious place for an AI-evaluation track.

candidates.name: Diverse Intelligences Summer Institute (DISI)
candidates.location: Rotating; 2026 at Hobart and William Smith Colleges, New York, USA (previously St Andrews)
candidates.one_line: A funded 3-week residential institute for about 40 early-career fellows from biology, anthropology, AI, cognitive science, computer science and philosophy, plus storytellers (artists, writers, podcasters). It explores 'the origins, nature, and future of intelligences'.
candidates.field_lens: Diverse intelligence across animals, humans and machines; arts and storytelling
candidates.ai_connection: It is one of the few standing venues where ML researchers work alongside animal-cognition and developmental scientists. It has no safety or alignment track, which makes it a ready-made recruiting ground for a 'biology for alignment' stream. Funded by the John Templeton Foundation (2024–present) and TWCF (2018–23).

alt_descriptions.one_line: Three-week residential institute (21 Jun to 11 Jul 2026). Fellows from biology, anthropology, AI, cognitive science, computer science, philosophy and sociology work alongside a 'storytellers' cohort of artists, writers and podcasters on the origins, nature and future of intelligences, and join a lifelong alumni network.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Trains exactly the cross-disciplinary people the int/a brief wants, with AI explicitly an eligible field, but has no safety framing. Pairing DISI fellows with Princint or CAIF-style safety mentors would be a cheap bridge. Funded by JTF since 2024, and by TWCF from 2018 to 2023.

candidates.name: Kinds of Intelligence programme / Animal-AI Environment, Leverhulme Centre for the Future of Intelligence (CFI)
candidates.one_line: A Cambridge CFI research strand that maintains Animal-AI, an open-source virtual laboratory of about 900 animal-cognition tasks (including the Animal-AI Olympics) for testing RL agents, LLM agents and humans on the same problems.
candidates.field_lens: Comparative psychology and animal cognition
candidates.ai_connection: It offers a cognition-first approach to AI capability evaluation: tasks designed to separate real competence (object permanence, causal reasoning, planning) from benchmark shortcuts, which counters anthropomorphic over-reading of AI abilities. The project is active and maintained (now supports Python 3.14). CFI's CASP group is on the classic map, but this strand is not.

candidates.name: Centre for the Advanced Study of Collective Behaviour (CASCB), University of Konstanz
candidates.location: Konstanz, Germany (with the Max Planck Institute of Animal Behavior)
candidates.one_line: A Cluster of Excellence studying how groups coordinate, from locusts, fish and bees to robot swarms, across species and scales of organisation.
candidates.field_lens: Collective animal behaviour, swarm intelligence, collective decision-making
candidates.ai_connection: Its knowledge of consensus formation, information cascades, leadership and collective failure modes bears directly on emergent behaviour in large populations of interacting AI agents and on hybrid human-AI collectives. Today it engages machines only through robot swarms, such as bee-inspired consensus algorithms and fish teaching robots in VR.

candidates.name: International Society for Artificial Life (ISAL)
candidates.one_line: The professional society of the artificial-life field. It runs the ALIFE conference series and the Artificial Life journal, and is the main community studying open-ended evolution, self-organisation and synthetic agency.
candidates.field_lens: Artificial life, open-ended evolution, evolutionary computation, self-organisation
candidates.ai_connection: ALife is the field that understands open-ended, self-improving evolutionary systems, which frontier labs now pursue under the name 'open-endedness'. ISAL has no AI-safety track, initiative or statement on its site. Its knowledge bears on the safety of open-ended search, on emergent agency, and on whether creativity in open-ended systems can be controlled (Ecoffet, Clune and Lehman 2020). The next conference is ALIFE 2027 in Prague, 19–23 July 2027.

candidates.name: IAS-Research Centre for Life, Mind and Society (UPV/EHU)
candidates.location: San Sebastián / Donostia, Basque Country, Spain
candidates.one_line: A theoretical-biology and philosophy-of-mind centre working on organismal autonomy and agency, levels of biological organisation, and the enactive approach to mind, with active seminars in 2026.
candidates.field_lens: Enactivism, theory of biological autonomy and minimal agency, philosophy of biology
candidates.ai_connection: Its account of what makes a system an agent (self-maintenance, sense-making, norm-generation) bears on a live safety question: when LLM-based systems should be treated as agents with goals. Members (Xabier Barandiaran) have analysed the mode of agency of LLMs, but the centre's own site shows no AI programme, so this is a potential bridge.

candidates.name: Rethink Wellbeing
candidates.one_line: Runs facilitated, group-based online mental health programmes (CBT Lab, IFS Lab) for 'ambitious altruists'; 285 participants from 35 countries, 66 trained lay facilitators, and an AI-assisted CBT Lab for low- and middle-income countries.
candidates.field_lens: Clinical psychology (CBT), Internal Family Systems, peer-support and lay-facilitator models from global mental health
candidates.ai_connection: The main existing structured mental health programme serving the EA/AI-safety talent pool. Its peer-group format is the scalable 'buddy system' that Kendiukhov's Sept 2026 LessWrong post asks for. It isn't tailored to AI-safety stressors such as short timelines, NDA-bound work or anticipatory grief, so an AI-safety-specific cohort is an obvious extension.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Runs peer-facilitated, evidence-based CBT Lab programmes for ambitious altruists, including AI-safety researchers: 285 participants in 35 countries and 66 trained facilitators so far. It is now building an AI-assisted version for young people in low- and middle-income countries.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Practically the only organised mental-health provision aimed at AI-safety workers, the 'health of the people doing the work' gap the seed list flags (a 59% burnout figure). It is on the classic map but small relative to need.

candidates.name: Mental Health Navigator (Mental Health Navigator CIO)
candidates.one_line: A curated, searchable database of mental health resources, with a sister directory of EA-familiar therapists and coaches (managed by Julia Wise), last updated June 2026.
candidates.field_lens: Mental health care navigation; clinical and coaching practice
candidates.ai_connection: The de facto referral layer for AI-safety people looking for a therapist who understands their worldview, named as existing infrastructure in the Sept 2026 'Psychological Support for AI Safety Researchers Is Neglected' post. It can't solve the core problem that NDA- or infohazard-bound work can't be discussed with outside therapists.

candidates.name: Upgradable
candidates.one_line: A 'life optimization' coaching nonprofit (the Upgrade Program) that explicitly focuses on helping AI-safety advocates. Its founder now spends most of his effort on Collective Action for Existential Safety (CAES).
candidates.field_lens: Behavioural science, applied rationality, coaching and personal-systems design
candidates.ai_connection: One of very few coaching services built for x-risk/AI-safety workers. It offers pro bono life-design calls for altruists and management consulting for EA leaders. Its shift toward CAES means less dedicated support capacity than its classic-map listing suggests.

candidates.name: AI Safety Support (AISS)
candidates.one_line: A former field-building organisation that offered free coaching and health/wellbeing coaching to early-career and independent AI-safety researchers. It now survives mainly as the home of the 'Lots of Links' resource list.
candidates.field_lens: Coaching and health coaching
candidates.ai_connection: The clearest precedent for AI-safety-specific wellbeing support. Its wind-down left a gap that the Sept 2026 LessWrong post explicitly points to ('previously offered free coaching').

candidates.name: Center for Applied Rationality (CFAR)
candidates.one_line: A rationality-training nonprofit that resumed its immersive 4.5-day mainline workshops in Nov 2025 (latest: 30 Sept–4 Oct 2026, full). The workshops mix classic techniques (TAPs, Inner Simulator, Goal Factoring) with new material on wholeness, aesthetics and team formation.
candidates.field_lens: Applied rationality, cognitive science, therapy-adjacent introspective techniques (for example, internal double crux)
candidates.ai_connection: Historically the main 'inner tooling' provider for the AI-safety community, with MIRI-linked workshops for alignment researchers. Its 2025–26 reboot reframes rationality around wholeness and pride, which makes it the rationalist lineage's closest analogue to int/a's 'inner work, outer change'.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Rationality-training nonprofit that relaunched four-day immersive workshops in 2026, after declaring 'narrative bankruptcy' on its old approach.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: It shaped the reasoning culture of the AI-safety community and earlier co-ran AI-risk workshops with MIRI. Its turn toward wholeness and pride overlaps with int/a's 'inner work, outer change'. It works on the human side of reasoning well about AI, not on AI tools.

candidates.name: FABRIC / European Summer Program on Rationality (ESPR)
candidates.location: UK (2026 camp in Somerset); European team
candidates.one_line: A fully funded immersive camp for mathematically talented 16–19-year-olds 'with a desire to understand themselves and the world'. It covers game theory, logic, cognitive science, argumentation and AI evaluation, and is run by the FABRIC team.
candidates.field_lens: Applied rationality, cognitive science, self-understanding pedagogy
candidates.ai_connection: A European pipeline that pairs self-knowledge with technical and AI-evaluation skills for future AI researchers. It's one of the few places where developmental, introspective training reaches people before they enter the field.

candidates.name: The AI Whistleblower Initiative (AIWI)
candidates.one_line: Supports concerned AI-company insiders 'from day zero' with Third Opinion (anonymous expert opinions), pro bono legal referral, whistleblower defence grants and privacy guidance.
candidates.field_lens: Whistleblowing law, organisational ethics, insider support
candidates.ai_connection: The only organisation built around the moral situation of frontier-lab employees who see risks. It addresses the isolation and fear around speaking up, a core lab-culture and field-health issue. Its support is legal and epistemic rather than psychological, which leaves room for a psychological-support complement.

candidates.name: Integral Altruism (int/a)
candidates.one_line: A movement that integrates EA with wisdom traditions, systems thinking, metarationality and inner development. It runs residential retreats (summit July 2025, Kent), speaker series, practice circles, hackathons and local gatherings.
candidates.field_lens: Metamodernism, contemplative and inner development, systems and metacrisis thinking
candidates.ai_connection: Its principle 'inner work, outer change' treats psychological and spiritual development as a foundation for sustainable impact. It publishes on AI governance (for example 'Metacrisis as a Framework for AI Governance'), and its practice circles and retreats are one of the few community spaces where AI-safety people do inner work together.

candidates.name: Wisdom + AI
candidates.location: UK-based voluntary network; retreats in Yorkshire (UK) and Colorado (USA)
candidates.one_line: A voluntary network, 'the home of dialogue between AI professionals and Buddhist teachers', founded by Jonathan Garner, Vinciane Rycroft and Sophie Maclaren. It runs monthly online dialogues and 6-day 'Human Flourishing + AI' meditation and neuroscience retreats (Yorkshire, 12–18 Sept 2026, with Oxford's Centre for Eudaimonia & Human Flourishing; Colorado, 9–15 Nov 2026).
candidates.field_lens: Buddhist contemplative practice, affective neuroscience (Oxford Centre for Eudaimonia)
candidates.ai_connection: It offers retreat-based contemplative training that AI practitioners can attend, with topics including building AI aligned with human values, ethics and safety. It's a ready-made container that could be pointed at AI-safety researchers' wellbeing.

alt_descriptions.one_line: A membership network for dialogue between AI professionals and Buddhist teachers. It runs monthly online dialogues and six-day retreats that combine meditation with neuroscience.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Retreats are run with Oxford's Centre for Eudaimonia & Human Flourishing (UK, 12-18 Sep 2026; US, 9-15 Nov 2026), alongside members-only monthly dialogues (latest 30 Sep 2026). It is one of the few working pieces of inner-development infrastructure aimed at people who build AI, and a channel for contemplative input into labs. Leadership is not listed publicly.

candidates.name: Monastic Academy for the Preservation of Life on Earth (MAPLE): AI Fellowship
candidates.one_line: A residential Buddhist-style training community whose AI Fellowship combines intensive monastic practice with work on AI ethics and safety, plus regular 'Awakening Week' retreats scheduled through May 2027.
candidates.field_lens: Monastic contemplative training (Soryu Forall)
candidates.ai_connection: The most intensive contemplative formation programme aimed specifically at people who want to work on AI going well. It carries serious public high-control allegations (2025–2026) that the site does not address; any map listing should flag them.

alt_descriptions.one_line: A residential Buddhist training community founded by Soryu Forall that frames its mission around existential risk and runs an AI Fellowship for people in tech and AI. FLAGGED: subject of serious public allegations of high-control dynamics and abuse.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Its AI Fellowship brings practitioners to the monastery (fellows trained about five months in 2025) and runs retreats aimed at people working on AI. A July 2026 LessWrong post ('The High-Control Dynamics at MAPLE', Kyle Hubbard) and an earlier open letter from former residents allege high-control practices, psychological harm and covered-up misconduct, and describe eschatological AI teachings. The site makes no statement on investigations. Do not present it as a recommended resource without due diligence. It shows why contemplative support for AI workers needs safeguarding standards.

candidates.name: Stanford Contemplation by Design: 2026 Summit 'The Role of Contemplation in the Age of AI'
candidates.one_line: Stanford's 13th annual free Contemplation by Design summit (14–25 Oct 2026), directed by Tia Rich (Applied Contemplative Science, Stanford Medicine). It has 20+ speakers on how contemplative science can guide 'the responsible governance and evolution of AI'.
candidates.field_lens: Contemplative science, multi-tradition practice (Buddhist, Christian, Taoist, secular), workplace wellbeing
candidates.ai_connection: An academic contemplative-science programme at the heart of Silicon Valley that has turned its whole annual summit toward AI governance and personal relationships with technology. It's a natural partner for practices aimed at AI builders.

candidates.name: Garrison Institute (incl. Contemplative-Based Resilience project)
candidates.one_line: A contemplative institute whose Contemplative-Based Resilience (CBR) project, co-founded by Sharon Salzberg, trains helping professionals in evidence-based stress resilience. CBR has trained MSF and Red Cross staff and, in 2022, US Congressional staff. The institute is holding an 'Artificial Intelligence and Our Spiritual Imagination' forum on 17–18 Oct 2026.
candidates.field_lens: Secular meditation, stress psychology, embodied practice; humanitarian-worker resilience
candidates.ai_connection: CBR is the most directly transferable template for AI-safety field health: a proven resilience curriculum for high-stakes, mission-driven workers, already delivered to policymakers' staff. With its new AI forum, the institute is one step from a programme for AI-safety researchers, AISI staff and AI policy staff.

candidates.name: Search Inside Yourself Leadership Institute (SIYLI)
candidates.one_line: A Google-born mindfulness and emotional intelligence nonprofit that trains mission-driven organisations in resilience. It now runs an 'Addressing AI Anxiety Workshop'.
candidates.field_lens: Mindfulness, emotional intelligence, neuroscience of resilience
candidates.ai_connection: One of the few established contemplative-training providers with a packaged AI-anxiety offering. Its tech-industry origins make it well placed to adapt the workshop for AI developers and safety teams facing doom-distress.

candidates.name: Jhourney
candidates.location: USA (retreats in Lake Tahoe and the UK, plus online)
candidates.one_line: A meditation edtech startup that teaches jhāna states through week-long retreats with daily facilitator check-ins, AI-assisted support and a post-retreat community. Its participants include engineers from OpenAI, Anthropic and Google.
candidates.field_lens: Theravāda jhāna practice, contemplative pedagogy
candidates.ai_connection: It is already reaching frontier-lab staff at scale with deep contemplative training, though framed around happiness rather than safety or wisdom. Its existing reach into lab culture is unused by the AI-safety community.

candidates.name: Art of Accomplishment
candidates.one_line: Joe Hudson's coaching and course company (Connection Course, Master Class, Great Decisions) teaching emotional and nervous-system integration for decision-making, with a featured testimonial from Sam Altman.
candidates.field_lens: Somatic and emotional coaching, decision science, inner-development practice
candidates.ai_connection: A rare inner-development provider with direct access to frontier-lab leadership. It shows a route by which emotional maturity work already shapes the people steering AI, outside any safety framing or accountability.

candidates.name: Data Workers' Inquiry (DWI)
candidates.location: Berlin (Weizenbaum Institute) and DAIR (remote); nine countries
candidates.one_line: A participatory research initiative, supported by DAIR and the Weizenbaum Institute, in which data annotators and content moderators research their own labour conditions, including trauma, mental health crises and exploitative management. Reports cover Kenya, Syria, Brazil, Europe and other countries.
candidates.field_lens: Labour studies, participatory action research (workers' inquiry), STS
candidates.ai_connection: It documents the psychological toll on the people who label data and moderate content to make models 'safe', the hidden workforce behind RLHF and safety filtering. That cost is absent from AI-safety discussions of 'field health'.

candidates.name: Fairwork
candidates.location: Oxford, UK (Oxford Internet Institute origin); 41 countries
candidates.one_line: An independent certification and research programme (led by Mark Graham) that rates firms commissioning AI data work against five fair-work principles. It publishes the 'Fairwork AI Principles' and reports such as 'The Workers Behind AI at Sama' and 'Humans in the Loop: Who Powers AI?'.
candidates.field_lens: Labour economics, development studies, internet geography
candidates.ai_connection: It provides auditable standards for the wellbeing of the annotation and moderation workforce whose judgements shape model safety behaviour. AI-safety labs and funders could adopt these standards for their own red-teaming and data pipelines.

candidates.name: The Wellbeing Project
candidates.one_line: Builds 'a culture of inner wellbeing' for changemakers through research (State of Changemaker Wellbeing survey), peer networks (including one for funders), and global and regional Hearth Summits (Ljubljana 2025).
candidates.field_lens: Changemaker wellbeing research, trauma-informed practice, social-sector culture change
candidates.ai_connection: It holds the best-developed evidence and practice on burnout in mission-driven fields, and its funder network and recurring wellbeing survey are exactly what AI safety lacks. The Aug 2026 survey finding of 59% burnout among AI-safety workers points to the need. It has no AI engagement yet.

candidates.name: Climate Psychology Alliance (CPA)
candidates.one_line: A UK community of therapists and practitioners working on the emotional and psychological dimensions of the climate crisis, through climate cafés, therapeutic support, parent circles and a journal that recently discussed 'AI and power'.
candidates.field_lens: Depth and psychoanalytic psychology, eco-psychology, group process
candidates.ai_connection: It has a decade of practice in holding existential-threat distress (eco-anxiety, anticipatory grief). Its methods, such as climate cafés, could be ported directly to AI doom-distress among researchers, advocates and the public. No 'AI café' network exists yet.

candidates.name: The Mindfulness Initiative
candidates.one_line: A policy institute that argues 'capacities of heart and mind' belong at the centre of policymaking. It has supported about 300 UK politicians through mindfulness training, set up an All-Party Parliamentary Group, and inspired programmes in 14 national parliaments.
candidates.field_lens: Mindfulness, contemplative policy, public-sector inner development
candidates.ai_connection: It has proven channels for inner-capacity training inside legislatures. These are directly applicable to the stress and complexity facing AI policymakers and AI Safety Institute staff, but it has no AI-specific work yet.

candidates.name: Inner Development Goals (IDG)
candidates.one_line: A nonprofit framework of 25 inner skills across five dimensions (Being, Thinking, Relating, Collaborating, Acting), with summits, a business coalition and an IDG Business Forum 2026.
candidates.field_lens: Adult development, leadership science, sustainability transitions
candidates.ai_connection: It is a widely adopted shared language for inner capacities among corporate and policy leaders, but no AI programme was found. An 'IDGs for AI developers and governors' track is an obvious, unbuilt bridge.

candidates.name: Presencing Institute
candidates.location: Cambridge MA, USA and Berlin, Germany
candidates.one_line: Otto Scharmer's action-research platform for Theory U, with u.lab (Sept 2026–May 2027), Social Presencing Theater (including Berlin, Nov 2026) and 4D mapping trainings.
candidates.field_lens: Awareness-based systems change, Theory U, embodied social-field methods
candidates.ai_connection: Its awareness-based leadership and multi-stakeholder sensing methods bear on the culture and decision quality of AI lab leadership and governance convenings. Its current programmes show no AI-specific work.

candidates.name: Iliad
candidates.one_line: Umbrella organisation that develops AI safety as a 'theoretical and experimental science': it runs the Iliad Intensive (four-week course) and the Iliad Fellowship, the annual Iliad and Agent Foundations conferences and the Alignment Journal, and incubates four research groups.
candidates.field_lens: Applied mathematics, theoretical physics, theoretical CS, learning theory, decision theory, causality
candidates.ai_connection: It runs the Agent Foundations conference series (third edition at CMU, March 2026: decision theory, learning theory, abstractions and world models, causality, logical induction, bounded optimality). It incubates AIXI Labs (algorithmic-information models of superintelligence), Principia ('theoretical model organisms' of neural nets), Stormglass (causal mechanisms of training) and XOR Labs (emergence of agency). It trains mathematicians and physicists in London and the Bay Area, with cohorts scheduled from October 2026 to January 2027. Led by Alexander Gietelink Oldenziel with David Udell.

candidates.name: Resolution (incorporating Timaeus)
