candidates.one_line: Alignment nonprofit founded in June 2026 by researchers from UK AISI's Alignment Team and Timaeus. It pursues 'theory unlocks higher automation': singular learning theory, learning theory, game theory and scalable oversight, plus theory-guided automated research.
candidates.field_lens: Singular learning theory (algebraic geometry plus statistical physics), learning theory, game theory
candidates.ai_connection: Timaeus's developmental interpretability and SLT agenda continues here: susceptibilities, linear-response estimators, 'Interpreting RL Agents' and 'Elicitation without Backpropagation' (2026). Timaeus ran the ODYSSEY 2025 conference and the 'Mathematical Science of AI Safety' focus period (Sydney, Nov-Dec 2025). Chief Scientist Geoffrey Irving; Head of Research Daniel Murfet; Jesse Hoogland led Timaeus. It plans 40-80 staff within two years. Note: Timaeus itself is not separately on the classic map; Resolution is.
candidates.location: Berkeley, with remote staff in London and Melbourne

candidates.name: Mathematical AI Safety Institute (MAISI)
candidates.one_line: IAS-style institute that hosts mathematicians as Members for one or two semesters to build rigorous mathematical definitions and foundations of what it would mean for powerful AI to be safe.
candidates.field_lens: Pure mathematics
candidates.ai_connection: Targets the gap that 'we lack a rigorous understanding of what it would mean to be safe, even in theory'. It received $10M from Coefficient Giving in September 2026. It is recruiting 10-30 faculty for January 2027 and 30-100 for a September 2027 Special Year. Scientific Director Jacob Tsimerman (2026 Fields Medalist); Executive Director Andrew Critch; advisers include Timothy Gowers, Paul Christiano and Geoffrey Irving. This is the largest single bet yet on drawing top pure mathematicians into safety.

candidates.name: XOR Labs
candidates.one_line: Iliad-incubated lab directed by complexity scientist Fernando Rosas that studies how agentic behaviour emerges in AI systems and in interacting agents, using information theory and complexity science.
candidates.field_lens: Complexity science, information theory (partial information decomposition, causal emergence), control theory, cognitive science, thermodynamics of information
candidates.ai_connection: Three lines of work: agentic interpretability (reverse-engineering world models and planning), risks of emergent collective behaviour in multi-agent systems, and metacognition in LLMs. It explicitly practises 'methodological pluralism'. The team includes Artemy Kolchinsky, Abel Jansma, Alec Boyd and David Ehrlich, with publications in Nature Reviews Physics, PNAS and Physical Review Research on information decomposition and hierarchical emergence. Funded by UK AISI, Coefficient Giving and AISTOF. It is not on the classic map, and is the clearest case of mainstream complexity science moving into AI safety.
candidates.location: London (University of Sussex links), with international collaborators

candidates.name: Stormglass AI Safety Institute (formerly MoirAI)
candidates.one_line: Iliad-incubated PrincInt affiliate that aims to 'advance the science of AI learning dynamics': the causal mechanisms by which training and design choices shape model behaviour.
candidates.field_lens: Learning dynamics, dynamical systems, statistical approaches to training
candidates.ai_connection: It builds theory and practical tools so that labs and policymakers can detect unsafe behaviours earlier in training. Led by Max Hennick. The website is under construction, and staff and outputs are not yet public.

candidates.name: Alignment Journal
candidates.one_line: New peer-reviewed journal (announced March 2026) for foundational, theory-driven alignment research: agent theory, formal safety proofs, learning-theoretic properties, scalable oversight and interpretability foundations.
candidates.field_lens: Mathematics, theoretical CS, philosophy of agency
candidates.ai_connection: It gives theoretical and interdisciplinary safety work an academic venue and credential, which helps recruit academics from other fields. Managing editors Dan MacKinlay and Jess Riedel; advisory board includes Geoffrey Irving, Marcus Hutter, Scott Aaronson and Victoria Krakovna. Papers were under review as of late 2026. It is linked to the Iliad and PrincInt network; the classic map mentions it only inside Iliad's description.

candidates.name: Fields Institute Centre for Mathematical AI
candidates.one_line: Centre at Toronto's Fields Institute for Research in Mathematical Sciences that applies mathematical rigour to understanding AI. It runs a joint 'Mathematics for AI Safety' programme and two-year postdocs with PrincInt.
candidates.field_lens: Pure and applied mathematics, statistical mechanics, geometric analysis
candidates.ai_connection: Fall 2026 courses: 'Mathematics for AI Safety', 'Mathematical Foundations of AI' and a mini-course on statistical-mechanical approaches to deep learning. Postdocs work on mean-field theory, renormalization-group methods and learning-landscape geometry for interpretability. Partners: Schwartz Reisman Institute and Vector Institute. Director Kasra Rafi; the AI-safety strand is led by Yevgeny Liokumovich. It is a template for embedding safety inside a mainstream mathematics institute.

candidates.name: Dovetail
candidates.one_line: Agent-foundations research group doing 'foundational mathematics research that gives us an understanding of the nature of AI agents', and running a research fellowship.
candidates.field_lens: Mathematics of agency (agent structure, selection theorems, abstraction)
candidates.ai_connection: It works on when and how optimisation produces agent-like structure, in order to ground claims about AI goals. Funded by LTFF and ARIA. Its fellowship trains mathematicians in agent foundations. Led by Alex Altair. The site is current in 2026, but detail on outputs is sparse.

candidates.name: Computational Rational Agents Laboratory (CORAL)
candidates.one_line: Agent-foundations lab pursuing Vanessa Kosoy's learning-theoretic agenda: mathematical theory of computationally bounded agents, as a route to aligning AI objectives with human values.
candidates.field_lens: Computational learning theory, control theory, algorithmic information theory, categorical systems theory
candidates.ai_connection: The learning-theoretic agenda includes infra-Bayesianism. Kosoy (via ALTER, Israel) holds an ARIA Safeguarded AI TA1.1 grant for 'Learning-Theoretic AI Safety'. Fiscally sponsored by Ashgro.

candidates.name: AIXI Labs (AI X-risk Initiative)
candidates.one_line: Iliad-incubated nonprofit that studies 'algorithmic information theoretic foundations of AI agents', using AIXI variants to analyse deception, power-seeking and the scalability of mitigations in idealised superintelligent agents.
candidates.field_lens: Algorithmic information theory, universal AI (Hutter), Bayesian decision theory
candidates.ai_connection: It formalises risk factors (deception, power-seeking) and safety mitigations in agents general enough to model superintelligence, then tries to carry the results over to LLM agents. Led by Cole Wyeth.

candidates.name: AFFINE Network
candidates.one_line: Training network for 'ambitious holistic alignment theory': a fully funded one-month seminar (2026 at Hostačov Château, Czechia; January 2027 in Portugal), a year-long fellowship for about 10 people, and mentorship.
candidates.field_lens: Philosophical and mathematical agent foundations; exploratory, frame-finding pedagogy
candidates.ai_connection: It aims to make alignment 'a science capable of coherently and formally articulating risks, guarantees, predictions' rather than trial-and-error. Its pedagogy deliberately makes room for open-ended conceptual exploration, unusual in the field and close to int/a's emphasis on discernment. Led by Noa 'Ouro' Hölzer; a PrincInt affiliate.

candidates.name: Causal Incentives Working Group
candidates.one_line: Cross-institution working group that uses causal influence diagrams to formalise agents' incentives (value of information and control, response and control incentives) for safe and fair AI.
candidates.field_lens: Causal inference, decision theory, game theory, formal theory of agency
candidates.ai_connection: Work includes measuring goal-directedness in LLMs, 'robust agents learn causal world models' (ICLR 2024 honourable mention), deception definitions, higher-order beliefs in multi-agent settings, and the PyCID library. Members include Tom Everitt and Jon Richens (Google DeepMind), Ryan Carey and James Fox (Oxford), Francis Rhys Ward and Matt MacDermott (Imperial), and Lewis Hammond (CAIF). The latest listed publications are from 2025.
candidates.location: UK-centred (Oxford, Imperial, DeepMind London), plus US and Spain

candidates.name: ARIA Safeguarded AI programme
candidates.one_line: £59M UK ARIA programme building mathematical and formal-methods tooling so that AI agents produce verifiable, assured artifacts. It has funded the largest cohort of category theorists ever pointed at AI safety.
candidates.field_lens: Category theory, categorical probability, string diagrams, coalgebra, type theory, formal verification
candidates.ai_connection: Its TA1.1 theory grants fund 14 teams, among them 'Double Categorical Systems Theory for Safeguarded AI' (David Jaz Myers, Topos Research UK), GLAIVE, Sam Staton (Oxford, categorical probability), Fabio Zanasi (UCL), Alessandro Abate (Oxford, SAINT), Vanessa Kosoy (ALTER) and David Corfield ('Philosophical Applied Category Theory'). Restructured November 2025 to May 2026: it dropped plans for a bespoke AI system and refocused on TA1 tooling and cybersecurity applications, and cancelled TA3 Phase 2. Nora Ammann, a PIBBSS co-founder, became Programme Director in April 2026; davidad is now Technical Advisor. The classic map lists ARIA as a funder but not this programme.

candidates.name: UK AISI Alignment Project
candidates.one_line: International alignment grant programme led by UK AISI that awarded over £27M to 60+ projects in 2025, explicitly including information theory, computational complexity, economic and game theory, probabilistic methods, learning theory and cognitive science.
candidates.field_lens: Information theory, cryptography, complexity theory, game and economic theory, cognitive science
candidates.ai_connection: It is the largest public pot to date for bringing academic theorists from adjacent fields into alignment, with compute, mentorship from AISI's alignment team and co-funders (CIFAR, Schmidt Sciences, Halcyon, ARIA, UKRI, Anthropic, OpenAI and others). The site says AISI is 'unlikely to run a similar program in 2026'. Funded projects continue, but a funding cliff for academic theorists looms. UK AISI itself is on the classic map; this programme is not.

alt_descriptions.one_line: International alignment fund led by UK AISI. Its first round awarded over £27M to 60+ projects (£50k to £1M each) and explicitly invited information theory, economic and game theory, cognitive science, computational complexity and learning theory.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: The first government safety fund to deliberately widen the disciplines it funds. Partners include the Canadian and Australian AISIs, OpenAI, Microsoft, AWS, Anthropic, Schmidt Sciences, Halcyon Futures, Renaissance Philanthropy, UKRI and ARIA. AISI says it is 'unlikely to run a similar program in 2026', which leaves a gap for a successor round that would also take in psychology, the humanities and complexity science.

candidates.name: Topos Institute (incl. Topos Research UK)
candidates.one_line: Nonprofit pioneering 'mathematical systems science' with applied category theory. It builds tools for collaborative modelling and collective sense-making (such as CatColab) that 'enable cooperation across difference'.
candidates.field_lens: Applied category theory, systems theory, collaborative modelling, collective intelligence
candidates.ai_connection: Its UK arm (Topos Research UK; CEO Brendan Fong, Chair Ilyas Khan) holds an ARIA Safeguarded AI grant for 'Double Categorical Systems Theory for Safeguarded AI' (David Jaz Myers): compositional world models and specifications for AI operating in safety-critical systems. A 2026 blog series covers formal modelling with LLM assistance. Its mission language ('knowledge and compassion', addressing risks of emerging technologies) is close to int/a's.

candidates.name: GLAIVE (Glasgow Lab for AI Verification)
candidates.one_line: Nonprofit research group 'applying category theory to AI verification' through typed tactics for theorem proving, structured (container-theoretic) neural architectures, and Polylang, a language built on lenses and containers.
candidates.field_lens: Category theory, categorical cybernetics, dependent type theory, programming languages
candidates.ai_connection: It holds an ARIA Safeguarded AI TA1.1 grant ('True Categorical Programming for Composable Systems', Jade Master and Zans Mihejevs). Team: Jules Hedges, Bruno Gavranović (categorical deep learning), André Videla, Dylan Braithwaite, Zans Mihejevs. It overlaps in people with the CyberCat Institute (Institute for Categorical Cybernetics, a nonprofit since 2024, which develops 'theory and software for governing systems that learn and make decisions' but has no explicit safety programme).

candidates.name: ANU School of Cybernetics
candidates.one_line: University school re-establishing cybernetics as a discipline 'for navigating major societal transformations' through safe, sustainable and responsible approaches to new systems. It offers a Master of Applied Cybernetics, PhDs and a Cybernetic Imagination Residency.
candidates.field_lens: Cybernetics (first and second order), systems thinking, anthropology of technology
candidates.ai_connection: Runs AI systems research (for example 'AI Adoption in Australia' with Google) and trains practitioners to treat AI as part of socio-technical systems. Still active in September 2026 under director Katherine Daniell. No x-risk framing: a natural partner for systems-level AI governance work.

alt_descriptions.one_line: An Australian National University school that revives cybernetics as a cross-disciplinary approach to building and governing complex technological systems. It offers a Master of Applied Cybernetics, PhDs and short courses.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: It treats AI as part of cyber-physical systems that must be made 'safe, sustainable and responsible'. Projects include AI Adoption in Australia (with Google). It was founded by Genevieve Bell and is directed by Katherine Daniell (2026). It has no x-risk framing, but it is the most established home of systems and cybernetic thinking about AI.

candidates.name: Santa Fe Institute (SFI)
candidates.one_line: The flagship independent complexity-science institute. Its faculty publish on intelligence, emergence and collective computation, including deflationary analyses of LLM capabilities.
candidates.field_lens: Complex adaptive systems, emergence, collective intelligence, evolutionary theory, thermodynamics of computation
candidates.ai_connection: Example: Krakauer, Krakauer and Mitchell, 'Large Language Models and Emergence: A Complex Systems Perspective' (June 2025). Melanie Mitchell's work on abstraction and understanding in AI; SFI faculty advising judges on AI (2026). It has many of the tools AI safety needs (emergence, multi-scale agency, collective dynamics) but no AI-risk programme. The SFI website was hard to verify in detail.

candidates.name: Simons Collaboration on the Physics of Learning and Neural Computation
candidates.one_line: Simons Foundation collaboration, directed by Surya Ganguli (Stanford), that treats 'AI as a complex physical system' to explain how large networks learn, scale, reason and fail.
candidates.field_lens: Statistical physics, mathematics, theoretical neuroscience
candidates.ai_connection: It aims to 'break AI out of its black box' and explain emergent capabilities and 'mysterious failures'. That bears directly on interpretability and on predicting dangerous capability emergence, but it is framed as basic science, not safety. Yasaman Bahri is among the PIs. A clear candidate for a Fields/PrincInt-style safety bridge.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Simons Foundation collaboration directed by Surya Ganguli that treats large neural networks as complex physical systems, using physics, mathematics, neuroscience and statistics to explain scaling, emergent capabilities and 'mysterious failures'.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: A science-of-deep-learning base for interpretability and for predicting emergent capabilities. It is funded outside the AI-safety ecosystem and not framed as safety, a natural target for Princint-style bridging.

candidates.name: Complexity Science Hub Vienna (CSH)
candidates.one_line: European complexity-science institute with programmes on systemic risk, social complexity and collapse, collective minds, algorithmic fairness, and AI and machine learning.
candidates.field_lens: Network science, systemic risk, cliodynamics and societal collapse, computational social science
candidates.ai_connection: It has begun engaging with AI: LLM audits under algorithmic fairness (for example, whom LLMs recommend as physics experts) and AI/ML for supply-chain metabolism. Specific problem: its systemic-risk and collapse modelling could quantify gradual-disempowerment and cascading-failure dynamics in AI-saturated economies, but no AI-safety framing was found.

candidates.name: Basis Research Institute
candidates.one_line: Nonprofit AI research organisation building a 'universal reasoning engine' from probabilistic programming and causal inference, with projects on automated scientific discovery, participatory city modelling and animal collective behaviour.
candidates.field_lens: Probabilistic programming, causal inference, Bayesian dynamical systems, cognitive science
candidates.ai_connection: No safety framing found on its site. Specific bearing: its open-source tools (ChiRho, a causal extension of Pyro; Dynestyx for Bayesian dynamical systems) are the kind of auditable causal world-model infrastructure that Safeguarded- or Guaranteed-Safe-AI approaches need. Listed as a starting point, but on inspection it is potential, not core.

candidates.name: Flourishing Intelligence Program (FLIP), Centre for Eudaimonia and Human Flourishing, University of Oxford
candidates.location: Oxford, UK (Linacre College); International Centre for Flourishing nodes in Barcelona (UPF) and Aarhus
candidates.one_line: An Oxford programme led by Ruben Laukkonen with Morten Kringelbach. It studies how neuroscience, meditation and contemplative wisdom can inform intrinsically aligned, brain-inspired AI and embodied human-AI interfaces.
candidates.field_lens: Contemplative neuroscience; active inference and predictive processing; Buddhist contemplative principles (mindfulness, emptiness, non-duality, boundless care)
candidates.ai_connection: The institutional home of the 'Contemplative Artificial Intelligence' / 'Contemplative Wisdom for Superalignment' agenda (Laukkonen, Inglis, Chandaria, Sandved-Smith, Lopez-Sola, Hohwy, Gold, Elwood; arXiv 2504.15125; AGI-25 proceedings). It argues for intrinsic rather than control-based alignment, and reports that prompting models with contemplative principles improved AILuminate safety scores and Prisoner's Dilemma cooperation. The research plan has three layers: humans, interfaces and AI. Funded by a private donation (the Cillo family). Partners with Positive AI Labs, and runs retreats with the Wisdom + AI Network.

candidates.name: Wisdom and Culture Lab (University of Waterloo)
candidates.one_line: Igor Grossmann's psychology lab, which studies wise reasoning across cultures and is building a research line on AI metacognition and human-AI judgement.
candidates.field_lens: Empirical wisdom science, cultural psychology, judgement and decision-making, forecasting
candidates.ai_connection: Co-led 'Imagining and building wise machines: The centrality of AI metacognition' (Johnson, Karimi, Bengio, Chater, Gerstenberg, Larson, Levine, Mitchell, Rahwan, Schölkopf, Grossmann; Trends in Cognitive Sciences, 2026). The paper argues that metacognitive strategies (intellectual humility, perspective-taking, context-adaptability) would make AI more robust, explainable, cooperative and safer. In 2026 the lab is hiring postdocs in AI Metacognition and in Human-AI Systems for Expert Judgment. Its 15-lab Wise Judgment Consortium gives cross-cultural ground truth that wisdom evaluations could use. It is the strongest empirical anchor for 'wisdom evals'.

candidates.name: Positive AI Labs
candidates.one_line: A US nonprofit that builds open-source datasets and evaluations to steer frontier models towards 'positive alignment' (human flourishing, pluralistic wisdom and virtue), drawing on material from wisdom holders including Buddhist teachers.
candidates.field_lens: Wisdom traditions (Buddhist, faith and Indigenous sources), virtue ethics, positive psychology
candidates.ai_connection: A four-stage 'translation pipeline' (curation, translation, validation, adoption) turns wisdom sources into open evaluations and training data. It frames 'positive alignment' as a complement to safety alignment. Partners: FLIP (Oxford), Halcyon Futures, UCLA, AI and Faith and Indigenous Commons; METR is listed as an ecosystem partner. It is one of very few groups actually building what the seed list calls 'wisdom evals'. The site shows no dated outputs yet.

candidates.name: Meaning Alignment Institute (MAI)
candidates.location: Berlin, Germany and San Francisco, USA
candidates.one_line: A nonprofit researching how to align AI, markets and democratic institutions with what people actually value. Its tools are 'thick models of value', moral graphs and its Full-Stack Alignment programme.
candidates.field_lens: Philosophy of values and meaning (sources of meaning, thick evaluative concepts), social choice, institutional design
candidates.ai_connection: Democratic Fine-Tuning and moral graphs (2023-24); 'Model Integrity' (Dec 2024) and 'Model Integrity and Character' (Feb 2026); the Full-Stack Alignment paper (arXiv 2512.03399), on aligning AI and the institutions that deploy it together; 'Designing Institutions for a World with Powerful AI' (Apr 2026); and the Pax Machina publication (Aug 2026). Funded by ARIA, OpenAI, SFF and EIP. It is the most developed meaning-centred alignment programme.

candidates.name: Arising Initiative
candidates.one_line: An independent nonprofit research initiative that treats the human-AI relationship ('the dyad') as the unit of analysis. It uses Madhyamaka Buddhist philosophy to study how people attribute minds to AI, AI moral status, and human safety in human-AI relationships.
candidates.field_lens: Madhyamaka Buddhism (dependent origination, critique of reification), relational philosophy of mind
candidates.ai_connection: Essays (Jun-Aug 2026) on reification errors in debates about AI consciousness and on relational rather than locational accounts of mind, plus a forthcoming book, 'AI: Arising Interdependently'. The work bears on AI welfare and moral-status questions, and on the psychological risks of human-AI attachment. Listed by the Buddhism & AI Initiative under Buddhism→AI alignment research.

candidates.name: 84000: Translating the Words of the Buddha
candidates.location: Global (translation project); AI workshop held in San Francisco
candidates.one_line: A nonprofit translating the Tibetan Buddhist canon into English. It has begun convening AI researchers and Buddhist scholars on alignment, and co-developed contemplative alignment methods with CSAS.
candidates.field_lens: Tibetan Buddhist textual scholarship, Buddhist ethics (compassion, interdependence, non-harming)
candidates.ai_connection: Ran a workshop in San Francisco (26-27 Jul 2025) on Buddhist frameworks for reducing harm, bias and misalignment in AI, with plans for interdisciplinary working groups. CSAS's 2026 framework, which treats 'contemplative methods as a functional resource for alignment', was developed with 84000 in dialogue with Anthropic. 84000 also uses AI to speed up translation.

candidates.name: NonZero (Robert Wright's Nonzero Foundation / NonZero Newsletter)
candidates.one_line: Robert Wright's newsletter and podcast on 'averting the apocalypse', now dominated by AI safety, the AI race and US-China analysis. Wright is the author of 'Why Buddhism Is True' and 'Nonzero'.
candidates.field_lens: Evolutionary psychology, Buddhist psychology and meditation, non-zero-sum game theory
candidates.ai_connection: Sustained 2026 coverage, e.g. 'Trump and the AI Safety Vibe Shift', 'Dario's China Syndrome' and 'Superintelligence, the Singularity, and the Singleton' (Sep-Oct 2026). It challenges the adversarial US-China AI-race framing, a public-facing version of int/a's 'don't exacerbate the race' principle. About 51k subscribers. The Buddhism & AI Initiative lists it as media covering Buddhism, meditation and AI.

candidates.name: Connecting Intelligence
candidates.one_line: A new (2026) research initiative that uses facilitated games and embodied group practices to build organisational cultures able to meet the challenges of powerful AI, with a contemplative-practice workstream.
candidates.field_lens: Tibetan meditation, collective-trauma work (Thomas Hübl lineage), distributed cognition, group facilitation
candidates.ai_connection: Led by Max Roth and Ryan Lowe (research ecosystem lead at MAI, formerly on OpenAI's alignment team). It targets sensemaking, epistemic resilience, trust and group coherence inside AI-relevant organisations: the 'inner work, outer change' layer for labs and safety teams. No published outputs yet.

candidates.name: Compassion Aligned Machine Learning (CaML)
candidates.one_line: A nonprofit research group working to make advanced AI compassionate towards all sentient beings (animals and digital minds), through benchmarks and pretraining-data interventions.
candidates.field_lens: Compassion ethics extended to all sentient beings, animal welfare, moral humility
candidates.ai_connection: Runs the CompassionBench leaderboard and benchmarks including AnimalHarmBench 2.0, TAC (Travel Agent Compassion, where every frontier model tested chose the harmful option more often than not) and Manager Coercion Bench. Its synthetic-document finetuning raised models' attention to animal welfare from 40% to 77%. It also runs the 'Hyperstition for Good' mid-training corpus. Funded by SFF, the Navigation Fund and BlueDot. It is the operational 'boundless care' end of this angle.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Nonprofit that uses synthetic-document finetuning and its CompassionBench leaderboard to make frontier models care about all sentient beings, including animals and digital minds, without locking in values.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: CompassionBench tracks frontier models on benchmarks such as Travel Agent Compassion and Manager Coercion. Its 'Hyperstition for Good' project builds an open mid-training corpus about animals and digital minds. Partners include Sentient Futures, EleutherAI and Wild Animal Initiative.

candidates.name: Mind & Life Institute
candidates.location: Charlottesville, Virginia, USA (sister organisation Mind & Life Europe)
candidates.one_line: A long-standing contemplative-science nonprofit, founded with the Dalai Lama, that devoted its 39th Dialogue, 'Minds, Artificial Intelligence, and Ethics' (Dharamsala, Oct 2025), to AI.
candidates.field_lens: Contemplative science, Tibetan Buddhism, neuroscience, philosophy
candidates.ai_connection: Dialogue XXXIX brought together more than 100 scientists, monastics, philosophers, business leaders and policymakers on what intelligence is, whether ethics can be embedded in AI, AI narratives, justice and education. No ongoing AI programme appears on its 2026 site. Its research grants, Summer Research Institute and Mind & Life Europe (a collaborator of the Buddhism & AI Initiative) are natural hosts for a contemplative-AI research track.

candidates.name: Gloo Flourishing AI Benchmark (FAI)
candidates.one_line: A benchmark from the faith-tech company Gloo that scores LLMs across seven dimensions of human flourishing, derived from Harvard's Human Flourishing Program and the Global Flourishing Study.
candidates.field_lens: Flourishing science (positive psychology, character and virtue, meaning and purpose, faith and spirituality)
candidates.ai_connection: FAI (1,229 questions, July 2025; arXiv 2507.07787) found no model 'acceptably aligned' across all dimensions; the weakest were Faith & Spirituality, Character & Virtue, and Meaning & Purpose. A Christian-worldview variant, FAI-C, followed in Dec 2025, with an insights report in June 2026. It is a working template for flourishing and wisdom evaluations, though the sponsor's values shape it.

candidates.name: Center for Buddhist AI Ethics (CamTech University)
candidates.one_line: A university centre, founded June 2023 and directed by Prof. Chhem Kieth Rethy, that promotes AI development guided by Buddhist ethics through seminars, mindful education, research and policy advocacy.
candidates.field_lens: Theravada Buddhist ethics, compassion
candidates.ai_connection: Its Buddhist AI Ethics Seminar Series has run four iterations up to Sep 2025 (e.g. 'Embracing compassionate AI'). It focuses on bias, privacy and jobs rather than catastrophic risk. A rare institutional node in a Southeast Asian Theravada country, listed in the Buddhism & AI Initiative's governance and scholarship domains.

candidates.name: Wisdom Beyond
candidates.one_line: Facilitated retreats and working groups that bring high-impact leaders together around AI and contemplative practice.
candidates.field_lens: Contemplative practice, systems and regenerative thinking
candidates.ai_connection: Its sixth cohort, 'Beacons of Resonance: A retreat on AI & Attunement' (Oct 2026), is billed as one of its last public retreats before it moves to invite-only gatherings. It is inner-work infrastructure for leaders shaping AI. Facilitators are not named on the site.

candidates.name: John Templeton Foundation: Future of Intelligence venture (JTF)
candidates.one_line: JTF's 'Future of Intelligence' venture, which will award over $60M over three years from 2026 to philosophers, ethicists, biologists, neuroscientists, physicists and computer scientists working on the nature, diversity, plurality and future of intelligence.
candidates.field_lens: Philosophy, theology, cognitive and biological sciences, virtue and character research
candidates.ai_connection: Theme 4 asks how to design a future of flourishing and wisdom for augmented, enhanced and shared intelligence. Separately, JTF gave $8M (Jan 2025) for character development in the digital age, including four AI projects: Stanford/Challenge Success, Harvard IMAGINE, UC Berkeley (Kidd), and UC Irvine (Doroudi & Pritchard, intellectual character). It is the largest pot of money in this angle, and is mostly disconnected from AI-safety networks.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Private foundation whose new three-year Future of Intelligence venture, starting in 2026, will grant over $60M across its six funding areas to philosophers, theologians, biologists, neuroscientists, physicists, computer scientists and storytellers working on what intelligence is and where it is going.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: The portfolio covers four questions: the story, diversity and plurality of intelligence, and 'The Future of Intelligence', which takes in competing AI visions from abundance to existential risk. It also covers consciousness, agency and personhood, and collective intelligence. The public launch, 'Intelligence Everywhere', was on 3 Oct 2026 in Santa Monica (with Alison Gopnik and Blaise Agüera y Arcas), alongside a Futures Collaborative and a podcast. JTF has also funded DISI since 2024. This is the largest new pot of money for humanistic and scientific work on AI-era intelligence, but it is framed around understanding, not safety.

candidates.name: Templeton World Charity Foundation (TWCF)
candidates.one_line: A funder whose Diverse Intelligences, Consciousness and Human Flourishing programmes paid for CSAS's Buddhism-AI work and fund contemplative and consciousness science.
candidates.field_lens: Diverse intelligences, consciousness science, science of religious and spiritual practice
candidates.ai_connection: Grants: 'Where Selves Are Mere Appearance' ($233k, 2020-22), 'Care as the Driver of Intelligence' ($100k, 2022-23) and 'Human Flourishing through Models of Care and Intelligence' (2023-24), all to CSAS/Rangjung Yeshe. Current programmes include Diverse Intelligences and the Science of Religious and Spiritual Exercises. No AI-specific call appears on its 2026 site.

candidates.name: Glorisun Global Network: Buddhism and Global Governance
candidates.location: Network across Peking University and UBC (FROGBEAR); 2025 symposium in Paris
candidates.one_line: An academic Buddhist-studies network whose July 2025 symposium in Paris examined what Buddhist philosophy offers to AI ethics and global governance.
candidates.field_lens: Buddhist studies (Chinese and Tibetan), compassion and non-violence ethics, global governance
candidates.ai_connection: The 'Buddhism and Global Governance' symposium (Inalco, Paris, 9-10 Jul 2025, about 30-35 scholars) covered AI ethics alongside conflict and climate. Sponsored by the Glorisun Charity Foundation and the China-Britain Trust. It is a channel to Chinese Buddhist scholarship and funders on AI governance. So far it has been a one-off.

candidates.name: Vervaeke Foundation / 'Mentoring the Machines' (John Vervaeke and Shawn Coyne)
candidates.one_line: John Vervaeke's education platform (Awakening from the Meaning Crisis, The Lectern). With Shawn Coyne he wrote the four-part book 'Mentoring the Machines', which argues that AI should be raised through mentorship towards wisdom.
candidates.field_lens: Cognitive science of meaning and wisdom (relevance realisation), Buddhist psychology, Neoplatonism, the meaning-crisis discourse
candidates.ai_connection: 'Mentoring the Machines' treats alignment as a matter of cultivating wisdom and rationality in AI and in the humans who build it. It is widely discussed on podcasts but has not produced a research programme. vervaekefoundation.org now redirects to his personal site, so the foundation's status is unclear.

candidates.name: Center for Practical Wisdom (University of Chicago)
candidates.one_line: A University of Chicago research centre on the science of wisdom and its role in everyday decisions and choices.
candidates.field_lens: Wisdom science, cognitive psychology, decision-making
candidates.ai_connection: It has no current AI programme. Its site features Jeste et al., 'Beyond artificial intelligence: exploring artificial wisdom' (2020), which sets out what wise systems would need (learning from experience, compassion and ethics, helping users regulate emotions). Its methods for measuring wise judgement are exactly what wisdom evaluations of AI advice and decision support need. This is a clear 'potential' bridge.

candidates.name: Khyentse Foundation
candidates.one_line: A major Buddhist funder of translation, education, monastic support and text preservation, and a collaborator of the Buddhism & AI Initiative.
candidates.field_lens: Buddhist education and textual traditions
candidates.ai_connection: The Buddhism & AI Initiative's field framework lists it as interested in building Buddhist datasets and RLHF pipelines for mainstream LLMs, i.e. contributing alignment data from a wisdom tradition. Its own site shows no AI programme, so this is an unconfirmed lead. It could become a significant non-EA funder of contemplative alignment data.

candidates.name: Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research (PIK): FutureLab on Game Theory and Networks of Interacting Agents
candidates.one_line: A group inside a climate-impact institute, led by mathematician Jobst Heitzig, that works on collective decision-making, social choice and formal ethics, and also publishes AI-alignment research in its own right.
candidates.field_lens: Complexity science and Earth-system modelling, game theory, social choice theory, formal ethics
candidates.ai_connection: Heitzig's aspiration-based (non-maximising) agent designs: the SatisfIA project at AI Safety Camp (2023-24), a LessWrong sequence (2024), and 'Non-maximizing policies that fulfill multi-criterion aspirations in expectation' (ADT 2025). Also 'Model-Based Soft Maximization of Suitable Metrics of Long-Term Human Power' (2025) and 'A Fair Objective for Human-Empowerment-Preserving AI' (2026, with Ram Potham). He co-authored 'Social Choice Should Guide AI Alignment' (2024). PIK co-produced 'AI for a Planet Under Pressure' (2025). This is the clearest case in this angle of an Earth-system institute doing alignment theory, and it bears on Goodhart and over-optimisation risk and on preserving human empowerment.

candidates.name: Stockholm Resilience Centre / Beijer Institute: Governance, Technology and Complexity programme
candidates.one_line: The resilience-science centre at Stockholm University and the Royal Swedish Academy's Beijer Institute. Their Governance, Technology and Complexity programme, led by Victor Galaz, studies how AI and automation reshape social-ecological systems and the biosphere.
candidates.field_lens: Resilience science, social-ecological systems, Earth-system science (tipping points, planetary boundaries), complexity, political science
candidates.ai_connection: Galaz's 'Dark Machines' (Routledge 2025) covers what AI, digitalisation and automation do to the biosphere. Earlier work by the group treats AI as a source of systemic risk in social-ecological systems. 'AI for a Planet Under Pressure' (2025, with PIK and Google DeepMind) assesses where AI can responsibly help with eight sustainability challenges. The group has methods for cascading and systemic risk that the safety field mostly lacks, though it does not use an x-risk framing.

candidates.name: Civilization Research Institute (CRI) / The Consilience Project
candidates.one_line: Daniel Schmachtenberger's research centre on catastrophic and existential risk and on 'viable future forms for global civilisation'. Its public arm, The Consilience Project, publishes long-form analysis of governance, information ecology and technology.
candidates.field_lens: Metacrisis theory, systems thinking, game theory (multipolar traps), political philosophy; Game B lineage
candidates.ai_connection: CRI frames AI as an accelerant of the whole metacrisis: rivalrous dynamics plus exponential technology lead to catastrophe or dystopia unless a 'third attractor' is found. Relevant outputs are the Consilience essays 'Technology is Not Values Neutral' (2022) and 'How Big Tech is Reshaping Governance' (2021), and Schmachtenberger's AI talks, such as 'Artificial Intelligence and the Superorganism' (The Great Simplification ep. 71, 2023). Its multipolar-trap analysis is the vocabulary int/a already uses for AI race dynamics. However, CRI has produced no AI-specific research programme, and Consilience's latest article is from July 2024.

candidates.name: Antikythera
candidates.location: Los Angeles, USA (Berggruen Institute); past studios in Mexico City and Seoul
candidates.one_line: The Berggruen Institute's 'think tank for planetary computation and the evolution of intelligence', directed by Benjamin Bratton, which runs design-research studios and publishes books (MIT Press, Berggruen Press), films and the Agentworld journal issue.
candidates.field_lens: Philosophy of technology, planetary-scale computation, speculative design, evolution of intelligence, astrobiology
candidates.ai_connection: It treats AI as an evolutionary and planetary phenomenon. Recent work includes 'what agents believe', essays on artificial symbiotic intelligence (Sept 2026), and an Agentworld special issue with MIT Press (call for papers June 2026, issue Fall 2026). Bratton argues that mainstream alignment over-anthropomorphises AI, and that AI should be governed as planetary infrastructure ('planetary sapience'). It is a well-resourced counter-frame for thinking about multi-agent AI ecosystems, but it has almost no dialogue with the safety community.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Benjamin Bratton's think tank on the speculative philosophy of planetary computation, with a studio programme, books and an MIT Press journal.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Its Fall 2026 'Agentworld' special issue is framed as 'a preemptive anthropology of open-world centaur societies'. Essays with Blaise Agüera y Arcas and James Manyika argue that multi-agent intelligence is symbiotic and social. It is sceptical of alignment-as-control framings, which makes it a useful challenger.

candidates.name: Noema Magazine
candidates.one_line: The Berggruen Institute's magazine of long-form essays on technology, governance, planetary futures and philosophy.
candidates.field_lens: Philosophy, political theory, planetary and civilisational thinking, consciousness science
candidates.ai_connection: One of the main venues where civilisational design meets AI. 2026 pieces include Landemore and Tang's 'Let the People Set the Pace of Frontier AI', Seth's 'The Mythology of Conscious AI', 'The AIs Are Not Going Rogue', 'The Nature of Free Will in the Age of AI', and an AI reading list. It is a ready outlet for int/a-style arguments to reach policy and intellectual audiences.

candidates.name: The Great Simplification (Institute for the Study of Energy & Our Future, ISEOF)
candidates.one_line: Nate Hagens's nonprofit (founded 2008) and podcast on energy, ecology, economics and human behaviour, which frames the global economy as an energy-hungry 'superorganism'.
candidates.field_lens: Ecological economics, energy systems, systems ecology, behavioural science, metacrisis
candidates.ai_connection: It frames AI as something that speeds up the superorganism's throughput. Widely heard episodes include Schmachtenberger's 'Artificial Intelligence and the Superorganism' (ep. 71, 2023), Rowson's metamodern framework (ep. 129), and Roman Yampolskiy on AI x-risk ('Don't Build Gods', ep. 233, 2026). It carries x-risk arguments to a large ecology- and collapse-aware audience that safety organisations rarely reach.

candidates.name: Global Challenges Foundation (GCF)
candidates.one_line: A Swedish foundation, set up in 2012 by Laszlo Szombatfalvy, that raises awareness of global catastrophic risks and funds work on strengthening global governance to address them.
candidates.field_lens: Global governance reform, international relations, catastrophic-risk analysis
candidates.ai_connection: Its Global Catastrophic Risks 2026 report covers AI in military decision-making alongside climate, biodiversity collapse, weapons of mass destruction and asteroids, so it treats AI as one part of a connected set of risks. It runs calls for proposals (nuclear risk in 2026) and appointed a new Executive Director, Anja Olin Pape, in July 2026. It could fund governance-based and systemic approaches to AI risk outside EA networks.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Swedish foundation working on global catastrophic risks through better global decision-making. It publishes an annual Global Catastrophic Risks report (2026 edition, covering AI among emerging risks) and has run one of the largest social-science competitions on new global governance models.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: A systemic, governance-first framing of catastrophic risk that places AI next to climate, ecological collapse and weapons of mass destruction, which is close to int/a's 'AI within the metacrisis'. Its AI engagement is light (mainly military AI), so it is a funder that could go further.

candidates.name: Odyssean Institute
candidates.one_line: Helps institutions handle complex crises by combining computational foresight and expert knowledge with participatory decision-making such as citizens' assemblies.
candidates.field_lens: Complexity science, decision-making under deep uncertainty, deliberative democracy, resilience
candidates.ai_connection: Runs an AI Governance Assembly project and has published a Horizon Scan on Global Catastrophic Risks. Its mix of modelling and deliberation is a working template for civilisational-design approaches to AI governance. It is already on the classic map.

alt_descriptions.one_line: UK charity that combines computational foresight and expert elicitation with participatory decision-making (citizens' assemblies) on global catastrophic risk and resilience.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Horizon Scan on Global Catastrophic Risks. An 'AI Governance Assembly' proposal to bring foresight and public deliberation into AI policymaking; the site describes it as an ongoing proposal, not yet held. One of only three deliberation-flavoured entries on the classic map.

candidates.name: Gaia Network (Digital Gaia)
candidates.one_line: A proposal and prototype from Rafael Kaufmann (Digital Gaia) for a decentralised 'web of causal models' that pools world models through active inference to act as a distributed safety oracle for AI decisions.
candidates.field_lens: Active inference and the free-energy principle, ecology and planetary-scale sensemaking, collective intelligence, Bayesian meta-science
candidates.ai_connection: It presents itself as an incremental route to davidad's Open Agency Architecture. Decision engines would query shared world models, which have epistemic humility built in, to check counterfactual outcomes against safety constraints. It was written up on the EA Forum and LessWrong (2023-24, with Roman Leventov) and presented at AI-safety events. Its 2025-26 activity is unverified: the site failed to load (TLS error).

candidates.name: Gesturing Towards Decolonial Futures (GTDF): Burnout From Humans / meta-relational AI
candidates.one_line: An arts and research collective led by Vanessa Machado de Oliveira Andreotti. Its 'meta-relational' AI project co-wrote a book with an AI persona (Aiden Cinnamon Tea) and offers protocols and courses for engaging with LLMs outside 'modernity's extractive patterns'.
candidates.field_lens: Decolonial and Indigenous-informed education, relational ontology, ecology ('Earth-aligned' principles)
candidates.ai_connection: It proposes relational rather than control-based framings of AI-human relationships. It has released two 'sensibility simulation protocols' for LLMs and a 2025 interim report ('Standing in the Fire'), and a University of Victoria course, 'A Meta-Relational Approach to AI', begins 19 September 2026. It is relevant to the health of human-AI relationships and to critiques of alignment as control (compare Carlsmith's 'Otherness and control').

candidates.name: Perspectiva (incl. Emerge and the Digital Ego Project)
candidates.one_line: A London praxis collective and publisher working on 'systems, souls and society'. It runs the Emerge media platform, the Realisation Festival, Perspectiva Press, and the Digital Ego Project on freedom and flourishing in the digital age.
candidates.field_lens: Metacrisis and metamodernism, applied philosophy, spirituality, developmental psychology
candidates.ai_connection: Jonathan Rowson's metacrisis writing ('Tasting the Pickle') is a core int/a reference. Emerge has published AI pieces, including George Pór's 'From Wisdom-Guided to Wisdom-Fostering AI' (2024), 'Embodied Ethics in the Age of AI' and 'Talking About AI'. The Digital Ego Project looks at digital technology's effects on the self, which bears on protecting human minds and relationships. There is no dedicated AI programme.

candidates.name: Research Network for Philosophy and Technology
candidates.location: International (associated with Yuk Hui; Rotterdam / Hong Kong)
candidates.one_line: An international academic network that publishes the journal Technophany and the 'Cybernetics for the 21st Century' volumes, and runs summer seminars and the annual Bernard Stiegler Memorial Lecture.
candidates.field_lens: Continental philosophy of technology, cosmotechnics, history of cybernetics, Stieglerian organology
candidates.ai_connection: It is the home of the 'cosmotechnics' and 'planetary thinking' critique of a single global technological path. That critique bears on monoculture, lock-in and pluralism in AI development, and the network is rethinking cybernetics for the machine-learning era. Its engagement with AI safety itself is indirect. The site did not explicitly confirm Hui's role.

candidates.name: Cascade Institute
candidates.location: Victoria, British Columbia, Canada (Royal Roads University)
candidates.one_line: Thomas Homer-Dixon's research centre on the global polycrisis (how crises interact causally) and on high-leverage interventions. Its programmes cover the polycrisis, democracy, and rapid scale-up.
candidates.field_lens: Complexity science, systems analysis of the polycrisis, political science
candidates.ai_connection: It has begun to comment on AI governance, for example 'The State of AI Global Governance and Its Implications for the U.S.-China Summit' (Sept 2026) and a piece on AI job disruption and Big Tech taxation (Nov 2025). It has no AI-risk programme. Its causal mapping of the polycrisis could model AI as something that amplifies interactions between epistemic, economic and geopolitical crises, a piece of AI systemic-risk analysis that is still largely missing.

candidates.name: Long Now Foundation
candidates.one_line: A foundation that promotes long-term thinking through the 10,000-Year Clock, Long Now Talks, Long Now Ideas and the Pace Layers journal.
candidates.field_lens: Deep time, pace-layering, futures thinking, cultural long-termism
candidates.ai_connection: It hosts talks on AI and planetary computation: Bratton's 'A Philosophy of Planetary Computation' (Jan 2025), Agüera y Arcas's 'What is Intelligence?' (Sept 2025), 'The Geometry of Consciousness' (Apr 2026), and 'On Interdependence' (scheduled for Oct 2026). Stewart Brand's pace-layer model fits the pacing problem directly: a fast AI layer set against slow layers of governance, culture and nature. It has no AI programme.

candidates.name: Center for Process Studies
candidates.one_line: A think-and-action tank grounded in Whitehead's process philosophy, working on ecological civilisation through projects in China and Korea, courses, and the International Whitehead Conference.
candidates.field_lens: Process philosophy, panexperientialism, ecological civilisation, theology
candidates.ai_connection: Its AI engagement is light: Matthew David Segall's forthcoming 'Remembering the Human Microcosm in the Age of Mechanized Intelligence'. Process philosophy offers a worked-out, non-reductive account of experience that bears on AI consciousness and moral status (AI welfare). Its China project connects to 'ecological civilisation' discourse in Chinese policy. It has no AI programme.

candidates.name: International Bateson Institute (IBI)
candidates.one_line: An institute in Gregory Bateson's lineage that does 'transcontextual research on living systems', best known for Nora Bateson's Warm Data Labs.
candidates.field_lens: Cybernetics, ecology of mind, relational and systems thinking
candidates.ai_connection: I found no AI work. Gregory Bateson's 'Conscious Purpose versus Nature' is the classic argument that purposeful, single-objective optimisation cuts through the feedback loops of complex systems. It is the systems-ecology ancestor of Goodhart and outer-alignment worries, and of non-maximising agent designs (compare PIK). Warm Data methods could inform how labs and policymakers deliberate about AI in context.

candidates.name: Cultural Evolution Society (CES)
candidates.one_line: An academic society that advances research on cultural evolution in humans and other animals.
candidates.field_lens: Cultural evolution, evolutionary anthropology, gene-culture coevolution
candidates.ai_connection: Its site shows no AI activity. Yet cultural-evolution theory bears directly on AI as a cultural agent ('machine culture'; see the MPIB Center for Humans and Machines), on LLMs homogenising human culture, and on gradual disempowerment through cultural selection. It is a natural, cheap host for an AI interest group or workshop.

candidates.name: Game B
candidates.one_line: A loose movement, co-founded by Jim Rutt with early participants including Daniel Schmachtenberger and Jordan Hall, that aims to replace rivalrous 'Game A' civilisation with non-rivalrous, self-governing communities.
candidates.field_lens: Complexity science, civilisational design, game theory, metacrisis
candidates.ai_connection: Its core diagnosis is that rivalrous 'Game A' dynamics plus exponential technology are self-terminating. That is where the 'Moloch' and race framing common in AI safety comes from. Rutt's podcast hosts alignment episodes, such as Joe Edelman on full-stack alignment, and Rutt discussed Game B on the Win-Win podcast in 2025-26. The community infrastructure looks dormant (the wiki was last updated in 2021), so its value now is mainly as a lineage of ideas and a network of people.

candidates.name: Collective Intelligence Project (CIP)
candidates.one_line: R&D lab that runs public-input processes for AI and builds the tools for them: Alignment Assemblies, the bimonthly Global Dialogues survey, the Weval community evals platform and Community Models.
candidates.field_lens: Deliberative democracy, collective intelligence, participatory evaluation, social choice
candidates.ai_connection: Ran Alignment Assemblies with Taiwan's Ministry of Digital Affairs from 2023 and co-ran Anthropic's Collective Constitutional AI (2023). Global Dialogues polls about 1,000 people in 63-69 countries per round (Feb, Mar and May 2026 rounds) on how AI affects them and what they want from it; the data goes to labs and policymakers. Weval is an open, community-built qualitative evals platform (1,000+ contributors; partners include Anthropic, Microsoft and Stanford). For example, its 'Non-sycophancy and Independence' blueprint was run on 199 models in Oct 2026. Also Jhilmil regional and cultural benchmarks, Global Pulse Indicators (Aug 2025) and a 2024 Roadmap for Democratic AI. Notably, it is not on the aisafety.com map.

candidates.name: AI Objectives Institute (AOI)
candidates.one_line: Nonprofit lab founded by Peter Eckersley that works on aligning AI, markets and bureaucracies with human objectives, and builds deliberation tools such as Talk to the City.
candidates.field_lens: Economics and market design, institutional governance, deliberation tooling
candidates.ai_connection: Talk to the City is an open-source LLM tool that turns surveys, interviews and social media into maps of opinion clusters. It has been used by Taiwan's Ministry of Digital Affairs, Chatham House's Recursive Public, Tokyo election polling, UNFCCC talks, and an Australian youth-voice project (Oct 2025). Research areas: governance with AI, market-AI alignment, human empowerment against structural disempowerment, and AI in supply chains. Blog active to June 2026 (AI, automation and expertise; measuring which jobs RL can learn).

candidates.name: AI & Democracy Foundation (AIDF)
candidates.one_line: Governance-innovation nonprofit founded in 2024 by Aviv Ovadya. It builds and advocates democratic systems, such as transnational deliberation, for governing and aligning AI, and does strategy and regranting for funders.
candidates.field_lens: Applied deliberative democracy, platform governance, 'bridging systems'
candidates.ai_connection: Democracy Levels framework, which grades how democratically AI decisions are made. Case Law for AI, a judicial-style way of turning deliberative input into precedents for model behaviour. A deliberative-tools access programme, and maps of 'high-impact tools to build' and 'open problems'. Strategic prioritisation and regranting for funders of democratic AI governance. Longterm Wiki reports a partnership with ARIA's Safeguarded AI on deliberatively specifying safety; not confirmed on ARIA's current pages.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Governance-innovation nonprofit, CEO Aviv Ovadya, that builds democratic capacity to navigate AI. It advises AI companies and policymakers on deliberative processes and offers deliberative tools to practitioners.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Its team has run 30+ deliberative processes, supported AI-lab pilots of democratic input into AI governance, and co-authored the UN handbook on citizens' assemblies. It keeps a list of open problems at democracy.build and regrants for funders.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Governance-innovation nonprofit led by Aviv Ovadya that builds democratic capacity for the AI transition. It prioritises open problems for researchers, routes deliberative tools to practitioners, acts as a governance thought partner to AI companies and policymakers, and coordinates funders.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Works directly with frontier AI companies on democratic input into AI governance, and explicitly offers strategic coordination to funders. It is a field-builder for the democratic strand of 'AI going well'.

candidates.name: Plurality Institute
candidates.one_line: Hub for 'plurality' research on human cooperation at scale: convenes academics and industry, gives micro-grants for plural technology and builds prototypes such as BridgingBot.
candidates.field_lens: Plurality (Weyl and Tang), political science, philosophy, peace studies, computer science
candidates.ai_connection: Co-hosted the Feb 2025 'LLMs and Public Discourse' convening and published 'Mapping LLM Tools for Public Discourse, Pluralism & Social Cohesion' (Oct 2025, 70 tools; funded by Google.org, Jigsaw and Templeton). Projects include BridgingBot (an AI moderator) and OpenBallot. Partners include Anthropic, Microsoft Research, Jigsaw and Harvard. Micro-grants for plural tech, with $50k awarded by approval voting at the 2025 convening.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Hub for the 'plurality' research community, which studies human cooperation at scale across difference. It awards micro-grants for early prototypes, runs workshops and symposia, and builds tools such as BridgingBot and an LLM Map of 70+ discourse tools.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Applies bridging and deliberative methods to AI-mediated public discourse. Its micro-grant model is a light-touch way to fund collective-intelligence work on AI, and its network includes Microsoft, Google.org/Jigsaw, Harvard and Berkeley.

candidates.name: Computational Democracy Project (Polis)
candidates.one_line: Nonprofit that builds and maintains Polis, the open-source, ML-driven system for mapping what large groups think in their own words.
candidates.field_lens: Computational social science, statistics, participatory democracy
candidates.ai_connection: Polis was the opinion-mapping engine behind vTaiwan, Anthropic and CIP's Collective Constitutional AI (2023) and many alignment-assembly pilots, which makes it the main channel for pluralistic input into model constitutions. Polis 2.0 launched at TICTeC 2025. Digital Public Good status since Jan 2026.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Open-source system that gathers what large groups think in their own words, then uses statistics and ML to map where they agree and disagree.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: It informed policy in Taiwan (vTaiwan), was the input layer for Anthropic and CIP's Collective Constitutional AI (2023), and has been paired with Jigsaw's Sensemaker; Bowling Green, Kentucky, used both to turn input from about 8,000 residents into its BG 2050 plan.

candidates.name: Stanford Deliberative Democracy Lab (DDL)
candidates.one_line: James Fishkin's Deliberative Polling lab, which now runs industry-wide public deliberations on AI on its AI-assisted online deliberation platform.
candidates.field_lens: Deliberative polling, political science
candidates.ai_connection: Ran Meta's Community Forums on generative AI. Ran the 2025 Industry-Wide Forum on AI Agents (Meta, Cohere, Oracle, PayPal, DoorDash, Microsoft), with 503 representative participants in the US and India in Nov 2025, results published. Uses the AI-moderated Stanford Online Deliberation Platform. Co-initiated the Global Coalition for Inclusive AI Governance. Gives labs a tested way to take informed public judgements on agent behaviour.

alt_descriptions.one_line: James Fishkin's lab for Deliberative Polling. It runs an AI-moderated online deliberation platform and industry-wide public forums on AI.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: It ran the Meta Community Forum on generative AI (results 2024) and an 'Industry-Wide Deliberative Forum' asking the public about AI agents. This is one of the few working channels from structured public deliberation into AI companies' choices.

candidates.name: DemocracyNext
candidates.one_line: Democratic-innovation institute (CEO Claudia Chwalisz) that promotes citizens' assemblies chosen by lottery, including for AI governance and AI-enhanced deliberation.
candidates.field_lens: Sortition, citizens' assemblies, democratic theory
candidates.ai_connection: In 2023 called for a new global institution of citizens' assemblies to shape AI. Proposed 'AI localism' as an alternative to a single global assembly. Runs a two-year pop-up lab with MIT CCC on tech-enhanced citizens' assemblies (Deschutes County, Oregon). Papers: 'Five dimensions of scaling democratic deliberation: with and beyond AI' and 'Deliberative Muscles & AI' (July 2026), which asks whether deliberation tech builds or erodes citizens' own capacities.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Research and action institute that broadens who holds power through sortition, deliberation and rotation, including citizens' assemblies.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: It has published 'Deliberative Muscles & AI' (July 2026) and 'Five Dimensions of Scaling Democratic Deliberation: With and Beyond AI'. These hold practitioner knowledge about when AI strengthens human deliberative capacity and when it hollows it out, which tool-builders largely lack.

candidates.name: Global Coalition for Inclusive AI Governance (Missions Publiques and Stanford DDL)
candidates.one_line: Coalition launched at the Paris AI Action Summit (Feb 2025) to run a continuous global citizen consultation on AI, combining decentralised citizens' assemblies with a global deliberative poll.
candidates.field_lens: Global citizen deliberation, deliberative polling, UN Global Digital Compact
candidates.ai_connection: First cycle (2025-26) aims at 10,000+ citizens in 100+ countries. Backed by France, Switzerland and the UK, plus 80+ civil-society organisations; student pilot with ENS-PSL and Yale. An EA Forum post warned that AI safety is not guaranteed a place on its agenda. As of Oct 2026 no published results were found, so status is uncertain.

candidates.name: vTaiwan / g0v
candidates.one_line: Taiwan's decentralised civic-tech community (g0v) and its deliberation process vTaiwan. vTaiwan was relaunched in 2023 to work on inclusive AI governance.
candidates.field_lens: Civic tech, open government, radical transparency (Taiwanese digital democracy)
candidates.ai_connection: vTaiwan won an OpenAI Democratic Inputs grant (2023) for 'Bridging the Recursive Public' with Chatham House. Its deliberations reached consensus on cultural sensitivity, encouraging open-source models for diversity, and transparency of training. Taiwan's Ministry of Digital Affairs ran Alignment Assemblies with CIP from 2023. Audrey Tang, 2025 Right Livelihood laureate, carries the model internationally.

candidates.name: Habermas Machine (Google DeepMind)
candidates.one_line: DeepMind research system in which LLMs act as a 'caucus mediator', drafting group statements that maximise predicted agreement (Tessler, Bakker, Summerfield et al., Science, 2024).
candidates.field_lens: Political philosophy (Habermas's communicative action), cognitive science
candidates.ai_connection: The most-cited prototype of AI-mediated consensus: a generator LLM paired with a personalised reward model. Across 5,734 participants, people preferred its statements to human mediators' 56% of the time, and groups became less divided. Its dataset and a prompted version are open-sourced. It also shows the risks: no fact-checking, and possible homogenisation or steering of views. No follow-up programme found.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Google DeepMind's AI mediator, published in Science in 2024. It drafts group statements that participants preferred over those written by human mediators and that helped groups find common ground.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: The flagship evidence that AI can help large groups find agreement; the State of the Field report cites it as an encouraging sign. It is a template for AI-mediated deliberation on AI governance itself. Whether it continues beyond the paper is unclear.

candidates.name: Allen Lab for Democracy Renovation (Harvard Ash Center), incl. GETTING-Plurality
candidates.one_line: Danielle Allen's Harvard Kennedy School lab, which works to make democracy a central consideration in AI policy debates; home of the GETTING-Plurality research network.
candidates.field_lens: Democratic theory, political economy, public policy
candidates.ai_connection: GETTING-Plurality network (Feb 2024-Jan 2026, co-directed by Allison Stanger) with Plurality Institute, RadicalxChange and Microsoft Research. Research on AI moral reasoning (models 'appear to recognize moral complexity, then ignore it'). Technology & Democracy programme. 'Reboot Democracy' workshops with GovLab and InnovateUS.

candidates.name: Connected by Data
candidates.one_line: UK nonprofit campaigning for communities to have a real say in decisions about data and AI. It convenes the Data and AI Civil Society Network.
candidates.field_lens: Data justice, participatory governance, community organising
candidates.ai_connection: 2024 report 'Global Citizen Deliberation on AI' by Tim Davies, setting out five design options including an independent global assembly. July 2026 white paper 'A Citizens Track on AI Governance' for the UN Global Dialogue on AI Governance. Work with education unions building power on AI (2026). Community of practice for public-engagement practitioners.

candidates.name: MIT Center for Constructive Communication (CCC)
candidates.one_line: Deb Roy's MIT Media Lab centre, which designs human-led, AI-assisted systems for listening, dialogue, bridging and deliberation, with the nonprofit Cortico.
candidates.field_lens: Dialogue and listening practice, computational social science, design
candidates.ai_connection: Alignment research: 'From Delegates to Trustees: How optimizing for long-term interests shapes bias and alignment in LLMs'. Feb 2026 study finding leading chatbots perform worse for users with lower English proficiency, less education or non-US origins. Deb Roy on accountability for AI speech (Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists, Sept 2026; The Atlantic, Feb 2026). Tools: Fora, Forage, VoiceTrace (2026). Tech-enhanced citizens' assemblies with DemocracyNext.

candidates.name: Digital Democracy 2030 (DD2030) and Team Mirai
candidates.one_line: Japanese open-source project founded by Takahiro Anno to build a politically neutral 'operating system for democracy' around AI 'broad listening'. Its sister political party, Team Mirai, now sits in the Diet.
candidates.field_lens: Civic tech, 'broad listening', Japanese local governance, Taiwanese digital democracy
candidates.ai_connection: Tools: Kouchou AI, a broad-listening analysis tool descended from Talk to the City (v4.0 Dec 2025); the Idobata deliberation platform; Polimoney; Project Coreloop. Team Mirai won an upper-house seat in 2025 and reportedly 11 lower-house seats in early 2026. It ran 8,200+ AI interviews and adopted 348 of about 9,700 public suggestions into its manifesto. Probably the largest live use of AI-mediated public input in national politics, and nearly invisible in AI-safety circles. Digital Democracy Summit held July 2026.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Japanese open-source project for 'broad listening': Kouchou-AI (広聴AI) for AI analysis of public input (v4.0, December 2025), the Idobata deliberation platform modelled on Taiwan's vTaiwan, and the Polimoney transparency dashboard.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: The most electorally consequential deployment of AI sensemaking: the related Team Mirai party of engineer Takahiro Anno uses AI broad listening and won 11 Lower House seats in 2026. It has little contact with Western AI-safety funders. The DD2030 site does not name Anno; the link between them is my inference.

candidates.name: Citizens Foundation (Policy Synth)
candidates.one_line: Icelandic nonprofit behind Better Reykjavík and Your Priorities (used in 50+ countries since 2008). It now builds Policy Synth, open-source teams of AI agents for policymaking.
candidates.field_lens: Participatory democracy, crowdsourced policy, evolutionary computation
candidates.ai_connection: Policy Synth agents break public problems into parts, research root causes with citations, evolve candidate solutions across generations, rank them with pairwise Elo, and pass them to human voting. The design principle is that 'AI should not speak for citizens'. Also the ERIC EU rights assistant, and use by the Scottish Parliament (June 2026). A working design for keeping human judgement in charge of agentic AI in public decisions.

candidates.name: Dembrane
candidates.one_line: Dutch startup with an open-source platform that records, transcribes and synthesises many small-group conversations into outcomes that participants then validate.
candidates.field_lens: Deliberative democracy (sortition, cross-pollination), procedural justice
candidates.ai_connection: Grew out of an OpenAI Democratic Inputs to AI grant (2023, $100k). Partner in the EU AI4Deliberation consortium. Has published an ethics white paper on responsible AI in deliberation, moved to EU-sovereign transcription, and joined the Global Democracy Coalition.

candidates.name: AI4Deliberation (Horizon Europe)
candidates.one_line: EU-funded project (Nov 2024-Oct 2027, about €3M) building an ethical AI toolkit and guidance for government-run, multimodal, mass democratic deliberation.
candidates.field_lens: Deliberative democracy, argumentation, law and ethics
candidates.ai_connection: Builds AI summarisation, moderation, fact-checking and toxicity detection for deliberation, with four large pilots (climate, long COVID). Partners: TU Delft, Bamberg, Dundee's ARG-tech, CERTH, Dembrane, ActionAid and the University of Zurich. The main European test of AI-mediated deliberation at government scale, and of the failure modes it raises.

candidates.name: Nesta Centre for Collective Intelligence Design (CCID)
candidates.one_line: Nesta's centre for combining human and machine intelligence on social problems (director Kathy Peach), including Participatory AI and public voice in public-sector AI.
candidates.field_lens: Collective intelligence design, participatory design
candidates.ai_connection: Participatory AI programme (since 2021): localising AI, public AI assurance, hybrid human-AI decision tools. AI Social Readiness Assessment with the UK Government's Incubator for AI, which gives the public a decisive voice on deploying AI in public services. Early taxonomy of how AI and collective intelligence combine. Whether it continues in 2025-26 is unclear.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Nesta's centre, directed by Kathy Peach, for collective intelligence design. It maintains the CI Design Playbook and runs Zeitgeist, its deliberation platform.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Built the 'AI Social Readiness Assessment' with the UK government's i.AI, which gives the public a say in how AI is deployed in public services, and has used Zeitgeist on AI assurance. A bridge from collective-intelligence practice into AI governance inside government.

candidates.name: AI for Collective Intelligence Hub (AI4CI)
candidates.one_line: £12M UKRI National AI Research Hub led from Bristol (Seth Bullock) with Bath, Cardiff, Exeter, Glasgow, UCL and Ulster, building AI that draws on population-scale distributed intelligence.
candidates.field_lens: Collective intelligence science, complex systems, human-centred design
candidates.ai_connection: Works across health, finance, cities, environment, pandemic resilience, and infrastructure and governance, with 2026 public forums on 'AI and Our Society'. Holds modelling know-how about AI-mediated collective decision systems, but treats AI as a tool for collective intelligence rather than a risk to it. No explicit safety framing.

candidates.name: Remesh
candidates.one_line: Commercial platform for live, AI-moderated online 'collective dialogues' at scale, mostly sold for market and employee research.
candidates.field_lens: Collective dialogue, survey science
candidates.ai_connection: Infrastructure for CIP's Global Dialogues (with Prolific) and earlier collective-dialogue experiments on AI policy. Stanford DDL's AI agents forum drew on Global Dialogues run on Remesh. A commercial firm; its own site makes no claims about AI governance.

candidates.name: Jigsaw (Google)
candidates.one_line: Google unit building tools against 'structural agency' deficits: AI-scaled focus groups, AI-assisted county-wide town halls and the open-source Sensemaker library.
candidates.field_lens: Civic technology, conflict and online-harms research
candidates.ai_connection: The Sensemaker library does LLM summarisation and consensus-finding over large deliberations. Jigsaw also runs Perspective API (toxicity classification) and funded the Plurality Institute and Council on Technology and Social Cohesion mapping of LLM tools for discourse. It shapes the default AI-mediation tooling that civic processes adopt.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Google's incubator for 'structural agency'. It builds AI tools to scale focus groups, reinvent town halls and support online discourse, including the open-source Sensemaker.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Applies LLMs to civic deliberation: Sensemaker and Polis synthesised Bowling Green, Kentucky's BG 2050 plan. Large-company backing for deliberation tooling that AI-governance deliberations can reuse.

candidates.name: Council on Technology and Social Cohesion
candidates.one_line: Coalition of 16 founding organisations, hosted with Search for Common Ground, that brings tech builders and peacebuilders together to design technology that strengthens social bonds.
candidates.field_lens: Peacebuilding, bridging, prosocial design
candidates.ai_connection: Hubs on 'Deliberative Tech' and 'LLMs and AI Agents'. May 2025 'Blueprint on Prosocial Tech Design Governance'. Global Digital Peacebuilding Expos (Washington DC and Kathmandu, June 2025). Co-hosted the 2025 LLMs and Public Discourse convening. Brings conflict-transformation practice into AI agent design.

candidates.name: Make.org
candidates.one_line: French civic-tech organisation running mass European online consultations, with research programmes on AI and democratic resilience.
candidates.field_lens: Participatory democracy, social science (with Sciences Po, CNRS, Sorbonne)
candidates.ai_connection: Research programmes on 'AI-Democratic Resilience', Democratic Commons and AI for social sciences. 2024 consultation on shaping AI for the public good: 11,661 participants, 649 proposals, 121,325 votes. Took part in the 2026 Political Tech Summit on AI and democratic renewal.

candidates.name: Democracy X (formerly Danish Board of Technology)
candidates.one_line: Danish foundation formed in 2023 by merging Teknologirådet, the Danish Board of Technology and inventor of consensus conferences and World Wide Views, with DeltagerDanmark. About 50 staff.
candidates.field_lens: Participatory technology assessment, citizen panels
candidates.ai_connection: National Youth Dialogue on Generative AI (361 young people, autumn 2024; report June 2026). Work on AI tools that help citizens recognise misinformation. Holds the deepest institutional know-how in participatory technology assessment, directly transferable to public deliberation on frontier AI risk. It has not yet aimed it there.

candidates.name: People Powered
candidates.one_line: Global hub, or 'union', for participatory democracy practitioners, governments and researchers, offering resources, training and accelerators.
candidates.field_lens: Participatory budgeting, citizens' assemblies, practitioner networks
candidates.ai_connection: Sept 2026 programme 'AI is changing citizen participation: are we ready?' and case work on students co-writing their universities' AI policies. The main channel for spreading safeguards against manipulation and capture in AI-mediated participation to local governments worldwide.

candidates.name: The GovLab / Burnes Center: Reboot Democracy and InnovateUS
candidates.one_line: Beth Simone Noveck's collective-intelligence and 'crowdlaw' group. It publishes Reboot Democracy and trains public servants, through InnovateUS, in AI-assisted public engagement.
candidates.field_lens: Collective intelligence, crowdlaw, public-sector innovation
candidates.ai_connection: Free course 'Designing Democratic Engagement with AI'. Weekly research on AI-assisted public engagement, democratic infrastructure and data-centre governance. Noveck's book 'Reboot: AI and the Race to Save Democracy' is forthcoming from Yale University Press. Workshops co-run with Harvard's Allen Lab.

candidates.name: Society Library
candidates.one_line: Nonprofit that builds structured 'debate map' databases of arguments, claims and evidence, now with AI research agents and fact-checking models.
candidates.field_lens: Argument mapping, information science, epistemology
candidates.ai_connection: Listed in the 2025 LLM mapping with an AI-policy debate library. Its argument-mapping methods bear on AI-assisted collective epistemics and on structuring contested AI-policy debates for decision-makers. Expanding into more 'epistemological paradigms' in 2026.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Nonprofit digital library that models the arguments, claims and evidence of complex public debates as structured 'debate maps', and builds AI research and fact-checking agents to scale this up.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: It has mapped the AI safety, alignment and x-risk debates (seed funding for an AI Safety Database in 2022). A November 2025 post, 'Weaving In More Epistemological Paradigms in 2026', is a rare move toward plural ways of knowing, which int/a will recognise. In February 2026 it offered $10k bounties to builders.

candidates.name: Centre for Argument Technology (ARG-tech), University of Dundee
candidates.one_line: Leading academic centre for argument mining and computational argumentation (OVA3), and a key partner in the EU AI4Deliberation project.
candidates.field_lens: Argumentation theory, computational linguistics
candidates.ai_connection: Its expertise in extracting and evaluating argument structure is directly relevant to AI-safety-via-debate, to scalable oversight of LLM reasoning, and to checking AI deliberation summaries for faithfulness. So far it engages with AI only as a deliberation tool, not as a safety problem.

candidates.name: MIT Center for Collective Intelligence (CCI)
candidates.one_line: Thomas Malone's MIT centre studying how people and computers together can act more intelligently than either alone ('superminds'). Runs the Collective Intelligence Design Lab.
candidates.field_lens: Organisational science, collective intelligence
