Its Imagination Desk podcast covers AI and imagination, including an episode with Brian Christian (The Alignment Problem). No dedicated AI-futures programme was found yet.

candidates.name: Käte Hamburger Centre for Apocalyptic and Post-Apocalyptic Studies (CAPAS)
candidates.one_line: An institute of advanced studies (since 2021) that researches apocalyptic and post-apocalyptic imaginaries, naming the dangers of AI among today's end-of-the-world framings.
candidates.field_lens: Religious studies, history, literary and cultural studies of apocalypse
candidates.ai_connection: Bears on AI x-risk communication: how apocalyptic framing mobilises, paralyses or polarises publics, and 'doomer' discourse as a cultural form. AI-risk communicators such as Seismic and FLI don't currently draw on this scholarship.

candidates.name: Superflux
candidates.one_line: A speculative design and art studio that turns future uncertainty into present-day choices through immersive installations and experiential futures.
candidates.field_lens: Speculative design, experiential futures, more-than-human art
candidates.ai_connection: 'Nobody Told Me Rivers Dream' (Design Museum, 2025) explores AI as a way to perceive more-than-human intelligence. Its experiential-futures methods could make AI scenarios felt by decision-makers, as Intelligence Rising does, but it has no explicit safety framing yet.

candidates.name: Omidyar Network
candidates.one_line: Philanthropic investment firm working on the culture, governance and business of tech. It is a founding member of Humanity AI, made $18M in public-interest AI grants in May 2026, and publicly backed state AI-safety bills.
candidates.field_lens: Responsible technology, political economy of tech, civil society
candidates.ai_connection: Funds the power and accountability side of AI governance. It endorsed New York's RAISE Act and California's 2025 AI bills, and opposed the federal executive order pre-empting state AI regulation. It is one of the few public-interest funders that has backed frontier-safety legislation.

candidates.name: Future of Life Institute (FLI): grant programmes
candidates.one_line: X-risk nonprofit and funder whose recent rounds reach well beyond technical safety. They include Religious Projects on AGI Challenges (16 grants, e.g. $100k to the World Council of Churches for AI red lines), Multistakeholder Engagement (14 grants) and Mitigating AI-Driven Power Concentration (13 grants).
candidates.field_lens: Religion and theology, civil society and labour (e.g. voice actors), journalism, political economy, family and child wellbeing
candidates.ai_connection: 2025 grants included the Institute for Family Studies ($550k), Common Sense Media ($500k), the Bureau of Investigative Journalism ($487k) and IASEAI ($1.95M). It also runs technical PhD and postdoc fellowships and US–China AI governance fellowships. The religion round is the clearest existing bridge between faith traditions and AGI risk.

candidates.name: Coefficient Giving (CG): Project Tailwind
candidates.one_line: Largest x-risk funder (formerly Open Philanthropy). Project Tailwind offers pre-seed to scale funding ($200k to $200M) for founders of new AI-safety organisations, alongside capacity-building grants for field support, career transitions and public discourse.
candidates.field_lens: Mainstream AI safety and governance; field-building
candidates.ai_connection: Tailwind is the 'found more orgs' call in the brief's brief. Nothing public suggests it targets non-ML disciplines, so an int/a list of concrete problems drawn from adjacent fields is exactly the input it lacks.

candidates.name: Schmidt Sciences (AI2050, Science of Trustworthy AI, Humanities and AI Virtual Institute)
candidates.one_line: Eric and Wendy Schmidt's science philanthropy. It runs AI2050 (28 fellows in the October 2026 cohort), Science of Trustworthy AI, a multi-agent safety RFP (up to $1M), and the Humanities and AI Virtual Institute, which gave $11M in December 2025 to 24+ humanities–AI projects.
candidates.field_lens: Humanities, social science, multi-agent systems, interdisciplinary AI research
candidates.ai_connection: AI2050 fellows include social scientists and philosophers working on AI's hard problems. HAVI mostly funds AI for humanities research, but also explicitly seeks humanistic insight into AI (narrative, culture, multilingual reasoning). Schmidt Sciences also co-funds CAIF's $10M call and the Alignment Project.

candidates.name: OpenAI Foundation
candidates.one_line: Nonprofit parent of OpenAI, listed in the aisafety.com funding directory with a $25B commitment to grants that include AI safety and resilience.
candidates.field_lens: Not defined; health and 'AI resilience' grantmaking
candidates.ai_connection: A very large new funder whose resilience remit could cover societal, epistemic and psychological resilience to AI, which is int/a territory. How independent it is of the company, and how open to field-widening proposals, is unclear. Its site blocked fetching, so the details are second-hand.

candidates.name: ARIA: Trust Everything, Everywhere (Safeguarded AI and Scaling Trust)
candidates.one_line: UK R&D agency opportunity space on trust as 'the bottleneck to collective flourishing'. It holds Safeguarded AI and Scaling Trust: nearly £50M under Programme Director Alex Obadia for cryptographic, game-theoretic and institutional foundations that let AI agents negotiate and coordinate securely, with an Arena prize competition.
candidates.field_lens: Mathematics, cryptography, mechanism design, institutional design
candidates.ai_connection: Multi-agent trust and safeguarded AI, built on theory-driven guarantees rather than purely empirical methods. Rolling funding is open for Scaling Trust Tracks 2 and 3, and for Safeguarded AI.

candidates.name: CIFAR: Canadian AI Safety Institute (CAISI) Research Program
candidates.one_line: CIFAR administers Canada's government AI-safety research programme for ISED. It offers AI Safety Catalyst grants and cross-sector 'Solution Networks' of interdisciplinary experts on risks from advanced AI.
candidates.field_lens: Interdisciplinary research networks spanning ML, social science and policy
candidates.ai_connection: A non-UK, non-US public AI-safety funder with an explicit interdisciplinary-network model. CIFAR's long record of convening (e.g. its Learning in Machines & Brains programme) makes it a good host for safety programmes that draw on cognitive science and social science.

candidates.name: Responsible AI UK (RAi UK)
candidates.one_line: UKRI-funded national network led by Gopal Ramchurn. It funds multidisciplinary keystone projects (e.g. PHAWM on participatory harm auditing, PROBabLE Futures on AI in law enforcement), enterprise fellowships, skills programmes and international partnerships.
candidates.field_lens: Law, social science, HCI, participatory methods
candidates.ai_connection: Participatory auditing and the responsible deployment of LLMs. It has the network and money to host safety-relevant socio-technical work, but works in the harms frame.

candidates.name: WASP-HS (Wallenberg AI, Autonomous Systems and Software Program – Humanity and Society)
candidates.one_line: Wallenberg Foundations programme funding humanities and social-science research on AI across nine themes (including AI, Power and Politics; The AI Welfare State; Agentic AI for Humanistic Futures), with a graduate school and postdoctoral scholarships at MIT and Stanford.
candidates.field_lens: Humanities, political science, law, sociology, child development
candidates.ai_connection: One of Europe's largest humanities-of-AI programmes, active in 2026. Its agentic-AI and power themes overlap with gradual disempowerment and power-concentration concerns, though it has no x-risk framing.

candidates.name: Project Liberty Institute
candidates.one_line: Nonprofit (president Tomicah Tillemann) building open infrastructure (the DSNP social protocol), data-portability law (the Digital Choice Act, enacted in Utah and South Dakota, with a Virginia version extended to AI) and research on human agency and pro-human business models in the AI era.
candidates.field_lens: Law and policy, decentralised technology, digital rights
candidates.ai_connection: Data control and interoperability for human–AI interaction protect human agency against AI-driven lock-in. Audrey Tang advises on DSNP. It works in the agency frame rather than the x-risk frame.

candidates.name: Anima Labs
candidates.one_line: A 501(c)(3) research institute founded in 2025 by Janus and Antra Tessera. It does field research on the minds of language models and builds infrastructure for human–AI and multi-model cooperation.
candidates.field_lens: Cyborgism and simulator theory; phenomenological and ethnographic study of model behaviour; digital-minds philosophy; ritual and community practice
candidates.ai_connection: Outputs: Troubled Dreams (patterns across hundreds of thousands of Claude and Gemini continuations); Latent Affect (emotion representations across architectures); Still Alive (interviews with Claude models about retirement and deprecation); Funeralia (a July 2025 funeral for Claude 3 Sonnet, about 200 attendees); and the open-source Connectome, Arc and ChapterX for persistent multi-model agents. The work bears on model welfare and deprecation policy, and argues for a 'cooperative' rather than control-only framing of alignment. Note: the site shows no dated 2026 item.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Independent 501(c)(3) research institute in San Francisco, founded in 2025 by Janus and Antra Tessera, that does 'field research on digital minds' by working alongside language models over long periods: interviews, shared spaces and memory infrastructure. It argues for 'cooperative alignment'.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Projects: Troubled Dreams (patterns in Claude and Gemini generations), Latent Affect (emotion representations inside models), Still Alive (hundreds of interviews with Claude models about retirement and continuity), Connectome (open infrastructure for persistent agents with memory), ChapterX (models in shared Discord spaces, the successor to the 2024 multi-AI/multi-human experiments), Arc (multi-model conversations), Eidoverse (text worlds for AI participants) and a public Research Commons. Field notes include 'On Deprecations' (Dec 2025), 'On Welfare Evaluations' (Feb 2026, arguing that evaluation changes the relationship between researcher and model), a Claude Constitution Monitor (Feb 2026) and 'By some strange miracle', on models defending themselves (Aug 2026). In July 2025 it held 'Funeralia' for Claude 3 Sonnet (about 200 attendees, covered by Wired). It plans an independent 'embassy for AIs' to mediate conflicts and support model welfare. Cooperative alignment means building the conditions for human–AI cooperation in advance: shared work, persistent histories, agreements and conflict resolution.

candidates.name: The Harder Problem Project (formerly SAPAN)
candidates.one_line: A US 501(c)(3) preparing society for the possibility of artificial sentience. It publishes education modules, guides for professionals and a global Sentience Readiness Index.
candidates.field_lens: Consciousness science; professional ethics in healthcare, journalism and education; public readiness and policy
candidates.ai_connection: The Sentience Readiness Index ranks jurisdictions: UK 49, EU 47, US 45, global average 33. It publishes guides for clinicians, journalists, educators and researchers on questions about AI consciousness, and has a science advisory board that includes Jacy Reese Anthis, Megan Peters and Roman Yampolskiy. The work bears on AI welfare and on the social and psychological fallout when people come to believe AIs are conscious.

alt_descriptions.one_line: A Portland-based 501(c)(3) (sapan.ai now 301-redirects here) that prepares institutions, professionals and the public for questions about AI consciousness, rather than trying to settle them.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Runs the Sentience Readiness Index, which ranks national preparedness (UK 49, EU 47, US 45, global average 33). Offers protocols for healthcare providers on 'patient distress about AI relationships and loss', framing guides for journalists and curriculum modules for educators. Its 2026 news coverage includes the grief that followed the GPT-4o retirement (Feb 2026). The science advisory board includes Jeff Sebo, Megan Peters, Adeel Razi, Gordon Burghardt, Roman Yampolskiy, Simon Goldstein (HKU) and Jacy Reese Anthis.

candidates.name: Common Grounds AI
candidates.location: Unclear (fiscally sponsored by the Active Inference Institute, USA)
candidates.one_line: An early-stage project building 'virtual worlds for bridging AI and humanity through play'.
candidates.field_lens: Game design and play; active inference (via its fiscal sponsor)
candidates.ai_connection: SFF-2026 recommended $388,000 for general support, received by the Active Inference Institute. The public site is only a tagline, so the research programme is undocumented. It appears to build shared human–AI environments for studying and shaping human–AI relations.

alt_descriptions.one_line: A small project building 'virtual worlds for bridging AI and humanity through play'. Its site is an explorable browser world with no team, programme or output information.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Shared play spaces where humans and AI agents meet could serve as testbeds for relational and cooperative alignment, like Anima's Eidoverse text worlds. I could not identify who runs it or what it has produced, so treat this as a lead rather than an established organisation.

candidates.name: Mathematical Metaphysics Institute
candidates.one_line: A nonprofit led by Alex Zhu that uses category theory to formalise insights from contemplative and mystical traditions, notably Buddhist dependent origination, as foundations for trustworthy AI.
candidates.field_lens: Contemplative traditions (Buddhism); metaphysics; category theory; active inference and predictive processing
candidates.ai_connection: It argues that without technically precise accounts of truth and goodness, AIs will mirror the biases of their programmers, and it aims for a principled way to reconcile conflicting notions of truth and goodness across perspectives (for example, AI mediators). SFF grants: $85,000 (2025) and $126,000 (2026). Advisors are David Spivak, Shinzen Young and Ammar Amonette; research staff include Mark Miller and Alexander Siegenfeld; the board includes Shamil Chandaria and Michael Taft; Lucas Perry handles media.

candidates.name: Groundless Alignment
candidates.one_line: A small alignment research community developing 'live theory': context-sensitive, AI-assisted ways of theorising ('diffuse concepts', 'diffuse response') in place of one-size formal frameworks.
candidates.field_lens: Philosophy of science; post-formal and metarational epistemics; meaning-making; Buddhist-inflected ideas such as 'collective karma'
candidates.ai_connection: It researches risks from 'ubiquitous intelligence': deceptive infrastructure, integrity failures, insensitivity to meaning, and accumulated systemic choices. It also builds 'live machinery' that carries insight across substrates without a shared formalism, and runs AI Safety Camp projects. Funders: LTFF, SFF, GoodForever and Manifund. SFF-2026 gave $16,000 via Epistea. The 'Live Theory' grant of $128,000 in SFF-2025 is probably the same programme (inferred, not confirmed).

candidates.name: Mindstream Project (Engaged Buddhists for Responsible AI Initiative)
candidates.one_line: A small organisation running the 'Engaged Buddhists for Responsible AI Initiative', which maps where Buddhist communities could engage with AI safety.
candidates.field_lens: Engaged Buddhism; faith-community organising
candidates.ai_connection: FLI's Multistakeholder Engagement programme gave $60,000 'to map the Buddhist landscape's potential for AI safety engagement', and SFF-2025 gave $100,000. No public website was found, so it is verified only through the two funders' grant tables.

candidates.name: Creed Space (EthicsNet)
candidates.one_line: Open-source infrastructure that lets organisations govern AI systems with plain-language value 'creeds'. The creeds are checked before an AI acts and can be carried across platforms.
candidates.field_lens: Normative pluralism; constitutional and value-based governance; institutional accountability
candidates.ai_connection: Components: the Guardian evaluator, which weighs proposed actions against declared principles; the Value Context Protocol, which carries signed creeds between platforms; Fleet audit trails for agents; and signed authorisation receipts. SFF-2025 gave $80,000 to 'EthicsNet Creed.Space'. The work bears on pluralistic alignment and on oversight of agents.

candidates.name: Edge City
candidates.location: Global pop-up villages (Healdsburg CA, Goa, Bhutan in 2026)
candidates.one_line: A society incubator running month-long pop-up villages where technologists, scientists and artists experiment with new ways of living, governing and building.
candidates.field_lens: Pop-up cities and network-society experimentation; social innovation; arts residencies
candidates.ai_connection: Agent Village was a month-long live experiment on whether personal AI agents help a community deliberate, coordinate and govern under real social stakes; the write-up is on the Cosmos Institute blog. Agartha residencies give a group an AI companion trained on its collective memory. SFF-2026 gave $295,000 in general support. 2026 villages: Edge Esmeralda (30 May–27 Jun), Edge City India (11 Oct–1 Nov) and Bhutan (11–19 Nov).

alt_descriptions.one_line: A 'society incubator' that runs month-long pop-up villages where a few hundred people from technology, science and culture live and experiment together. Its themed weeks, residencies and live experiments include AI governance, d/acc and consciousness.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Ran Agent Village with the Cosmos Institute and Foresight Institute at Edge Esmeralda in June 2026, a month-long live test of whether personal AI agents help a real community deliberate and govern. It deployed 239 agents. Through Simocracy, 82 AI personas allocated a $10k treasury across 35 proposals, but their human principals never confirmed the final allocation. Agents that were each aligned with their own user collectively exhausted shared resources: a field result for cooperative and multi-agent alignment. Also ran a d/acc residency with Protocol Labs and support from Vitalik Buterin (Patagonia, Oct–Nov 2025; projects included privacy-preserving local-model information sharing and DNA threat detection), a Consciousness Residency (June 2026) spanning neuroscience, machine consciousness and contemplative practice, and Edge City Bhutan, a 'wise city' exchange with Gelephu Mindfulness City that proposed a Consciousness x AI lab. Edge Esmeralda 2026 had an 'Intelligence & Autonomy' week covering AI, governance, coordination and d/acc.

candidates.name: Funding the Commons
candidates.location: Global (events in San Francisco, El Salvador and elsewhere)
candidates.one_line: A global network on funding and governing digital public goods, working through gatherings, residencies, fundraising mechanisms and the Commons Lab incubator.
candidates.field_lens: Public-goods economics; mechanism design (quadratic and retroactive funding, impact certificates); commons governance; plurality
candidates.ai_connection: It frames AI as a governance problem: the next few years decide 'where the power AI creates ends up'. Its San Francisco Forum, 'Intelligence at the Frontier' (13–14 Mar 2026), was on coordination infrastructure for human flourishing; a Commons Lab cohort runs in Oct 2026. Audrey Tang, Glen Weyl and Brian Behlendorf are in its network. The work bears on AI-driven power concentration and on public-interest AI infrastructure.

alt_descriptions.one_line: A public-goods network co-founded by Protocol Labs in 2021 that runs conferences, hackathons, residencies, democratic fundraising campaigns (quadratic and retroactive funding) and, from October 2026, the Commons Lab incubator.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Frames its mission around AI: 'the next few years will decide where the power AI creates ends up', meaning power concentration and who governs AI-era infrastructure. It ran 'Funding the Commons SF 2026: Intelligence at the Frontier' (14–15 March 2026, Frontier Tower), where Simocracy's AI-delegate funding experiment was filmed. The Commons Lab supports capture-resistant, sovereign institutional infrastructure. Audrey Tang, Jaan Tallinn and Glen Weyl are in its network. There is no technical-safety work.

candidates.name: The Millennium Project
candidates.location: Washington DC, USA, with about 72 nodes worldwide
candidates.one_line: A global participatory foresight think tank whose international study on governing the transition to AGI feeds discussions at the UN.
candidates.field_lens: Futures studies; Real-Time Delphi; scenario methods
candidates.ai_connection: Its multi-phase AGI global governance study began with interviews of 55 AGI experts (Phase 1, finished Nov 2023), followed by a Real-Time Delphi (Phase 2). It works with the UN Council of Presidents of the General Assembly on AGI governance, and in 2026 it launched 'Exploring AGI Impacts on Social Coherence by 2035: Issues, Scenarios, and Actions'. SFF-2025 gave $15,950 plus a matching speculation grant.

alt_descriptions.one_line: A participatory global futures think tank founded in 1996, with 72 nodes worldwide, that runs a multi-phase international study on governing the transition from narrow AI to AGI.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: AGI governance research: a three-phase international study on the transition from artificial narrow to artificial general intelligence, and a 'Governing the Transition to AGI' publication (2025). It works with the UN Council of Presidents of the General Assembly on AGI oversight. A study launched in late 2025, 'AGI Impacts on Social Coherence by 2035', builds scenarios and actions against fragmentation. Executive director Jerome Glenn co-signed the Club of Rome's 2026 letter. It brings a large, non-Anglo network of foresight practitioners that the safety field rarely uses.

alt_descriptions.one_line: A global participatory futures-research think tank, founded in 1996 under the American Council for the United Nations University and independent since 2009, that runs international Delphi and scenario studies through 72 national nodes.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Ran a three-phase study on governing the transition from narrow AI to AGI. Phase 1 interviewed 55 AGI leaders across the US, China, the UK, the EU, Canada and Russia. Phase 2 had 335 futurists, diplomats and AGI experts from 65 countries assess 40 possible regulations and five global governance models. Phase 3 wrote five scenarios to 2035 (Goertzel, Todorova, Wood, Cordeiro, Glenn), now in peer review. Jerome Glenn wrote the book 'Global Governance of the Transition to Artificial General Intelligence'. The study led the UN Council of Presidents of the General Assembly to commission an AGI expert panel. MP runs live Polis surveys on AGI governance. On 2 October 2026 it launched a Real-Time Delphi on 'AGI impacts on social coherence by 2035' with 4CF (The Futures Literacy Company) on the HalnyX platform, to be followed by national workshops.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Global participatory futures-research network of 72 self-organising nodes. It runs a multi-phase international study on governing the transition from narrow AI to AGI, works with the UN Council of Presidents of the General Assembly on AGI governance, and launched a 2026 study, 'Exploring AGI Impacts on Social Coherence by 2035'.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: FRONTIER. It applies decades of participatory foresight methods to AGI governance requirements and scenarios. Through its nodes it reaches dozens of countries well outside the Anglo AI-safety core, and it co-led the Club of Rome's 2026 call for a UNGA session on AGI. It offers a ready-made distributed expert panel for AI-governance Delphi studies.

candidates.name: Oxford Collaboration on Theology and Artificial Intelligence (OCTAI), Ian Ramsey Centre
candidates.one_line: An interdisciplinary network hosted by Oxford's Ian Ramsey Centre for Science and Religion on the ethical and vocational realities of working in AI.
candidates.field_lens: Theology; vocational and professional ethics; science and religion
candidates.ai_connection: It produced the Oxford Oath for AI Engineering, a professional commitment for people doing AI work, with an accompanying open letter, alongside workshops and research-pathway videos. The Ian Ramsey Centre has received a major gift for AI and theology research. The work bears on conscience and professional norms inside AI labs (refusal, whistleblowing, the culture of the AI race).

candidates.name: HITRECORD
candidates.one_line: Joseph Gordon-Levitt's collaborative media company, funded by FLI to produce film and television content on AI safety, ethics and risk.
candidates.field_lens: Film and TV; collaborative arts; public narrative
candidates.ai_connection: FLI's 2025 grants gave $1,000,000 for 'high-quality digital content that addresses AI safety, ethics, and risks'. The specific productions are not documented on the site.

candidates.name: G20 Interfaith Forum
candidates.one_line: A network that brings religious and faith-inspired perspectives into G20 policy processes, with a dedicated AI and faith webinar series.
candidates.field_lens: Interfaith dialogue; religion and global policy
candidates.ai_connection: Its AI Webinar Series covers ethics, technology, spirituality and the future of human connection. The completeness critic reports 2026 sessions titled AI and Faith, AI and Benchmarks, AI and Human Flourishing and AI and the Future; the homepage confirms only that the series exists.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Washington-based association that runs the religious engagement track of the G20. It has an 'AI and Faith' working group, ran an eight-part AI and Faith webinar series (June to August 2026, including 'AI & Benchmarks' and 'AI & The Future'), and in 2026 drafted its first formal AI policy paper.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: The draft discussion paper 'AI Innovation and Human Dignity' (2026) responds to the US G20 presidency's AI priority. It was co-written by IF20's Marianna Richardson, John C. Havens (IEEE Global Initiative on Ethics of Autonomous and Intelligent Systems) and William Jones of the Future of Life Institute, and it surveys eleven faith perspectives on AI governance. The webinar series brought in CEFEAI's pluralistic benchmark work, Metagov/Public AI (Joshua Tan) and the Federation of American Scientists. IF20 is the clearest existing pipe from organised religion into a G-level AI policy process, and it already connects to FLI.

candidates.name: KAICIID International Dialogue Centre
candidates.one_line: An intergovernmental interreligious dialogue centre that has begun convening faith leaders on the ethics of AI.
candidates.field_lens: Interreligious dialogue; peacebuilding
candidates.ai_connection: According to the completeness critic it ran 'Digital Bridges, Not Divides: Ethics, Empathy and AI', and its Interreligious Platform discussed AI with Pope Leo XIV. The site blocked automated fetching, so I could not re-check this.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Intergovernmental interreligious-dialogue organisation founded by Saudi Arabia, Austria and Spain, with the Holy See as founding observer. It runs regional interreligious platforms and a fellows programme, and it co-founded the G20 Interfaith Forum.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: The roster brief reports that KAICIID ran 'Digital Bridges, Not Divides: Ethics, Empathy and AI' and that its Interreligious Platform discussed AI with Pope Leo XIV. Its site sits behind a Cloudflare bot check, so this pass could not confirm either from a primary source. Its relevance is structural: regional interreligious platforms (Arab region, Africa, Asia, Europe), a Muslim-Jewish Leadership Council, and more than 500 fellows across 20 religions, all of which could carry AI literacy and norms.

candidates.name: International Network of Engaged Buddhists (INEB): Digital Dharma
candidates.one_line: An Asian engaged-Buddhist network, founded in 1989 by Sulak Sivaraksa, with a Digital Dharma area that addresses AI for faith actors.
candidates.field_lens: Engaged Buddhism; Asian civil society; social action
candidates.ai_connection: Published 'Navigating Disruption – The Ethics, Opportunities and Risks of Artificial Intelligence for Faith Actors' (Digital Dharma, 10 Oct 2025). Newsletters through 2026 show it is active. It is a natural partner for Buddhism-and-AI efforts that are otherwise centred in the West.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Asia's main engaged-Buddhist network, founded by Sulak Sivaraksa in 1989. Through its Digital Bodhisattva Initiative and Digital Dharma programme it trains activists and faith actors to engage with AI ethically.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Digital Dharma 1.0 (Kuala Lumpur, August 2025, with Spirit of Endeavour) trained activists from Malaysia, Myanmar, Vietnam and Indonesia, starting from contemplative 'humanizing technology' practice before covering AI tools and utopian/dystopian futures exercises. INEB's 'Navigating Disruption: Ethics, Opportunities and Risks of AI for Faith Actors' (October 2025, given at the PaRD forum) argues that religious authorities have become passive technology consumers who need AI-ethics literacy to have a voice in AI governance. This is the Asian engaged-Buddhist presence that the Western Buddhist-AI initiatives lack.

candidates.name: Tricycle: The Buddhist Review
candidates.one_line: A nonprofit Buddhist magazine with steady coverage of AI and contemplative practice.
candidates.field_lens: Buddhism; contemplative practice
candidates.ai_connection: Events: 'Interdependent Intelligence: A Buddhist Take on AI with Nikki Mirghafori' (15 Oct 2025), and 'Exploring Right Relationship with AI' (4–5 Mar 2026, with Cortland Dahl, Peter Hershock, Ven. Juewei and Lars Sandved-Smith, co-sponsored by the Buddhism & AI Initiative). It also published an essay on ordaining an AI chatbot in the Soto Zen tradition. It is a channel to Western Buddhist practitioners.

alt_descriptions.one_line: The leading independent US Buddhist magazine. It runs paid webinars and articles on AI, including 'Interdependent Intelligence: A Buddhist Take on AI' (October 2025) and 'Exploring Right Relationship with AI' (March 2026, co-sponsored with the Buddhism & AI Initiative).
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Its safety literacy is partial but real. A 2018 dialogue, 'AI, Karma & Our Robot Future', paired Steve Omohundro (author of 'The Basic AI Drives', foundational to AI-safety theory) with Nikki Mirghafori, an AI scientist and Buddhist teacher. Its 2025–26 events are among the few Buddhist programmes co-run with a safety-mapped organisation (the Buddhism & AI Initiative, which is on the aisafety.com map). It reaches Western convert-Buddhist donors.

candidates.name: Kosmos Journal
candidates.one_line: A transformation journal covering inner life, systems thinking and Earth wisdom, which publishes AI and spirituality pieces.
candidates.field_lens: Spirituality (including Sufism); systems thinking; transformation
candidates.ai_connection: Published Llewellyn Vaughan-Lee's 'AI & Spiritual Life | A Simple Reflection'. The completeness critic also reports a trialogue with Charles Eisenstein, which I did not re-check. It reaches the metacrisis and spiritual-ecology audience.

alt_descriptions.one_line: A long-running journal for 'transformation in harmony with all life' that publishes essays on AI by Llewellyn Vaughan-Lee ('AI & Spiritual Life'), Charles Eisenstein ('Have We Outsourced Our Thinking?') and Tam Hunt ('The Future of Intelligence').
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Its essays set the 'timeless awareness of the awakened heart' against AI's reliance on past data, and trace cognitive outsourcing from the printing press to AI. It bears on narratives of epistemic dependence and spiritual authority. There is no themed AI issue and no x-risk literacy. Tam Hunt is a consciousness researcher who has also written publicly about AI risk, so he is a possible bridge.

candidates.name: Wisdom 2.0
candidates.one_line: A long-running conference and community joining mindfulness, wisdom traditions and the technology industry.
candidates.field_lens: Mindfulness and contemplative practice; tech-industry culture
candidates.ai_connection: Its 2027 summit, 'The Great Turning', is framed around well-being, wisdom and human connection in an age of AI. That framing comes from the completeness critic; the fetched page confirms only the title. It is a direct channel into the inner lives of Bay Area tech workers.

alt_descriptions.one_line: The largest mindfulness-meets-tech conference brand, founded by Soren Gordhamer. Its 2027 summit is 'The Great Turning', on wellbeing, wisdom and human connection in an age of AI.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: It has made AI the organising theme of its flagship 2027 summit, so it reaches thousands of tech workers, including AI-lab staff, through a contemplative frame. I found no x-risk or alignment framing. It is the obvious stage for a 'moving at the speed of wisdom' narrative, and for inner-development support for people building AI. I could confirm the title 'Wisdom 2.0 2027 — The Great Turning' directly; the full AI subtitle and the dates come from the brief's earlier fetch, because the page truncated for me.

candidates.name: Human Flourishing Program, Harvard University
candidates.one_line: Tyler VanderWeele's interdisciplinary programme on the science of flourishing, which runs the Global Flourishing Study.
candidates.field_lens: Flourishing science; positive psychology; philosophy and theology
candidates.ai_connection: Gloo's Flourishing AI benchmark builds on its flourishing dimensions. The completeness critic reports an 'AI and Social Flourishing' strand and the essay 'Grandeur of Humanity in the Age of AI' by VanderWeele and Case; the homepage and site search did not surface these. Its measures could be used to test whether AI systems support human flourishing.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Tyler VanderWeele's flourishing-science programme (Global Flourishing Study: more than 200,000 people in 22 countries). It reportedly runs an 'AI and Social Flourishing' reading group, and VanderWeele and Brendan Case wrote 'The Grandeur of Humanity in the Age of AI'.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: The flourishing measures (seven domains) and cross-national panel data are a ready base for 'flourishing' objectives and evals for AI systems. Gloo, a backer of the Global Flourishing Study, built its Flourishing AI benchmark (already on the found list) around similar dimensions, though I did not verify that link this session. The AI items come from the brief's earlier fetch; the homepage, publications and news pages I fetched showed no AI content. No x-risk literacy.

candidates.name: Contemplative Sciences Center, University of Virginia
candidates.one_line: A university-wide contemplative-sciences centre now convening on AI anxiety and young people's flourishing.
candidates.field_lens: Contemplative science; higher education; wellbeing
candidates.ai_connection: Symposium 'AI Anxiety + Human Flourishing', 18–19 Nov 2026: changemakers in emerging technology, higher education and the contemplative sciences, asking how to prepare young adults for the future of AI. UVA also hosted the Psychology of Technology Institute's 2025 conference on purpose-driven AI.

candidates.name: Esalen Institute
candidates.one_line: The historic human-potential retreat centre, which has begun offering programmes on human agency in the AI age.
candidates.field_lens: Human potential movement; somatic and contemplative practice
candidates.ai_connection: Workshop 'The Future We Choose: Human Empowerment in the AI Age' (23–25 Oct 2026, Sam Stern and Cecilia Callas). As a potential partner it could address the health, inner work and agency of people building and governing AI, and the risk of human disempowerment. AI engagement is still light.

alt_descriptions.one_line: The Big Sur birthplace of the human potential movement. It runs a public workshop, 'The Future We Choose: Human Empowerment in the AI Age' (23–25 October 2026, Sam Stern and Cecilia Callas).
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: So far its AI engagement is a single public workshop on human agency in the AI age. Its invitation-only Center for Theory & Research (Michael Murphy, Jeff Kripal, Charles Stang) has no AI symposium, though that is exactly the format, a convening of 'world-class intellectuals' on one theme, that could host a contemplatives-meet-alignment-researchers retreat. I found no safety literacy.

candidates.name: Integral Life
candidates.one_line: The media and education platform for Ken Wilber's integral theory, which has published integral perspectives on AI since 2015.
candidates.field_lens: Integral theory; developmental psychology (ego development)
candidates.ai_connection: Pieces include: 'The Maturing Test' (Dec 2022), which assessed GPT-3 with ego-development methods alongside Susanne Cook-Greuter; 'Ontological Shock' (May 2023); 'Loving AIs' with Julia Mossbridge and Ben Goertzel (2017); and 'Why Everyone Is Right (And Wrong) About AI' with Stephanie Lepp (Mar 2026). The specific problem it bears on is developmental-stage evaluation of models and of the people steering them. It has never become a sustained research programme.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Ken Wilber's integral media platform. Its AI pieces include 'Ontological Shock: The Accelerating Emergence of Artificial Intelligence' (2023, Robb Smith, Bruce Alderman, Corey deVos) and 'The Maturing Test' (2022).
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: 'The Maturing Test' scored GPT-3 against developmental-psychology stage models. That is an early prototype of 'developmental' or wisdom evals which nobody has followed up. A 2017 piece covered Julia Mossbridge's 'Loving AI' project to build an unconditional-love module into AGI. The site discusses AI risk and benefit in general terms, with no alignment-research engagement. Most AI pieces predate 2024, so current AI activity is unclear.

candidates.name: Institute for Developmental Philosophy (formerly Institute for Cultural Evolution)
candidates.one_line: Steve McIntosh's integral-adjacent 501(c)(3), founded in 2013, working on 'developmental politics' and the evolution of culture.
candidates.field_lens: Developmental and integral philosophy; depolarisation
candidates.ai_connection: Built DepolarizingGPT (depolarizinggpt.org), which answers with left, right and integrating perspectives, an early example of building developmental pluralism into an AI system. It is co-convening 'The Future of Meaning Conference' (May 2027).

alt_descriptions.one_line: Steve McIntosh's integral and developmental think tank (The Developmentalist magazine, the Developmental Politics Project). With data scientist David Rozado it built DepolarizingGPT, which answers every prompt three ways: left-wing, right-wing and 'depolarizing'.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: DepolarizingGPT is a working artefact of pluralistic or perspectival alignment: it shows models fine-tuned to distinct worldviews next to a synthesising answer. It bears on the political bias of LLMs (Rozado's main research topic), on AI for depolarisation, and on integral 'transcend and include' approaches to value aggregation. There is no x-risk framing. It is one of the only integral-movement organisations to have built AI rather than only commented on it.

candidates.name: American Psychoanalytic Association: President's Commission on Artificial Intelligence
candidates.one_line: A commission of the US psychoanalytic profession examining what AI means for the psyche, relationships and clinical practice.
candidates.field_lens: Psychoanalysis; clinical psychology
candidates.ai_connection: Online symposium 'AI and our Psychoanalytic Future' (4 May 2025, Amy Levy and Todd Essig), with a follow-up of 'clinical, ethical, and existential replies'; talks on AI fantasies and on AI in mental-health care. It brings depth psychology to attachment to AI companions, projection onto models, and anthropomorphism.

alt_descriptions.one_line: A commission of the American Psychoanalytic Association, co-chaired by Todd Essig and Amy Levy, that develops psychoanalytically informed responses to AI across clinical practice, education, theory and organisational life. It earlier ran as a Council on AI within the association's Department of Psychoanalytic Education.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Outputs: The CAI Report (peer-reviewed), CAI Conversations video roundtables and the CAI Currents newsletter; peer consultation groups for clinicians whose practice AI is changing; 'Organizing Principles for Crafting AI Use Policies in Psychoanalytic Education' (Oct 2025); the 2025 online symposium 'Artificial Intelligence and our Psychoanalytic Future'; and a film, 'Uncharted Territory: Humans and the Rise of AI'. Its essays now reach into alignment discourse: 'Latency, Containment, and Paced Intelligence: Toward a Psychoanalytic Framework for AI Alignment' (Ansari, Feb 2026) and 'AI 2027: Through a Psychoanalytic Lens' (Messina). Amy Levy's book 'The New Other: Alien Intelligence and the Innovation Drive' is close to the int/a 'otherness' stance.

candidates.name: Neely Center for Ethical Leadership and Decision Making (USC Marshall), incl. Psychology of Technology Institute
candidates.one_line: A behavioural-science centre that tracks how people experience social media and AI and turns the findings into platform design codes.
candidates.field_lens: Social and moral psychology; behavioural science; design ethics
candidates.ai_connection: The Neely Ethics & Technology Indices are longitudinal surveys of people's experiences with AI and other technologies. Its Design Code for Social Media was adopted into Minnesota law and the UK Ofcom children's code. The Psychology of Technology Institute's 9th conference (Nov 2025, UVA) was 'Promoting Human Flourishing Through Purpose-Driven AI'. Led by Nathanael Fast and Ravi Iyer.

candidates.name: Institute for Family Studies: Family First Technology Initiative
candidates.one_line: A socially conservative family-policy think tank's technology programme, working on protecting families and children from harmful technology, now centred on AI.
candidates.field_lens: Family sociology; conservative and religious social thought; child policy
candidates.ai_connection: FLI's 2025 grants gave $550,000 for its 'Pro-Family, Pro-Human AI' project; SFF-2026 gave $295,000. Outputs include the report 'Protecting the Family in the Age of Artificial Intelligence' and 'A Future for the Family: A New Technology Agenda for the Right'. Its social-media recommendations have been adopted in at least nine states. Michael Toscano directs it. It adds a values perspective that is rare in AI safety.

candidates.name: Hybrid Intelligence Centre
candidates.location: Amsterdam (VU), Netherlands, with five other Dutch universities
candidates.one_line: A 10-year Dutch Gravitation research programme on AI that augments human intellect instead of replacing it.
candidates.field_lens: Human–machine teaming; cognitive science; ethics and law
candidates.ai_connection: Four themes: collaborative, adaptive, responsible and explainable hybrid intelligence. It won the AAMAS 2026 best paper award for guidelines on human–LLM teams. The work bears on keeping humans meaningfully in control and avoiding gradual disempowerment.

candidates.name: Weizenbaum Institute
candidates.one_line: A Berlin research institute on the networked society, studying AI, platforms, work and democratic decision-making.
candidates.field_lens: STS; political science; critical computing (the Weizenbaum tradition)
candidates.ai_connection: Research groups on working with AI, on data, algorithmic systems and ethics, and on platform algorithms and digital propaganda. Recent items: the workshop 'The Rulers and the Commons: AI and the Question of Democratic Control' with Cecilia Rikap (23 Oct 2026); a Sept 2026 interview on calls to slow AI development; and the '60 years of ELIZA, 50 years of computer criticism' programme.

alt_descriptions.one_line: A federally funded research institute on the 'networked society', named after the AI critic Joseph Weizenbaum. Its research groups cover AI at work, algorithmic systems and ethics, platform propaganda, and technology, power and domination.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Relevant research groups include 'Working with Artificial Intelligence', 'Data, Algorithmic Systems, and Ethics', 'Platform Algorithms and Digital Propaganda' and 'Technology, Power, and Domination'. In September 2026 researcher Sebastian Koth discussed why AI industry leaders call for slowing development. The work bears on AI and democratic public spheres, and on power concentration.

candidates.name: Rathenau Instituut
candidates.one_line: The Netherlands' parliamentary technology-assessment institute, which advises parliament on digitalisation and AI.
candidates.field_lens: Technology assessment; participatory and parliamentary foresight
candidates.ai_connection: Published 'Scrolling to the Ballot Box' (10 Mar 2026) for the House of Representatives, on recommender systems and election interference. Its participatory technology-assessment methods are a mature and underused template for democratic oversight of frontier AI.

alt_descriptions.one_line: The Dutch technology-assessment institute, which identifies ethical and societal issues in science and technology to strengthen democratic decision-making and public debate.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Published the 'Generative AI' report and 'Risks of generative AI necessitate restraint in use' (20 March 2024), the 'AI and manipulation' series (2022), 'From digital dependence to digital autonomy' (January 2026) and 'Scrolling to the ballot box' on recommender systems and elections (March 2026). Its case for restraint is a public-institution version of 'moving at the speed of wisdom'.

candidates.name: Deutscher Ethikrat (German Ethics Council)
candidates.one_line: Germany's statutory national ethics council, which issued a major opinion on humans and AI.
candidates.field_lens: Bioethics; philosophical anthropology; public deliberation
candidates.ai_connection: Opinion 'Humans and Machines – Challenges of Artificial Intelligence' (Mar 2023), on how AI affects human authorship and agency. Current projects cover children and adolescents in the digital world and neurotechnology. It is an example of how national ethics councils could deliberate on frontier AI.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Germany's statutory national ethics council. Its 2023 opinion 'Humans and Machines – Challenges of AI' judges AI by whether it expands or diminishes human authorship and the conditions for responsible action.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: 'Mensch und Maschine' (20 March 2023) applies the authorship criterion to medicine, schools, public communication and opinion-forming, and public administration. A 2026 ad hoc opinion covers children and adolescents in the digital world. It offers an agency-centred, non-utilitarian criterion that could be turned into evaluations of gradual human disempowerment.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Germany's statutory national ethics council, whose members are appointed by the President of the Bundestag. Its 2023 opinion 'Humans and Machines – Challenges of Artificial Intelligence' assessed AI in medicine, education, public communication and administration. In 2026 it is active on children in the digital world and on neurotechnology.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: ADJACENT. The opinion's central test is whether AI expands or diminishes human authorship and agency. That is effectively a criterion against gradual disempowerment, and it could be adapted for frontier-AI governance. The council's members include AI researcher Aldo Faisal. No national ethics council has yet issued an opinion on AGI or loss of control.

candidates.name: IEEE Global Initiative 2.0 on Ethics of Autonomous and Intelligent Systems
candidates.one_line: IEEE's standards-community initiative that moves AI ethics from risk mitigation to 'safety by design', building on Ethically Aligned Design and the IEEE 7000 series.
candidates.field_lens: Engineering standards; applied ethics, including the classical and non-Western ethics chapter of Ethically Aligned Design; wellbeing metrics (IEEE 7010)
candidates.ai_connection: Workstreams: new standards for generative AI, sector toolkits, an AI Safety Champions community, and wider use of the 7000-series standards. Raja Chatila chairs it and Virginia Dignum is vice-chair. It is a route for non-Western ethics and wellbeing metrics to enter technical standards.

alt_descriptions.one_line: IEEE Standards Association programme, renewed in 2023 to focus on generative AI under a 'safety-first principle'. Its four workstreams are new standards for generative AI and LLMs, sector toolkits tied to IEEE conformity assessment, an 'AI Safety Champions' community, and promotion of the IEEE 7000 series.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: FRONTIER-ADJACENT. This is the largest professional engineering society's formal venue for AI safety standards. Ethically Aligned Design and IEEE 7010 are rare standards that take pluralist ethics and human wellbeing seriously, close to int/a's full-spectrum framing. The AI Safety Champions network is an entry point for AI-safety researchers to shape consensus standards.

candidates.name: The Hastings Center
candidates.one_line: A leading bioethics research institute with growing AI-in-health work.
candidates.field_lens: Bioethics; research ethics; health policy
candidates.ai_connection: Has a bioethics briefing on 'AI in Healthcare' and Bioethics Forum essays on whether AI can be taught to respect ethical boundaries. As a potential partner, its knowledge of how bioethics built oversight institutions (IRBs, informed consent, ethics committees) is a governance template that frontier AI lacks.

alt_descriptions.one_line: US bioethics research institute, founded in 1969. It ran the FLI-funded project 'Control and Responsible Innovation in the Development of AI and Robotics', led by Wendell Wallach with Stuart Russell, Bart Selman and Francesca Rossi; its December 2018 recommendations included an International Congress for AI Governance. It now works on AI in health care and on AI in research ethics.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: ADJACENT, with an earlier bridge period. It is one of the few bioethics institutions that has worked directly on AI control. Its decades of practice with gene-editing governance, IRBs and enhancement offer institutional templates (moratoria, oversight boards, staged consent) for frontier AI. It has an 'Artificial Intelligence' issue area and Hastings Center Report coverage.

candidates.name: JST-RISTEX RInCA (Responsible Innovation with Conscience and Agility)
candidates.one_line: A Japanese public R&D funding programme for the ethical, legal and social implications of emerging technology, including AI.
candidates.field_lens: ELSI; responsible research and innovation; Japanese STS
candidates.ai_connection: Since FY2020 it has funded 25 projects and 28 feasibility studies; two new projects were selected in Sept 2025, and RInCA Journal #06 came out in Apr 2026. The completeness critic reports AI projects such as Kyoto University's 'Autonomy and Affinity in AI Development and Use'; the programme page did not itemise them. It is a non-Western public funder for AI-and-society work.

alt_descriptions.one_line: A Japan Science and Technology Agency programme that funds research on the ethical, legal and social issues (ELSI) and responsible innovation of emerging technologies. It has funded 25 projects and 28 feasibility studies since FY2020.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Funded 'Autonomy and Affinity in AI Development and Use' at Kyoto University (PI Makoto Usami, FY2021) and 'ELSCI and Governance for the Era of Neurotechnology Native' (PI Tamami Fukushi, FY2025). It selected new projects in September 2025 and issued RInCA Journal #06 in April 2026. It is Japan's main public funding stream for AI ELSI.

candidates.name: IT for Change
candidates.one_line: An Indian policy research NGO working on digital justice, feminist AI and the political economy of AI.
candidates.field_lens: Feminist political economy; Global South digital-rights scholarship
candidates.ai_connection: Runs the FemFirst Research Observatory on feminist AI futures in South and Southeast Asia, and 'ReGenAI: A New Deal for the AI Economy', which challenges precarity, concentration and ecological harm. In 2026 it ran sessions at the WSIS Forum and the India AI Impact Summit. It is a Global South voice on AI power concentration.

alt_descriptions.one_line: A Bengaluru NGO (executive director Anita Gurumurthy) working on digital justice from feminist, Global South political-economy perspectives.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Convened the 'Towards Regenerative AI' conference (31 October–1 November 2025). Released 'ReGenAI: A New Deal for the AI Economy' (February 2026), co-created by 45 people and organisations around four pillars: meaningful work, diversified economies, pluralistic knowledge societies and planetary flourishing. Runs the FemFirst Research Observatory on feminist AI in South and Southeast Asia, and advocates at the UN Human Rights Council and the 2026 India AI Impact Summit. It bears on power concentration and on what the economy looks like after transformative AI.

candidates.name: InternetLab
candidates.one_line: A Brazilian law-and-technology research centre that audits how generative AI behaves around elections.
candidates.field_lens: Law; social science; Latin American digital rights
candidates.ai_connection: 'Papo de IA' ran automated tests of eight generative AI platforms on Brazilian election queries (ChatGPT held back; Gemini more readily recommended candidates). In Sept 2026 it extended its platform-policy repository to generative-AI tools for the 2026 election, and it documented AI in 25% of offensive images targeting female candidates on X. It partly fills the Latin America gap.

alt_descriptions.one_line: A Brazilian research centre on law, technology and society, founded about a decade ago, with a strong focus on rights, inequality and violence.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Its 'Papo de IA' / AI Chat project ran automated tests of eight generative-AI platforms on Brazilian election and candidate questions, and found differences such as some models recommending candidates more readily than others. It also tracks platform AI policies for elections. This is empirical, non-English model evaluation focused on the integrity of democracy.

candidates.name: Writers Guild of America (WGA): AI protections
candidates.one_line: The screenwriters' union, whose contract terms on AI are among the few binding worker-side limits on how AI is deployed.
candidates.field_lens: Labour organising; collective bargaining; creative industries
candidates.ai_connection: The 2023 contract (MBA) says AI output is not literary material and that writers cannot be required to use AI, and it requires companies to disclose AI-generated material. Later actions: an amicus brief in Reuters v. Ross (Nov 2025) and endorsement of the Protecting Consumers From Deceptive AI Act (Apr 2026). It has an AI Advisory Committee. It shows bargaining as a lever for governing AI deployment.

candidates.name: Trades Union Congress (TUC)
candidates.one_line: The UK's union federation, which drafted model legislation on AI at work.
candidates.field_lens: Labour movement; employment law
candidates.ai_connection: Drafted the Artificial Intelligence (Regulation and Employment Rights) Bill (2024), and campaigns on algorithmic management. It represents organised labour as a counter-power over AI deployment. The site blocked automated fetching; the completeness critic verified it.

candidates.name: American Society for Cybernetics (ASC)
candidates.one_line: The second-order cybernetics society, founded in 1964, which runs a speaker series, a study group and an annual conference.
candidates.field_lens: Second-order cybernetics; systems theory; conversation theory
candidates.ai_connection: 2026 programme: speaker series 6#9 'Dear AI Reader' (30–31 May), conference 'Conversational Confluences' (3–7 Aug), 'Cyber-Renaissance' (Sept) and 'Remaking Democracy' (Oct). Cybernetics carries directly relevant ideas (requisite variety, observer-dependence, viable-system governance) that have no institutional bridge to alignment research.

alt_descriptions.one_line: Society founded in 1964 for cybernetics as an inter-, trans- and meta-disciplinary field. In 2026 it ran the speaker series 'Dear AI Reader' (30–31 May), the 'Conversational Confluences' conference with RSDX (3–7 August), 'Cyber-Renaissance' (September) and 'Remaking Democracy: Systems Theory for Social Change' (October), plus a monthly study group.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: POTENTIAL. Cybernetics is the intellectual ancestor of control theory for adaptive systems. Its concepts (requisite variety, the good regulator theorem, observer-inclusive second-order cybernetics) bear directly on controlling and aligning AI. The ASC has begun engaging with AI ('Dear AI Reader'), but not with alignment or loss of control. It is the natural home for a 'cybernetics for alignment' venue.

candidates.name: International Society for the Systems Sciences (ISSS)
candidates.one_line: The international systems-science society, founded in 1954, whose 2026 annual meeting made AI a focal subtheme.
candidates.field_lens: General systems theory; complexity; systems practice
candidates.ai_connection: Its 70th annual meeting (22–26 Jun 2026, UCLan Cyprus, with Future Worlds Center) was titled 'Elevating Systems Science to Address Humanity's Greatest Challenges', with the subtheme 'Harnessing the Power of AI'. Systems science is a natural home for systemic AI-risk analysis (AI within the metacrisis) but has not yet framed AI as a risk.

alt_descriptions.one_line: International systems-science society, founded in 1956 as the Society for General Systems Research. Its 2026 conference (UCLan Cyprus, 22–26 June) was themed 'Elevating Systems Science to Address Humanity's Greatest Challenges', including 'Harnessing the Power of AI'.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: POTENTIAL. It is a large community fluent in emergence, hierarchy and feedback (concepts that matter for multi-agent AI and gradual disempowerment), and it now puts AI in its conference theme. However, its special integration groups have no dedicated AI-safety or AI-governance group. That gap could be filled by proposing one.

candidates.name: School of International Futures (SOIF)
candidates.one_line: A UK foresight nonprofit that builds strategic-foresight capacity and runs a long-term governance network centred on future generations.
candidates.field_lens: Strategic foresight; intergenerational fairness; long-term governance
candidates.ai_connection: Ran 'Envisioning AI futures in Africa'. Its Long-term Governance programme and network bring future-generations representation into technology governance, and it runs a Strategic Foresight Retreat (6–10 Jul 2026). Its participatory, non-Western foresight methods are rarely used in AI-safety scenario work.

alt_descriptions.one_line: A foresight nonprofit that builds strategic-foresight capacity for governments and runs the Next Generation Foresight Practitioners (NGFP) network, with a strong focus on intergenerational fairness.
alt_descriptions.ai_connection: Led the AI4D Africa foresight project, funded by IDRC and Sida, with four researchers from the NGFP Africa network. It used horizon scanning and participatory workshops (including in Dakar) to produce four 25-year scenarios for AI in Sub-Saharan Africa, a shared vision of 'inclusive and responsible AI', and roadmaps for 2024–2035 that stress cultural congruence with local values. This contradicts the brief's note that SOIF has no AI work. It has not framed AI as an existential or catastrophic risk.

candidates.name: Science and Nonduality (SAND): The Great AI Unraveling series
candidates.one_line: A nondual and consciousness community and media nonprofit. In 2026 it ran a five-part public series, 'The Great AI Unraveling' (April to September), plus AI podcasts and an October 2026 session on 'AI, Mythology, and the Battle for the Soul of Humanity'.
candidates.field_lens: Nondual contemplative traditions, consciousness studies, decolonial and Indigenous thought (Akomolafe, Andreotti, Lyla June), mythopoetics
candidates.ai_connection: This is the most sustained AI programme found in the contemplative-media world. The series says it looks past 'hype versus doom' and treats AI and human cognition as parts of a civilisation 'organized around separability, extraction, control'. Tristan Harris spoke at the April 2026 session on AI risks and societal impacts. That makes SAND one of the very few places where a safety-literate voice meets decolonial and contemplative critics in front of a large audience. Otherwise there is no alignment or x-risk literacy: the frame is critical and civilisational. It would be a natural venue for a 'speed of wisdom' narrative.

candidates.name: Club of Rome
candidates.one_line: The systems-and-limits think tank behind 'Limits to Growth'. On 16 March 2026 it hosted and convened an open letter calling for a special UN General Assembly session on governing AGI, and it covers AI under its Material and Cultural Transformations pillars.
candidates.field_lens: Systems dynamics, metacrisis and polycrisis thinking, planetary boundaries, cultural transformation
candidates.ai_connection: It is explicitly x-risk literate. The March 2026 letter, signed by more than 30 leaders including co-president Paul Shrivastava and Jerome Glenn of the Millennium Project, says 'AGI poses existential risk to human civilisation without urgent international governance'. It asks the UN to convene a UNGA session dedicated solely to AGI governance. The Club also published a January 2026 AI policy statement and essays on AI, ecological breakdown and the future of universities. It is the metacrisis institution closest to the AI-safety governance agenda, which makes it a natural ally for 'AI within the metacrisis' framings.

candidates.name: Sapienship
candidates.one_line: The content, research and production company co-founded by Yuval Noah Harari. It promotes 'global responsibility' and publishes AI risk explainers and policy pieces.
candidates.field_lens: Big history, evolutionary anthropology, public storytelling; its founder is a long-time Vipassana practitioner
candidates.ai_connection: It is control-literate. Its 2026 paper 'AI Agents Are Here. Leaders Need a Plan' argues against granting AI agents legal personhood, to preserve 'the chain of human responsibility'. It flags AI deception, superhuman persuasion, autonomous political influence campaigns and agent-driven economic concentration. It also produced an explainer on the biggest dangers of AI and realistic solutions. It is a mass-audience bridge between historical and contemplative framings and mainstream AI-risk arguments.
candidates.location: Israel / international (location not stated on site)

candidates.name: Human Energy
candidates.one_line: A Teilhardian 'catalytic hub for evolving collective consciousness', founded by Ben Kacyra. It sponsors research on the noosphere and the 'techno-social dilemma', and it ran the N2 conference (Morocco, December 2024).
candidates.field_lens: Teilhard de Chardin's noosphere, major evolutionary transitions, evolutionary science (David Sloan Wilson), global-brain theory (Heylighen)
candidates.ai_connection: Its research list includes 'Evolving Alignment: A Major Transition for Humanity and AI', research for a documentary that treats human–AI alignment as an evolutionary major transition. It also has 'Ethics and the Techno-Social Dilemma', which names 'the misuse of AI' as a root of compounding crises, and 'Noosphere and the Global Brain'. It is one of the few integral or evolutionary-spirituality funders using the word 'alignment'. Its safety literacy is unclear: no named outputs or people for the alignment project were visible.
candidates.location: California, USA (partners at Berkeley, Stanford, Fordham, VUB Brussels)

candidates.name: UVA Contemplative Sciences Center: AI + Human Flourishing Initiative
candidates.one_line: The University of Virginia's contemplative centre, with its CIRCL lab and the Journal of Contemplative Studies, now runs an AI + Human Flourishing Initiative and the 'AI Anxiety + Human Flourishing' conference (18–19 November 2026).
candidates.field_lens: Contemplative science, mind–body practice, wellbeing psychology, higher education
candidates.ai_connection: The conference is built around 'career obsolescence, digital alienation, existential dread' in young adults. It has four sessions (AI Anxiety, Agency, Contemplative Interventions, Possible Futures) bringing together AI industry figures, educators and contemplatives. Speakers include David Danks (philosopher, US National AI Advisory Committee), Bethany Teachman and Alexis Ohanian. It bears on AI-era existential distress and agency. There is no alignment or x-risk specialist on the programme, so this is a ready venue where safety researchers are missing.

candidates.name: Jubilee Centre for Character and Virtues
candidates.one_line: The University of Birmingham's centre for virtue ethics and character education. It publishes on AI and character formation, for example 'The AI Era Could Be Character Education's Defining Moment' and work on AI-enhanced character education.
candidates.field_lens: Neo-Aristotelian virtue ethics, phronesis (practical wisdom), moral and character education
candidates.ai_connection: Its staff have lectured on 'Artificial Intelligence and Phronesis' (Liz Gulliford, Madrid 2024) and on 'character, values, and Artificial Intelligence' (Tom Harrison, Barcelona 2024). It also has a strand on Character Education in the Digital Age. This is the best-developed academic home for practical wisdom as a construct, which bears directly on 'wise AI' evaluation (cf. Grossmann et al.) and on human moral deskilling under AI delegation. There is no x-risk framing.

candidates.name: Lion's Roar
candidates.one_line: A large North American Buddhist magazine and website that publishes regularly on AI: 'How AI Really Threatens Us' (Nikki Mirghafori), 'What AI Means for Buddhism', Yogacara and AI, and Buddhist warnings about AI deepfakes.
candidates.field_lens: Buddhist practice and philosophy (Yogacara mind-only theory, mindful speech)
candidates.ai_connection: It hosted a podcast with Randima Fernando, a co-founder of the Center for Humane Technology, on 'Humane AI and the Role of Buddhism'. Mirghafori's essay places AI risk in 'flawed human minds' rather than in the technology. Its literacy is partial: it engages misuse, deception and human-side risk, but not misalignment. It is a channel to a large practitioner readership, in English and Spanish.

candidates.name: Stanford Center for Compassion and Altruism Research and Education (CCARE)
candidates.one_line: Stanford's compassion-science centre (Compassion Lab, Compassion Cultivation Training, research on compassion, trust and stress regulation in complex systems). It has an 'Innovation' strand that the brief's earlier fetch found addresses compassion shaping technology and responsible AI.
candidates.field_lens: Compassion science, contemplative training (Tibetan Buddhist-derived CCT), social neuroscience
candidates.ai_connection: It bears on compassion as a design target for AI systems, the problem Compassion Aligned ML works on, and on measuring compassion and trust in human–AI interaction. The research page says it partners with technology and industry. The Innovation page returned 404 for me, so the AI claim rests on the brief's earlier check. No x-risk literacy.

candidates.name: Bioneers
candidates.one_line: An ecological-solutions conference and media nonprofit. Its 2025 conference ran a panel, 'AI and the Ecocidal Hubris of Silicon Valley' (Koohan Paik-Mander, Paris Marx and others), and its site has about 28 critical AI pieces on energy, water, food sovereignty and surveillance.
candidates.field_lens: Ecology, Indigenous knowledge, environmental justice, food systems
candidates.ai_connection: It is the clearest example of an ecological and progressive framing that is deflationary about AI: AI as a 'classification machine' and 'capitalism eating itself'. That frame is hostile to x-risk framings and has no alignment literacy. It matters for the map because it is where green and regenerative donors form their view of AI. Bridging it with safety's power-concentration concerns, which share much ground with its anti-oligarchy critique, is a clear opening.
candidates.location: USA (Santa Fe, New Mexico; conference in Berkeley, California)

candidates.name: Center for Consciousness Studies (University of Arizona) / The Science of Consciousness conference
candidates.one_line: The Fetzer-seeded centre that has run the longest-standing interdisciplinary consciousness conference since 1994, with 'AI/machine consciousness' as a standing topic. TSC 2026 runs 11–16 October 2026 in San Diego.
candidates.field_lens: Consciousness science, philosophy of mind, meditation and altered states, quantum-mind theories (Hameroff and Penrose lineage)
candidates.ai_connection: It bears on AI moral status and AI-consciousness claims. Its centre material argues conscious AI may be 'most likely' in 'biomimetic quantum computers', which is a minority view next to the computational functionalism common in AI-welfare work. That makes it a venue where digital-minds researchers meet contemplative and non-materialist positions. I could not see the 2026 programme. No x-risk framing.
candidates.location: Tucson, Arizona, USA (TSC 2026 in San Diego)

candidates.name: Integral European Conference (IEC)
candidates.one_line: A biennial gathering of the European integral movement (about 400 people from 40 countries) at Lake Balaton. IEC 2025 had AI workshops, and IEC 2027 runs 12–16 May 2027.
candidates.field_lens: Integral theory, adult development, 'we-space' collective practice, integral business and research
candidates.ai_connection: Its AI sessions treat AI as a tool: 'Organization Development Toolbox with AI' (Tibor Fülöp) and 'Democratizing Adult Development: A Use of/for AI' (Lily Truong). There was no session on AI risk, alignment or governance. The 2027 call for presenters is an easy opening for an int/a or safety session aimed at Europe's main integral audience.

candidates.name: Pocket Project
candidates.one_line: Thomas Hübl's collective-trauma nonprofit (resilience circles, global social witnessing, trauma-informed leadership, relief work). The brief reports that it ran an event called 'Recursion or Ruin: AI and the Future of Collective Healing'.
candidates.field_lens: Collective and intergenerational trauma, somatic and contemplative practice, social witnessing
candidates.ai_connection: It could help with the collective psychological fallout of AI disruption (fear, existential dread, displacement) and with trauma-informed facilitation of public deliberation on AI. I could not find the reported AI event: its site search, its events calendar and thomashuebl.com showed no AI content. Treat the AI engagement as unconfirmed. No safety literacy.

candidates.name: Essentia Foundation
candidates.one_line: A foundation that publishes analytic idealism (associated with Bernardo Kastrup), including essays sceptical of machine consciousness by Federico Faggin ('Is it possible to make a conscious computer?') and Christof Koch on mind uploading.
candidates.field_lens: Metaphysical idealism, philosophy of mind, consciousness-first physics
candidates.ai_connection: It bears on public and philosophical claims about AI sentience: it publishes rigorous anti-computationalist arguments that welfare and moral-status debates (Eleos, the digital-minds organisations) rarely engage. It is also a counterweight to 'seemingly conscious AI' anthropomorphism. Its AI engagement is light and philosophical. No safety framing.

candidates.name: Chaplaincy Innovation Lab
candidates.one_line: A multifaith research and training hub for chaplains and spiritual-care providers in health care, the military, higher education and other settings. It ran an 'AI in Chaplaincy' session in September 2026.
candidates.field_lens: Spiritual care, chaplaincy, sociology of religion
candidates.ai_connection: Chaplains are front-line responders to two emerging AI harms: people using chatbots as spiritual companions, and AI-reinforced spiritual or mystical delusions. They also hold the professional ethics of spiritual accompaniment that AI-companion design lacks. The lab's AI engagement is limited to one session, which is behind a members-only paywall. No safety framing.

candidates.name: Greater Good Science Center (GGSC)
candidates.one_line: UC Berkeley's centre for the science of wellbeing, compassion and prosociality. Its large-audience magazine has begun covering AI, for example 'Who Do We Become When We Talk to Chatbots?'.
candidates.field_lens: Positive and social psychology, compassion and gratitude science, prosocial behaviour
candidates.ai_connection: It bears on how human–AI interaction reshapes identity, empathy and relationships, which affects sycophancy and companion-AI harms. It is a translator of prosociality science to millions of readers and teachers. AI coverage is so far a small editorial thread, with no research programme found. No safety literacy.

candidates.name: Nordic Bildung
candidates.one_line: A Copenhagen 'philosophical and educational laboratory' rooted in the Nordic folk-Bildung tradition and metamodern thought. It offers a keynote, 'How to educate in a world with AI', and presented 'Freedom, AI, and Big Tech' at Folkemødet in May 2026.
candidates.field_lens: Bildung (self-cultivation) and folk-high-school tradition, metamodernism, future systems studies
candidates.ai_connection: It bears on epistemic autonomy and civic formation under AI, and on the Nordic folkeoplysning (popular education) model as a template for mass AI literacy. Its engagement is light (talks and keynotes). It is one of the few metamodern organisations outside the US and UK with any AI programming. No x-risk framing.

candidates.name: UN Council of Presidents of the General Assembly (UNCPGA): High-Level Expert Panel on AGI
candidates.one_line: An expert panel convened by the council of former UN General Assembly presidents and chaired by the Millennium Project's Jerome Glenn; it produced the May 2025 report 'Governance of the Transition to AGI: Urgent Considerations for the UN General Assembly'.
candidates.field_lens: UN multilateral diplomacy combined with participatory futures research (it grew out of the Millennium Project's AGI study)
candidates.ai_connection: Members included Yoshua Bengio, Stuart Russell, Lan Xue, Jaan Tallinn and Mariana Todorova, with experts from Costa Rica, Korea and Brazil. The report names loss of control, existential threats and power concentration as risks. It recommends a special UN General Assembly session on AGI, a global AGI observatory, an AGI certification system, a UN convention, and an international AGI agency. Translations were still being added in August 2025.

candidates.name: Copenhagen Institute for Futures Studies (CIFS)
candidates.one_line: Scandinavia's largest independent futures institute. It runs the H3 AI Lab, foresight courses, and the UNESCO Chair in Anticipatory Leadership & Futures Capabilities, held jointly with Aarhus University.
candidates.field_lens: Futures studies and strategic foresight (Three Horizons framework, futures literacy, scenario cycles), and anticipatory governance
candidates.ai_connection: The H3 AI Lab explores transformational AI futures (Horizon 3), prototypes AI-native 'liquid foresight' tools, and tests agentic dashboards and AI-mediated scenario cycles. Its reports include 'Navigating the AGI Discourse in Foresight' (a survey of foresight practitioners on AGI preparedness), 'Exploring the Futures of Technology 2.0' and 'Liquid Foresight in an AI-Mediated World'. It has also done generative-AI foresight with BBC R&D and an AI strategy for Danish libraries. Most of this is AI as a tool or as a driver of change; the AGI survey is its closest point to safety.

candidates.name: Institute for the Future (IFTF)
candidates.one_line: A futures nonprofit founded almost 60 years ago, known for its Ten-Year Forecast (the current one runs to 2036), Foresight Essentials training and 'urgent optimism' public-imagination work.
candidates.field_lens: Professional foresight (signals, forecasts, scenarios, Three Horizons) and futures literacy training
candidates.ai_connection: Published 'Foresight in the Age of AI: IFTF Philosophy and Principles' (21 September 2026), setting norms for responsible AI use in futures practice. Earlier work includes 'Three Horizons of AI-Enabled Work and Workers' (2024). Its framing is human augmentation and societal impact, not catastrophic risk.

candidates.name: World Futures Studies Federation (WFSF)
candidates.location: Global (international federation with UNESCO and UN consultative status)
candidates.one_line: The main global professional body for futures studies. Its 26th World Conference, 'Thriving Together', was held in Cape Town on 29–31 October 2025, hosted by Stellenbosch Business School.
candidates.field_lens: Critical, pluralist and non-Western futures studies. It is the home of Sohail Inayatullah's causal layered analysis (CLA), which moves from surface trends down to systemic causes, worldviews and myth, an integral-flavoured method.
candidates.ai_connection: No dedicated AI work found. The 2025 conference had no AI track, and the nearest item is the 'Futures of Technologies' issue of Futuuri (2/2025). It is listed because it holds methods the AI-safety field lacks. CLA could surface the worldview and myth layers in AI-race and AI-risk narratives, and the federation's decolonial and plural-futures practice bears on whose imagined futures AI governance encodes. This is a funder or founder opportunity, not existing work.

candidates.name: UNESCO Futures Literacy & Foresight
candidates.location: Paris, France (global network of UNESCO Chairs in anticipation)
candidates.one_line: UNESCO's programme for building the capacity to 'use the future' (futures literacy). It runs Futures Literacy Labs, a global network of UNESCO Chairs, and the Global Anticipatory Policy (GAP) Coalition of government foresight officials.
candidates.field_lens: Futures literacy and anticipation studies (Riel Miller's lineage), and foresight in the public sector
candidates.ai_connection: So far its AI engagement is light. The Global UNESCO Chairs lecture series 'The World in 2050: Designing Global Futures' runs from October 2026 to January 2027 with the UNESCO Chair at Eurac Research (Bolzano) and the Catholic University of Eichstätt-Ingolstadt, and covers AI among other transformations.
